locations.setting: A 306-room hotel on Ulica kneza Borne in central Zagreb with two restaurants, a piano bar, casino and indoor pool, listed by the Zagreb Film Office.

locations.name: Sljeme Tunnel
locations.setting: A road tunnel through the Medvednica hills north of Zagreb, listed by the Zagreb Film Office under traffic-connection locations.

locations.name: ŠSD Dubrava Sports Hall
locations.setting: Multi-purpose school sports hall in Zagreb's Dubrava district, used for handball, basketball and other indoor sports, with bleacher seating and changing rooms.

locations.name: St. Nicholas Fortress
locations.setting: Triangular sixteenth-century sea fortress guarding the entrance to Šibenik's channel, a UNESCO World Heritage site reachable only by boat.

locations.name: Stadion Maksimir
locations.setting: Zagreb's largest football ground, home of GNK Dinamo Zagreb and the national team, with open bowl seating for more than 35,000 next to Maksimir Park.

locations.name: Svetice Sports and Recreation Centre
locations.setting: A public swimming pool complex in eastern Zagreb with several basins, run by the city's sport and youth office and listed for filming by the Zagreb Film Office.

locations.name: Tenis Centar Maksimir
locations.setting: A working tennis and squash club in the Maksimir neighbourhood of Zagreb, listed by the Zagreb Film Office under sport objects.

locations.name: The Westin Zagreb
locations.setting: High-rise hotel in central Zagreb with a casino, indoor pool and spa, conference and banqueting rooms, and a restaurant and bars used for hospitality shoots.
locations.facilities: 340 rooms and suites, 13 multifunctional congress and banqueting rooms, indoor swimming pool, spa and casino

locations.name: Tvornica Kulture
locations.setting: Former factory building in Zagreb converted into a concert and events venue, with a large and a small performance hall and an on-site bar, hired out for concerts, conferences and corporate events.
locations.facilities: Veliki pogon (large hall) and Mali pogon (small hall) performance spaces, on-site bar

locations.name: Vatroslav Lisinski Concert Hall
locations.setting: Zagreb's main concert hall on Trg Stjepana Radića, with a large auditorium and smaller performance space, listed by the Zagreb Film Office as an architectural filming location.

locations.name: Veli Rat Lighthouse
locations.setting: Working stone lighthouse of 1849 at the northern tip of Dugi Otok, one of the tallest on the Adriatic, reached by a track through pine forest above a rocky cove.

locations.name: West Railway Station, Zagreb
locations.setting: A smaller working railway station in the Črnomerec district of Zagreb, listed in the Zagreb Film Office catalogue alongside the nearby Hendrix and Youth bridges.

locations.name: Zadar Airport
locations.setting: An international airport at Zemunik Donji outside Zadar, with two runways and a modern terminal, listed by the Zadar Film Commission for filming.

locations.name: Zadar City Market
locations.setting: An open-air produce market with green and white awnings in the centre of Zadar's old town, listed by the Zadar Film Commission.

locations.name: Zadar County Office Building
locations.setting: The seat of the Zadar County administration on the Zadar peninsula, a walled building by the sea, listed by the Zadar Film Commission.

locations.name: Zagreb Bus Station
locations.setting: The city's main long-distance bus terminal on Avenija Marina Držića, a working transit hub catalogued by the Zagreb Film Office for traffic-connection scenes.

locations.name: Zagreb Faculty of Law
locations.setting: Main building of the University of Zagreb's Faculty of Law, listed by the Zagreb Film Office among the city's school and university buildings available for filming.

locations.name: Zagreb Fair
locations.setting: Mid-twentieth-century trade fair ground south of the Sava with modernist exhibition pavilions, large halls and an open showground used for trade events year round.
locations.facilities: 132,000 sq m of pavilion space and 6,000 sq m of open-air space; the Technology Park occupies pavilion 12, at 5,000 sq m.

locations.name: Zagreb Film
locations.setting: Croatia's veteran animation studio, producing shorts and features since 1953 across three Zagreb premises with artist studios, shooting equipment and a small theatre.
locations.facilities: Stop-animation studio at Savska cesta 9-11 in central Zagreb with 452 m2 of working space for building sets, puppets and props, plus a separate shooting studio with a concrete floor, professional lighting, a DitoGear motion control system and green chroma-key backgrounds, and an in-house post-production department. The institution also holds an archive of more than 700 animated, 600 documentary and 14 feature films.
locations.logistics: Vlaska 70, Zagreb.

locations.name: Zagreb Main Railway Station
locations.setting: Zagreb's principal railway station, an 1892 Austro-Hungarian building on Tomislav Square with a domed main hall and platforms facing the city's museum quarter.

locations.name: 64 U Hradeb, Prague
locations.setting: A derelict 1964 cinema behind a courtyard off Mostecka street in Prague's Mala Strana, flood-damaged in 2002 and left as raw concrete and brick around a 600-seat hall with a balcony.
locations.facilities: Around 3,000 square metres of interior including main hall, corridors and a paved courtyard atrium

locations.name: Archbishop's Palace, Kroměříž
locations.setting: UNESCO-listed baroque archbishop's palace with opulent state rooms and formal gardens that have stood in for imperial Vienna.
locations.facilities: Sala terrena (full hall): up to 150 people (100 seated). Single hall of the Sala terrena: 70. Stucco Hall and Tiled Stove Hall: 50 (with chairs and tables). Cold-kitchen catering available. Adjacent to the Palace Garden (own site).
locations.suitability: The palace's own site notes that films have been shot there ('Filmovalo se u nas') (own site).

locations.name: Automatic Mills, Pardubice
locations.setting: A 1909 Gocar-designed automatic flour mill on the Chrudimka river in central Pardubice, in continuous operation until 2013 and now being redeveloped as a cultural quarter with a gallery and public square.

locations.name: Aviation Museum Kunovice
locations.setting: Aircraft collection and hangars at Kunovice airfield near Uherské Hradiště, on the site of the former Let Kunovice aircraft works, with propeller planes and gliders on display.
locations.facilities: Nearly three dozen historic aircraft from the local aviation museum on site, in a production hall that has been in continuous operation since the 1950s (Czech Film Commission listing).

locations.name: AZ Tower, Brno
locations.setting: The tallest building in the Czech Republic, a 111 metre, 30-storey tower in Brno completed in 2013, with a ground-floor shopping gallery, mid-rise commercial floors and apartments on the top levels.

locations.name: Barrandov Studios
locations.setting: Prague studio complex dating from the early 1930s with large sound stages, extensive costume and prop stocks and backlot space.
locations.facilities: 14 soundproof stages totalling 10,900 m2 at Barrandov plus four at the Hostivar site, most with rigging pulley systems; permanent exterior sets include a 15,000 m2 medieval town with buildings up to 10 m and a 39 x 60 m Paris street with twenty facades and ten interiors. Production rooms, makeup and dressing rooms, wardrobe, camera and prop storage, catering spaces and a large costume and prop stock.
locations.suitability: Offers stage rental, set construction, costume and prop rental, dubbing and production support, with on-site firefighting services for pyrotechnics and high-risk scenes; the studio cites the Czech cash rebate of up to 35 percent.
locations.logistics: Barrandov site 10 minutes from Prague city centre and 15 minutes from Vaclav Havel Airport, Hostivar site 18 minutes from both; parking for cars and trucks on site. Website in Czech only.

locations.name: Bilina Spa (Kyselka)
locations.setting: A disused 19th-century spa in Bilina with an empty main building, two guest wings, an inhalation hall and a forest park, offered completely bare and open to interior changes for filming.

locations.name: Bohnice Psychiatric Hospital
locations.setting: Pavilion-style psychiatric hospital campus opened in 1909 on a wooded hillside in north Prague, dozens of period brick buildings connected by paths and gardens, still in clinical use.
locations.price_note: Filming from CZK 5,000 per hour for interior, CZK 4,500 per hour for exterior, plus CZK 2,000 per hour for professional supervision (own site).
locations.facilities: Interior and exterior filming spaces are available within the hospital grounds (own site).
locations.suitability: Interior and exterior filming are permitted (own site).

locations.name: Brněnec Textile Factory
locations.setting: 19th century textile mill complex on the Svitava river in the village of Brněnec, with brick production halls, a chimney and former worker housing.

locations.name: Brno Exhibition Centre
locations.setting: Large trade fair and exhibition ground south-west of Brno's centre, with functionalist 1920s pavilions and modern halls used for conventions, concerts and filming.
locations.facilities: 14 exhibition halls (19 conference halls). Conference hall E1abc: theatre capacity 1,008, congress capacity 936. Conference hall Rotunda: theatre capacity 450. Smaller halls from 30 (theatre). Open-air areas from 1,797 to 12,809 sqm (paved, gravel or bituminous surface). Hall heights from 2.9 to 26.7 m (own site).
locations.logistics: On-site Expoparking service (own site).

locations.name: Brummel's House, Plzeň
locations.setting: A 1929 townhouse in Plzeň with an interior designed by architect Adolf Loos for the Brummel family, its five rooms and original furniture surviving wartime bombing and a 1980s demolition attempt.

locations.name: Budweiser Budvar Brewery
locations.setting: Working state brewery on the northern edge of Ceske Budejovice, with early 20th century brick brewhouses, cellars, bottling lines and a visitor centre offering plant tours.

locations.name: Cafe Bajer, Pardubice
locations.setting: An early 20th-century cafe in Pardubice reopened by its current owners in 1998, its rooms filled with period advertising signs, a winter garden, a small courtyard terrace and a working antique cash register.

locations.name: Café Louvre
locations.setting: Grand 1902 Art Nouveau café on Národní street in Prague, with a billiard room and tall windows over the street, run continuously except for a closure during the communist period.

locations.name: Český Krumlov
locations.setting: Renaissance and baroque town wrapped in a tight bend of the Vltava river beneath a painted castle tower.
locations.known_for: The Adventures of Pinocchio (1996), Hostel (2005), The Illusionist (2006)

locations.name: Cheb Railway Station
locations.setting: Historic railway station in the west Bohemian border town of Cheb, with period platforms and a station building listed by the national film commission as a filming location.

locations.name: Chomutov Municipal Baths
locations.setting: A 1980s indoor swimming complex in Chomutov with a 50 metre pool, a two-storey entrance hall, an underground plant room and wide terraces, empty and awaiting redevelopment.
locations.facilities: Connected to mains electricity, several thousand square metres of interior

locations.name: Coal and Water Storage Tower Vratislavice
locations.setting: Early 20th century coaling station and water tower on the edge of Liberec, with a 75 metre boiler chimney and a steam power house linked by a two arch bridge, largely unaltered.
locations.facilities: Boiler room with a 75 metre chimney and a steam power plant connected to a tower bridge with two arches (Czech Film Commission listing).

locations.name: ČSOB Pojišťovna Office, Pardubice
locations.setting: A 1990s post-revolutionary office building on Pardubice's main square, housing most of the ČSOB insurance company, with filming possible by appointment.

locations.name: D1 Studios
locations.setting: Virtual production facility near Prague with one 29x27m stage, 11m high, and a 180-degree curved LED wall about 14m in diameter for XR and motion capture work.
locations.facilities: Single stage 29x27m, 11m height, with prep, make-up and office rooms. LED wall P2.6 1000nits, 180-degree curved, 14.32m diameter (18x6m), movable ceiling.
locations.suitability: Virtual production, XR stage shoots, full-body motion capture and digital doubles.
locations.logistics: Modletice 141, Praha-vychod, near Prague.

locations.name: Dalesice Brewery
locations.setting: Small joint stock brewery in the village of Dalesice with 19th century brewhouse machinery, a malting floor, an on site hotel and restaurant, and a brewery museum.

locations.name: DEPO2015
locations.setting: Former bus depot in Plzeň converted into a creative and cultural centre, with workshop halls, a gallery and event space that keep the building's industrial steel roof trusses.
locations.facilities: Industrial complex with a cafe, market hall and event spaces; wheelchair accessible throughout except some office areas (own site).
locations.logistics: On-site parking within the complex; address Presslova 14, Plzen (own site).

locations.name: Dlouhe Strane Power Plant
locations.setting: Pumped storage hydroelectric plant in the Jeseniky mountains with an upper reservoir on a bare ridge and a turbine hall built deep inside the mountain, open for guided tours.

locations.name: Dolní Morava Sky Bridge
locations.setting: 721-metre pedestrian suspension bridge strung between two ridges above the Dolní Morava mountain resort near Králický Sněžník, with a glass-floored lookout and a nearby forest canopy walkway.

locations.name: Dolní Vítkovice
locations.setting: Former ironworks and coking plant just south of Ostrava's centre, with blast furnaces, a gasometer and a coal tower preserved as an industrial heritage site with exhibition and event space.
locations.suitability: Photography and filming on site is governed by the venue's published rules for photography and filming in the area and its buildings (own site).

locations.name: Fantasy Studios
locations.setting: Virtual production studio in Kladno with two stages, 29.4x27.7m and 17.4x12.1m, used for content creation and motion capture, with a Prague production office.
locations.facilities: Studio A: 29.4x27.7m. Studio B: 17.4x12.1m. Virtual production and motion capture equipment.
locations.suitability: Virtual production filming.
locations.logistics: Studios at Hutska 249, Kladno; production office at Pristavni 16a, Prague 7.

locations.name: Flaje Dam
locations.setting: Concrete arch dam in the Krusne hory mountains near the German border, holding back a reservoir in a forested valley, with the dam wall and spillway accessible on foot.

locations.name: Gong
locations.setting: Former gasometer at the Lower Vítkovice ironworks in Ostrava converted into a circular concert and exhibition hall inside its riveted steel shell.

locations.name: Grandhotel Pupp
locations.setting: Baroque and neoclassical spa hotel at the head of Karlovy Vary's colonnade, with ballrooms, a casino and period guest rooms dating back to the 18th century.
locations.facilities: Festive Hall: 735 sqm, ceiling height 15 m, natural light, up to 500 people (cocktail), 424 (banquet), 400 (theatre). Johann Georg hall: 122 sqm, up to 84 (theatre), 70 (cocktail). Heinrich room: 32 sqm, up to 12 (block setup). Beethoven rooms: 29 to 73 sqm, 8 to 45 (theatre), combined Beethoven II+III up to 50 (cocktail). Floor loading capacity is described as sufficient for passenger cars (own site).
locations.suitability: The hotel says it has attracted filmmakers since the early days of cinema, with dozens of films shot there including the Bond film Casino Royale (own site).

locations.name: Hamza Treatment Centre, Luže-Košumberk
locations.setting: A working rehabilitation hospital founded in 1901 near Luže, with historic pavilions, functionalist buildings and newer wings set in an enclosed park with an arboretum, usable as a spa, hospital or period medical setting.

locations.name: Hlubina Coal Mine, Ostrava
locations.setting: A former coal mine in Ostrava's Lower Vítkovice industrial complex, reconstructed since 2015 into a cultural centre with studios, rehearsal rooms and multipurpose halls inside its 19th and 20th century mining buildings.
locations.facilities: Screening rooms for 22 and 60 people, 368 m2 of open office space, music rehearsal rooms and a recording studio in the Cineport building

locations.name: Holešovice Market
locations.setting: Late 19th century cattle market and slaughterhouse complex on the Vltava embankment in Holešovice, with brick market halls now used for food stalls, shops and events.
locations.facilities: Hala 13: 1,500 sqm. Hala 11: 560 sqm. Hala 17: 900 sqm. Trzni namesti (market square): 2,600 sqm. Korzo: 4,000 sqm. Hala 40 (4th floor): 485 sqm. Hala 22 market stalls from 10 sqm (own site).

locations.name: Horní Bradlo Glassworks
locations.setting: A partially abandoned 1866 glassworks in Horní Bradlo covering about 6,000 square metres, combining the original building with a 1960s extension and boiler house, with a Christmas-decoration shop still trading on site.
locations.facilities: 400 volt electricity supply on site

locations.name: Hotel Jalta
locations.setting: 1958 socialist-modernist hotel on Wenceslas Square with a preserved Cold War-era nuclear bunker in the basement, run today as a functioning hotel with a small museum.

locations.name: Hotel Thermal
locations.setting: Brutalist 1970s hotel and congress complex beside the Ohře river in Karlovy Vary, with a rooftop pool and an open-air cinema terrace, the home base of the city's international film festival.

locations.name: Hranicar
locations.setting: Former border crossing customs house on the Elbe riverbank, converted into a community arts centre with a cinema, gallery, bar and courtyard used for events.
locations.facilities: Main hall seats up to 305 people (330 with extra seating), with a 10 by 8 metre stage, a lighting rig and wifi. Foyer with cafe/bar holds 45 to 150 people depending on the event (own site).

locations.name: Jested Tower Hotel
locations.setting: Single cone shaped hotel and television transmitter on the summit of Jested mountain above Liberec, reached by cable car, with a circular restaurant and panoramic windows.

locations.name: Jihoceske Divadlo (South Bohemian Theatre)
locations.setting: Repertory theatre in central Ceske Budejovice with an early 20th century auditorium, stage house and backstage workshops still used for daily opera, drama and ballet productions.

locations.name: Karel Pippich Theatre, Chrudim
locations.setting: A restored 1931-1934 constructivist theatre in Chrudim, with a 302-seat main auditorium, a stage, an auxiliary stage, an orchestra pit, a foyer and a cafe spread over one basement and three upper floors.

locations.name: Kaznice Brno (Brno House of Correction)
locations.setting: A 1740s Baroque former prison and orphanage in central Brno, four linked wings around three courtyards under an intact 18th-century roof, mostly empty aside from monthly public tours.
locations.facilities: Electricity in the chapel, workshop room and corridor to the former death cells; running water in the front building; almost 8,000 square metres of interior.

locations.name: Klasterni Hradisko (Military Hospital Olomouc)
locations.setting: Former Premonstratensian monastery on the edge of Olomouc, now a working military hospital, with baroque courtyards and church interiors alongside functioning medical wards.
locations.price_note: Ceremonial hall from CZK 5,000 per hour, library from CZK 2,100 per hour, convent gardens from CZK 1,000 per hour, AV equipment CZK 5,000 per event, audio-only CZK 2,500 per event, excl. VAT, prices marked indicative, valid from 1 April 2024 (own site).
locations.facilities: Ceremonial hall, library, lecture hall and convent gardens available to hire, with AV or audio-only equipment (own site).

locations.name: Klementinum
locations.setting: Former Jesuit college in Prague's Old Town now housing the National Library, with a baroque astronomical tower, mirrored chapel and historic library halls available for events and filming.

locations.name: Klubcentrum Culture House, Usti nad Orlici
locations.setting: A 1980s culture house in Usti nad Orlici with a 600-seat multi-purpose hall, stage, bar and dressing rooms, its own lighting and sound equipment, next to a hotel and restaurant.
locations.facilities: Stage, bar, dressing rooms, lounges, in-house lighting and sound equipment

locations.name: Kraus Apartment, Plzen
locations.setting: An Adolf Loos-designed 1930-31 apartment in Plzen with a green Cipollino marble salon under a dark mahogany ceiling, mirrored walls, an adjoining dining room and a fitted-wardrobe bedroom.

locations.name: Lachema, Brno
locations.setting: Empty production halls and corridors of a former Czechoslovak chemical works in Brno that made laboratory reagents, dyes and biochemicals from 1953 until its 2010 closure, now home to a stunt team.

locations.name: Lahofer Winery, Znojmo
locations.setting: A working vineyard winery near Znojmo with a sculpted concrete roofline, a walkable viewing roof, an open-air summer amphitheatre and modern cellars, set among vines looking toward Austria.

locations.name: Landek Park
locations.setting: Former hard coal mine at Petrkovice on the edge of Ostrava, now an open-air mining museum with pit head towers, wagons and underground galleries open to visitors.

locations.name: Liebieg Villa, Liberec
locations.setting: A romantic historicist villa built in three stages between 1897 and 1911 for the Liebieg textile family in Liberec, with a mythological ceiling fresco in its Hall of Fables and a period motor garage.

locations.name: Lovosice Port
locations.setting: River port and container terminal on the Elbe at Lovosice in north Bohemia, with cranes, quaysides and warehouse sheds serving inland barge traffic.

locations.name: Lucerna Palace
locations.setting: 1921 Art Nouveau passage complex in central Prague, with a domed concert hall, one of the city's oldest cinemas and a chain of shopping arcades under glass roofs.
locations.facilities: Main cinema: 453 seats, 4K digital projection with 3D and Dolby Surround 7.1. Small cinema hall: 51 seats, 2K digital projection with 3D and Dolby Surround 7.1. Marble Hall: 300 sqm, 150 to 350 people depending on the event, parquet floor, stage, dressing room and toilets. Gallery: 400 sqm, 150 to 200 people. Cafe: 300 sqm, 120 seats. Club Konicek: 90 sqm, 44 seats (own site).

locations.name: Luhačovice Spa
locations.setting: Moravian spa town built up from 1902 around mineral springs, with colonnades and hotel buildings designed by architect Dušan Jurkovič in a distinctive folk-art style.

locations.name: Mahen Theatre
locations.setting: 1882 neo-baroque theatre in Brno, the first public building in Europe lit entirely by Edison electric light, still in use as part of the National Theatre Brno.
locations.known_for: First electrically lit theatre building in Europe (1882)

locations.name: Masaryk University
locations.setting: Brno's largest university, spanning a historic main building near the city centre and modern faculty campuses, with lecture halls and campus architecture listed by the film commission.

photo.author: Kounics_palace_in_Brno_2010.jpg: User:Sveter (Please credit as "Petr Šmerkl, Wikipedia" in case you use this outside WMF

locations.name: Mendel Greenhouse, Brno
locations.setting: A modern glasshouse rebuilt on the footprint of Gregor Mendel's original greenhouse at the Augustinian Abbey in Brno, combining a permanent exhibition, event space and working plant beds.

locations.name: Michal Mine
locations.setting: Complete early 20th century coal mine surface plant in Ostrava-Michálkovice, with preserved machine hall, boiler house and pithead baths run as a branch of the National Technical Museum.
locations.suitability: Exterior photography is permitted for personal use. Interior photography without flash, tripod, selfie stick or lighting equipment is allowed only in guide-designated rooms for personal use. Guided-tour filming and drone footage are not permitted (own site).
locations.logistics: Parking in front of the mine entrance; buses park within the grounds (own site).

locations.name: Michaluv Statek Farmstead, Pohled
locations.setting: A preserved farmstead in the small village of Pohled on the Sazava river in Vysocina, with a farmhouse, cattle byre, granary, barn and open dooryard illustrating rural life from the 17th to early 20th century.
locations.facilities: Farmhouse interior about 50 square metres, byre 60 square metres, granary 50 square metres, yard 2,000 square metres, garden 4,800 square metres

locations.name: Mladotický mlýn, Mladotice
locations.setting: A former mill estate of over 1,000 square metres near Ronov nad Doubravou, with three reconstructed buildings and one original late 19th-century mill, a natural lake, a theatre, an outdoor amphitheatre, an old forge and stables.

locations.name: Municipal House
locations.setting: Art Nouveau civic building on Republic Square in Prague completed in 1912, with the Smetana concert hall, ceremonial reception rooms, a café and restaurant behind an ornate mosaic facade.
locations.facilities: Ten halls and rooms including the Smetana Hall, Mayor's Hall, Gregr Hall, Sladkovsky Hall, Palacky Hall and Rieger Hall, plus several parlours and a confectionery space (own site).
locations.logistics: Address nam. Republiky 1090/5, Prague 1. Metro A (Mustek, 4 minute walk) or metro B (Namesti Republiky); tram lines 6, 8, 15, 26 to Namesti Republiky (own site).

locations.name: National Stud Kladruby nad Labem
locations.setting: A working national stud farm at Kladruby nad Labem breeding the Kladruber horse, pairing the historic stud with a chateau and open pastureland for the horses.

locations.name: Olomouc Town Hall
locations.setting: Gothic and Renaissance town hall on Olomouc's main square, with a tower, an open loggia and an astronomical clock rebuilt in a socialist-realist style after wartime damage.

locations.name: Pardubice Airport
locations.setting: A small international airport on the edge of Pardubice next to the racecourse, with a 2.5 kilometre by 75 metre runway, ground-support vehicles and hangar space, open to filming.
locations.logistics: Filming permits are typically issued within days rather than weeks, provided the runway does not need a long closure.

locations.name: Pardubice Hospital
locations.setting: Regional hospital campus in Pardubice combining older pavilion wings with newer clinical buildings, listed by the national film commission as an available filming location.

locations.name: Pardubice Prison
locations.setting: A working prison in Pardubice that makes cells, a visiting room and cellars available for filming, arranged directly through the facility's own spokesperson.

locations.name: Pardubice Racecourse
locations.setting: A horse racing track on the edge of Pardubice with a 2,200 metre circuit, host to a racing season that runs from May to October.

locations.name: Pardubice Town Hall
locations.setting: The municipal town hall of Pardubice, on náměstí Republiky in the historic centre.

locations.name: Pastviny Dam
locations.setting: A 1932-1938 dam on the Divoká Orlice river at Pastviny, combining a reservoir with a working hydroelectric power plant.

locations.name: Plumlov Castle
locations.setting: A single-wing Mannerist castle built 1680-1688 above the Hloučela stream near Plumlov for the Liechtenstein family, its 1686 stuccoed hall and painted ceilings surviving from an originally planned four-wing design.

locations.name: Prague Main Railway Station
locations.setting: Prague's principal railway terminus, with an Art Nouveau departure hall from 1909 by architect Josef Fanta grafted onto a modern underground concourse and platforms.

locations.name: Prague Metro
locations.setting: Three line underground network opened in 1974, with deep late-communist era stations finished in coloured anodised aluminium panels and marble, still in daily operation.

photo.author: Matěj Čadil=en:User:Neral as confirmed here 2007-01-25 (in Czech)

locations.name: Prague Studios
locations.setting: A large Prague production complex with nine sound stages, a 25-acre backlot and a dedicated water stage, used by international streaming and studio productions.
locations.facilities: Nine stages: Stage 1 2,953 m2 (31,786 sq ft), Stage 2 2,531 m2 (27,243 sq ft), Stage 3 1,269 m2 (13,659 sq ft), Stage 4 1,269 m2, Stage 5-6 water tank 1,269 m2, Stage 7 1,235 m2 (13,293 sq ft, listed as best for virtual production), Stage 8 (HIVE) 1,908 m2 (20,538 sq ft) and Stage 9 (HIVE) 1,760 m2 (18,944 sq ft), with full rigging and a 25-acre backlot.
locations.logistics: Touzimska 867, Prague 18.

locations.name: Přílepy Chateau
locations.setting: An abandoned chateau in the village of Přílepy in the Zlín Region, converted from a 15th-century fortress by 1885 and later run as a maternity hospital until it emptied, set in a public park with rare trees.
locations.logistics: 18 km from Kroměříž; crew accommodation available 3 km away in Holešov

locations.name: Schejbal's Villa, Choceň
locations.setting: A 1920 New Classical Revival villa in Choceň with a symmetrical facade and smooth plaster cladding, designed by architect Antonín Plíhal, its large hall, kitchen and veranda kept close to the original interior.

locations.name: Secondary School of Textile Engineering Liberec
locations.setting: Working textile college on Textilni street with period spinning and weaving machinery still in place alongside plain classroom interiors and a gated parking yard.
locations.logistics: Spacious parking lot on the premises with a lockable gate (Czech Film Commission listing).

locations.name: Sokol Hradec Králové Sports Complex
locations.setting: Functionalist gymnasium and sports hall complex built for the Sokol movement in Hradec Králové, with large open exercise halls and period fittings.

locations.name: Spielberk Office Centrum, Brno
locations.setting: A Class A business park in Brno made of five low-rise office villas in Dutch brick with roof terraces, set asymmetrically around a lake with a view toward the city's cathedral.

locations.name: Statek Uhersko Farmhouse
locations.setting: An early Baroque farmhouse near Uhersko standing for more than 400 years, with farm buildings, a yard, a dairy, an original malt house, a mill and a cow house around a working restaurant and guest accommodation.

locations.name: Štramberk
locations.setting: A small town in the Beskyd foothills known as Moravia's Bethlehem, with half-timbered 18th and 19th century cottages, a Baroque town square and the Gothic Trúba tower, the last remnant of its 13th-century castle.

locations.name: Techmania Science Center
locations.setting: Interactive science museum in a former Skoda Works foundry hall in the Bory district of Plzen, combining a large industrial shed with modern exhibition halls and a planetarium.

locations.name: Teplarny Brno (Spitalka heating plant)
locations.setting: A working district heating and power plant on Spitalka street in Brno, opened in 1930 on piled marsh foundations, with an old boiler house still holding historic Kolben-Danek machinery.

locations.name: Terezín Small Fortress
locations.setting: 18th century star fort east of Terezín used as a political prison under Austria-Hungary and as a Gestapo prison during the German occupation, with cell blocks and courtyards preserved as a memorial.

locations.name: The Factory, Lichkov
locations.setting: A disused timber factory in Lichkov near the Polish border, running from 1871 until a 1973 fire and 1990s privatisation closed it, its chimney with a stork's nest above an empty 22,400 square metre brownfield.

locations.name: The Papirna Multifunctional Center
locations.setting: Renovated paper mill building of about 4,000 square metres by the Radbuza river near central Plzen, holding a large industrial hall, an art studio, cafe and exhibition rooms.
locations.facilities: Renovated 4,000 m2 industrial space including an art studio, a cafe, exhibition spaces, a large industrial hall, rehearsal rooms, dance halls and an accessible roof, with high-quality technical facilities (Czech Film Commission listing).
locations.logistics: Near the Radbuza River, a short distance from the Pilsen city centre, and connected to the motorway (Czech Film Commission listing).

locations.name: Thomas Bata Villa
locations.setting: Functionalist 1911 villa built for shoe manufacturer Tomáš Baťa on the edge of Zlín's factory district, later enlarged and now used as a museum of the Baťa family and its management methods.

locations.name: Tlumacov Stud Farm
locations.setting: A working state stud farm near Zlin founded in 1925 on an 18th-century manor yard, with vaulted stables for around 115 breeding stallions of several breeds, a forge and a director's villa.
locations.facilities: Three stables, forge, insemination station, equine treadmill, riding hall, horse-drawn carriages available

locations.name: Tomas Bata University in Zlín
locations.setting: University built inside the former Baťa shoe factory's functionalist halls in Zlín, glass-and-steel-frame factory buildings from the 1930s adapted into lecture rooms and laboratories.

locations.name: TTC Studio Jinonice
locations.setting: Two sound stages in Prague's Jinonice district, about 1,200m2 and 270m2, used for film, television, commercials and photography since 2007.
locations.facilities: Studio 1: 24 x 48 m, 10 m high, usable area almost 1,200 m2, 400 V / 300 A power, acoustic wall with SONIT cladding and 42 dB sound-insulating doors, 82 hanging eyes rated 200 kg each, blacked out and insulated for sync sound, with ventilation and heating independent of the support areas. Studio 2: 11.5 x 23.5 m, 4.5 m high, 270 m2, 400 V / 125 A, a cyclorama backing 10 m wide, 5 m high and 10 m deep, daylight possible and hanging bars under the ceiling. Equipped makeup rooms, wardrobe, offices, changing rooms and storage; the studio opened in 2007.
locations.suitability: Film and television productions, commercials, photography and presentation events.
locations.logistics: Stodulecka 586/4, Prague 5, with ample on-site parking.

locations.name: Underground Water Reservoir Brno
locations.setting: Disused 19th century brick water reservoir cut into a hillside near Brno's exhibition grounds, with vaulted underground chambers now hired out for exhibitions and events.
locations.facilities: Vaulted underground spaces; declared a cultural monument in 2019 (Czech Film Commission).
locations.logistics: Owned by the City of Brno; administration is being handed to TIC BRNO (Brno Tourist Information Centre), which leases the space to film crews (Czech Film Commission).

locations.name: UPP (Universal Production Partners)
locations.setting: Prague visual effects house offering virtual production services and a dedicated stage at its Milin studio outside the city.
locations.facilities: Milin Studio outside Prague: a motion capture stage of 405 sq m active floor with 108 Vicon cameras, able to hold more than 20 actors at once of whom 10 in full performance capture, Manus Quantum Metagloves for hand capture, stereo headcams for facial capture and a 27 sq m LED display wall with virtual camera hardware and video assist. A film stage and a VFX art department / miniatures department are listed as coming soon.
locations.suitability: Virtual production filming and VFX supervision.
locations.logistics: Head office at Zitomirska 7, Prague 10.

locations.name: Ústí nad Orlicí Hospital
locations.setting: A working regional hospital in Ústí nad Orlicí with over 330 beds, including a four-storey emergency pavilion opened in 2022, part of a group of five Pardubice Region hospitals available for filming.

locations.name: Villa Stiassni
locations.setting: 1929 functionalist villa in Brno built for textile manufacturer Alfred Stiassni and later used as a state guesthouse, with period furniture, gardens and a swimming pool.
locations.facilities: Garden of over 3 hectares with a tennis court, swimming pool, terrace and loggia. Interior salons with wood panelling, marble fireplaces and stucco. A modern lecture building is also on site (current official site: vila-stiassni.cz).
locations.logistics: Parking on Hroznova street, not within the villa grounds. Address Hroznova 14, Brno-Pisarky (vila-stiassni.cz).

locations.name: Villa Tugendhat
locations.setting: UNESCO-listed 1930 modernist villa in Brno by Ludwig Mies van der Rohe, with a glass-walled living hall, an onyx wall and a travertine terrace over the garden and city.
locations.facilities: Garden and multiple floors, including exhibition rooms on the technical floor (own site).
locations.suitability: Filming and photo shoots are listed among the event types permitted at the villa (own site).

locations.name: Vodojemy na Zlutem kopci, Brno
locations.setting: Two disused brick water reservoirs from 1872 on Zluty kopec hill in Brno, joined later by two concrete tanks, decommissioned in 1997 and now toured as cavernous underground chambers.

locations.name: Vojna Memorial
locations.setting: An intact forced-labour camp near Pribram built in 1947-49 for uranium mining and later a political prison until 1960, preserved with its command building, bunker and unheated punishment cells.
locations.known_for: Zdivocela zeme, Bumerang, Piknik, Nackt unter Wolfen

locations.name: Vonwiller Factory, Zamberk
locations.setting: A former 1838 textile mill on the edge of Zamberk, now a museum of antique machinery and vehicles, with a working line-shaft machine shop, forge, narrow-gauge railway and a stock of vintage cars.
locations.facilities: Functional line-shaft machine shop with over 30 machines, forge, narrow-gauge railway, vintage car and motorcycle collection, restoration workshop

locations.name: Wesselský Water Mill, Loučky
locations.setting: A working watermill on the Oder river in Loučky, with a functioning 3.6 metre mill wheel, eight farm buildings and period interiors that can be adapted to different historical eras.
locations.facilities: Accommodation for up to 12 guests on site, parking for up to 10 cars and a bus, lockable storage space
locations.logistics: 50 km from Ostrava, 70 km from Olomouc; larger crews can be housed 5 to 8 km away

locations.name: Winternitz Villa
locations.setting: 1932 house in Prague's Smíchov district designed by Adolf Loos around his raumplan of interlocking split levels, now a museum open for tours and filming by appointment.

locations.name: Zabrdovice Municipal Baths, Brno
locations.setting: A 1932 Bohuslav Fuchs bathing complex in Brno's Zabrdovice district built around two courtyards, its outdoor pool still operating as a public lido while the closed indoor winter baths await reuse.

locations.name: Zbrojovka, Brno
locations.setting: The former Czechoslovak state arms works in Brno's Husovice district, founded in 1918, which also repaired cars and rail equipment and made weapons before its 1945 machinery seeded the Zetor tractor brand.

locations.name: Zlín Factory Complex
locations.setting: Grid of red brick functionalist factory halls built by the Baťa shoe company in Zlín from the 1920s, now reused as a university, offices and cultural venues.

locations.name: Bakken (Dyrehavsbakken)
locations.setting: An amusement park dating to 1583 inside the Jaegersborg Dyrehave deer park north of Copenhagen, with rides, variety theatres and restaurants under old beech trees.
locations.suitability: Hosts company events and group bookings (own site: 'Firmaarrangementer')

locations.name: Bella Center
locations.setting: Scandinavia's second-largest exhibition and conference centre in Copenhagen's Orestad district, with a congress hall for up to 4,200 people, four auditoriums and an adjoining hotel tower.
locations.known_for: Olsen-banden ser rodt (The Olsen Gang Outta Sight)

locations.name: Bornholm Airport
locations.setting: Regional airport near Roenne on Bornholm with scheduled flights to Copenhagen, Aalborg, Billund and Sonderborg, the island's only air link.

locations.name: Carlsberg Byen
locations.setting: Former Carlsberg brewery grounds in Copenhagen, redeveloped into a city district that keeps historic brewery halls and towers alongside new office, retail and residential buildings.

locations.name: Christiansborg Palace
locations.setting: Government palace on the Slotsholmen islet housing the Danish Parliament, Prime Minister's Office and Supreme Court, with a riding ground complex and palace square.
locations.suitability: The palace's manager, the Royal Danish Collection, states it welcomes press inquiries, including for TV shows, and that holders of valid press credentials get free admission to any of its palaces without advance booking (contact via the Head of Communications).

locations.name: Cirkusbygningen
locations.setting: A domed circus building from 1886 in central Copenhagen near Tivoli, its ring and tiered seating now hired out for shows, dinner theatre and events.
locations.suitability: Building available for hire for events (own site: 'Lej bygningen til dit event')

locations.name: Copenhagen City Hall
locations.setting: The seat of Copenhagen's municipal government on Radhuspladsen, a National Romantic building from 1905 with a public atrium and clock tower, used for a tower scene in a 1978 comedy and for hospital-atrium scenes in a 2015 drama.
locations.known_for: The Olsen Gang Goes to War, The Danish Girl

locations.name: Copenhagen Police Headquarters (Politigarden)
locations.setting: A 1924 neoclassical police headquarters in central Copenhagen built around a 45-metre circular courtyard with 44 Doric columns, still an active police building, that has repeatedly played itself on screen.
locations.known_for: Broen/Bron (The Bridge), Forbrydelsen (The Killing), Olsen-banden films

locations.name: CopenHill (Amager Bakke)
locations.setting: Working waste-to-energy plant in Copenhagen with a rooftop ski slope, climbing wall and hiking trail built onto its sloped roof, plus a rooftop bar and cafe.
locations.facilities: Rooftop bar and event space, cafe, elevator access to the roof

locations.name: Dokk1
locations.setting: A large glass and concrete public library and citizen service building on Aarhus harbourfront, with open multi-storey interiors and a public square outside.

locations.name: DR Byen
locations.setting: The headquarters and production complex of the Danish Broadcasting Corporation on Amager, opened between 2006 and 2010, combining newsrooms, TV studios and the DR Koncerthuset concert hall.

locations.name: DR Koncerthuset
locations.setting: Concert hall in Copenhagen's Orestad district built for Danish public broadcaster DR, with a main concert hall, four recording studios and a restaurant, available for external hire.
locations.facilities: Concert hall, four recording studios, external hire for concerts and conferences

locations.name: FAENGSLET (Horsens State Prison)
locations.setting: Former Danish state prison in Horsens, closed in 2006 and reopened as a prison museum whose cell wings, exercise yards and workshop buildings are hired out for events and overnight stays.
locations.facilities: Cell wings, museum halls, conference and event spaces, overnight accommodation

locations.name: Filmby Aarhus
locations.setting: Creative business park in Aarhus's Sydhavnen district housing over 80 film, TV, gaming and animation companies, with production premises and an event bar for hire.
locations.price_note: Studio 1 DKK 17,142.00 per day plus VAT and Studio 2 DKK 8,571.00 per day plus VAT (2026 rates, own site); film productions and cultural events can get a 50 percent discount, and cleaning and electricity, water and heating are charged on top
locations.facilities: Two studios: Studio 1 of 576 m2 with 10.5 m clear height, a 137-line grid, a 4.8 m high studio door, internet and an optional 4 x 10 m LED screen for virtual production; Studio 2 of 267 m2 with 10.5 m clear height, a 60-line grid, a 4.8 m high door and a green cyclorama. Workshop, toilets and a laundry room with washing machine and dryer next to the studios, plus meeting and production rooms and a makeup room for hire.
locations.logistics: Access to the studios from a large enclosed production yard with room for production vehicles and charging for a production vehicle; the studios run on green electricity. Address Filmbyen 21, 8000 Aarhus C.

locations.name: Gammel Estrup
locations.setting: Renaissance manor house in Jutland, home to Denmark's national museum of manor life, with period rooms, stables, a moat and surrounding parkland used for events.

locations.name: Godsbanen
locations.setting: A former railway goods yard in Aarhus converted into a production house for culture and the arts, with its long brick freight sheds and tracks-side hall available to rent for events.
locations.suitability: Rooms and halls for hire for events (own site: 'Lej lokaler og skab events')

locations.name: H.C. Andersens Hus
locations.setting: A museum in Odense's old town dedicated to Hans Christian Andersen, combining a modern underground exhibition building with the historic house and courtyard where he was born.

locations.name: Hotel Koldingfjord
locations.setting: A former sanatorium turned hotel and conference centre on the shore of Kolding Fjord, with period interiors, function rooms and parkland running down to the water.

photo.author: FaceMePLS from The Hague, The Netherlands

locations.name: Kronborg Castle
locations.setting: Renaissance fortress at the narrowest point of the Øresund strait, with ramparts, a large courtyard and vaulted casemates, known as the Elsinore of Shakespeare's Hamlet.

locations.name: MCH Messecenter Herning
locations.setting: Denmark's largest exhibition and entertainment complex, spread across roughly 130 acres in Herning with halls used for trade fairs, concerts, sport and stage productions.

locations.name: Moens Klint (GeoCenter)
locations.setting: White chalk cliffs on the island of Moen rising up to 128 metres above the Baltic Sea, with a science centre, forest trails and beach access at the cliff base.
locations.suitability: Group bookings, guided tours and business/school event hosting

locations.name: Musikhuset Aarhus
locations.setting: A concert and performance complex in central Aarhus with ten stages under one glass-fronted roof, hosting everything from opera and classical concerts to comedy and family theatre.

locations.name: Nordisk Film Shortcut (360 Stage)
locations.setting: A 360-degree LED volume in Valby, Copenhagen, 16 metres in diameter with walls and ceiling fully covered in LED panels, built for virtual production.
locations.facilities: 360-degree LED stage, 16m diameter, full LED coverage on walls and ceiling, Unreal Engine and optical camera tracking. On-site sound suites, editing suites and Dolby Atmos mixing theatre.
locations.suitability: Virtual production filming, previsualisation and driving plates.
locations.logistics: Mosedalvej 14, Valby, Copenhagen.

locations.name: Nordisk Film Studios
locations.setting: Working studio lot in Valby founded in 1906, the world's oldest continuously active film studio, with shooting stages, post-production facilities and a 360-degree LED stage.
locations.facilities: 360-degree LED stage of 16 m diameter and 5.5 m height with LED walls and ceiling and an optional LED floor (ROE panels, up to 6,000 nits), run by Nordisk Film Shortcut; dressing rooms, makeup facilities and large parking for crew and grip trucks.
locations.suitability: The LED stage is offered for films, series, commercials, music videos and live events with virtual production supervision, Unreal Engine content, previs and driving plates; it takes vehicles, boats and planes up to 15 m. The stage runs on solar power from 2023.
locations.logistics: Mosedalvej 14, 2500 Valby, on the Nordisk Film lot; large parking for crew and grip trucks.

locations.name: Nordkraft
locations.setting: Former coal-fired power station on Aalborg's harbour front converted into a culture house, with theatre, music and exhibition halls inside the original turbine building.
locations.price_note: Commercial photography in shared areas from DKK 1,000 (about EUR 134) per day (own site)

locations.name: Nyboder
locations.setting: A historic grid of yellow single-storey row houses in central Copenhagen built from 1631 as Royal Danish Navy housing and still partly used as service housing, with a street used for a home-visit scene in a 2015 drama.

locations.name: Odense Havn
locations.setting: Commercial port on Funen with 3.9 kilometres of quay, heavy-lift cranes and large storage areas, used for offshore wind component handling and industrial tenants.
locations.facilities: Industrial space and quay for lease, heavy-load area, crane operations up to 1,200 tonnes

locations.name: Oresund Bridge
locations.setting: A cable-stayed rail and motorway bridge running nearly 8 kilometres from the Swedish coast to the artificial island of Peberholm, continuing to Denmark via the Oresund Tunnel.

locations.name: Refshaleøen
locations.setting: Former B&W shipyard peninsula in Copenhagen harbour, its industrial sheds, open dock space and workshop halls now let out for events, studios and small businesses.
locations.facilities: Industrial halls, open quay and dock space, event venues for hire

locations.name: Roskilde Cathedral
locations.setting: Brick cathedral in Roskilde and UNESCO World Heritage site, burial church of the Danish monarchy for over 500 years, with regular organ concerts and cultural events.

photo.author: CucombreLibre from New York, NY, USA

locations.name: Tivoli Gardens
locations.setting: Amusement park and pleasure garden in central Copenhagen dating from 1843, with rides, concert stages, themed architecture and landscaped gardens.
locations.facilities: Event and meeting spaces named on the business site include Nimb, Axelborgsalen and Kilden i Haven.

locations.name: Torvehallerne
locations.setting: Two glass-roofed market halls in central Copenhagen with food and drink stalls under one enclosed roof, plus an adjoining public square outside for exterior coverage.

locations.name: Utzon Center
locations.setting: Waterfront exhibition and knowledge centre in Aalborg designed by architect Jorn Utzon as his last work, with gallery halls, a restaurant and rooms available for hire.
locations.facilities: Room hire and booking, on-site restaurant

locations.name: Vridslose Prison (Vridsloeselille Faengsel)
locations.setting: A closed state prison in Albertslund built in 1859 and shut in 2018, its walled complex of cell blocks and a main gatehouse still standing at the edge of the town.

locations.name: Aidu Water Sports Centre
locations.setting: Former oil shale open cast mine turned into a rowing canal, with terraced spoil ridges, bare rock faces, gravel service roads and a long flat sheet of water.

locations.name: Ammende Villa
locations.setting: Art nouveau villa of 1905 in Parnu run as a hotel, with panelled salons, a ballroom, stained glass, a wooden veranda and a garden near the beach.

locations.name: Balti Jaama Turg
locations.setting: Covered market on several levels next to Tallinn's Baltic station, with produce and meat counters, a street food floor, second hand traders and a roof car park.

locations.name: BFM Film Studio, Tallinn University
locations.setting: Teaching sound stage of 160 sq m at the Baltic Film and Media School, 13.5 by 11.85 m with a 6.5 m height, motorised lighting, black, white and green backgrounds and a television gallery.
locations.facilities: 160 sq m stage, motorised lighting fixtures, dimmer and DMX cabling, 360 degree black drape, white and green screen, eight camera television setup, projector and screen, sound mixing and editing rooms in the same building.
locations.suitability: Also used for receptions, seminars and training events; rental terms through the school's head of production.

locations.name: Estonian Academy of Arts
locations.setting: Concrete and glass art school of 2018 near Kalamaja, with open stairwells, corridors, print, metal and ceramics workshops, studios and a roof terrace.

locations.name: Estonian National Museum
locations.setting: Long low museum at Raadi that rises out of a former Soviet airfield runway, with a glazed front, wide concrete halls and large open exhibition floors.

locations.name: Estonian National Opera (Estonia Theatre)
locations.setting: Jugendstil theatre of 1913 in central Tallinn holding both an opera auditorium and a concert hall, with foyers, boxes, orchestra pit and backstage areas.

locations.name: Ida Hub Film Studios
locations.setting: Purpose built studio complex at Johvi Business Park with a 2,000 sq m stage up to 20 m high, a 1,200 sq m multifunction stage, workshops, wardrobe, SFX rooms and post production floors.
locations.facilities: Two sound stages of 2,000 sq m and 1,200 sq m, soundproof walls and doors, heavy vehicle entrances, four storage rooms of 176 to 537 sq m, make-up and costume rooms with laundry, SFX rooms, ten editing rooms, sound studio, screening room, production offices.
locations.logistics: Johvi Business Park in Ida-Viru county, about 50 km west of Narva and 165 km east of Tallinn.

locations.name: Johvi Concert Hall
locations.setting: Concert hall in Johvi with a main auditorium, a smaller hall, glazed foyers and rehearsal rooms, serving as the main performance venue of Ida-Viru county.

locations.name: Kadriorg Palace
locations.setting: Baroque palace begun in 1718 for Peter the Great, with a two storey main hall, stucco ceilings, an art museum, a formal flower garden and a large park.

locations.name: Kohtla Mining Park-Museum
locations.setting: Former oil shale mine at Kohtla-Nomme with underground galleries reached by mine train, surface headframe, sorting plant, machine halls and a spoil hill.

locations.name: Kolga Manor
locations.setting: Neoclassical manor north east of Tallinn, part ruin and part restored, with an empty columned main house, service wings and a park, listed in the Film Estonia catalogue.

locations.name: Kopu Lighthouse
locations.setting: Stone lighthouse begun in the 16th century standing on a hill in the middle of Hiiumaa island, square in plan with four buttresses and a viewing gallery.

locations.name: Kreenholm Manufacturing
locations.setting: Disused 19th century textile mill on an island in the Narva river, with red brick spinning halls, empty machine floors, water channels and rows of workers housing.

locations.name: Krulli Quarter
locations.setting: Walled site of the former Franz Krull machine works near Tallinn's Baltic station, with brick and steel workshop halls, cobbled yards and rail sidings under redevelopment.

locations.name: Kumu Art Museum
locations.setting: Limestone and copper museum cut into the Lasnamae escarpment behind Kadriorg park, with a curved facade, a full height atrium, ramps and top lit galleries.

locations.name: Kuressaare Castle
locations.setting: Well preserved 14th century bishop's castle on Saaremaa, a square stone block with a defensive tower, vaulted halls, a chapel, a moat and earth bastions.

locations.name: Laagna Road, Lasnamae
locations.setting: Six lane road sunk into a limestone cutting across the Lasnamae housing district, lined with rock walls, footbridges and Soviet era apartment slabs.

locations.name: Lahemaa National Park
locations.setting: Coastal national park east of Tallinn with pine forest, raised bogs, boulder fields, fishing villages, manor estates and long stretches of undeveloped shore.

locations.name: Lennart Meri Tallinn Airport
locations.setting: International airport 4 km from the centre of Tallinn, with a compact passenger terminal, apron, cargo area and hangars beside a lake and the city ring road.
locations.logistics: Four kilometres from Tallinn old town, on the tram and bus network.

locations.name: Linnahall
locations.setting: Semi abandoned limestone concert and sports hall built for the 1980 Olympic regatta, with stepped terraces over the harbour, an empty auditorium and an ice hall.

locations.name: Maiasmokk Cafe
locations.setting: Cafe on Pikk street in Tallinn old town trading since 1864, with dark wood panelling, mirrored counters, a marzipan display room and a period shop front.

locations.name: Mooste Manor
locations.setting: Manor complex in south east Estonia with a red brick main house, a long stone barn, stables and a granary, in use as a folk culture and arts centre.

locations.name: Narva Castle
locations.setting: Medieval Danish and Livonian order castle on the Narva river facing the Russian bank, with a tall keep, courtyards, ramparts, cellars and a museum inside.

locations.name: Noblessner
locations.setting: Former submarine shipyard on Tallinn bay, with tall brick and concrete production halls, a foundry converted to an event hall, quayside promenade and a marina.

locations.name: Old City Harbour, Port of Tallinn
locations.setting: Passenger port a short walk from the old town, with ferry terminals, vehicle ramps, quays, a cruise berth and open dock areas run by Port of Tallinn.

locations.name: Ontika Cliff and Valaste Waterfall
locations.setting: Limestone escarpment on the north coast rising about 55 m above the sea, with exposed rock layers, a viewing platform and the highest waterfall in Estonia.

locations.name: Original Sokos Hotel Viru
locations.setting: Tower hotel of 1972 on the edge of Tallinn old town, with a period lobby and bar, upper floor rooms and a preserved KGB listening post and museum on the top floor.

locations.name: Padaste Manor
locations.setting: Restored manor hotel on Muhu island facing the sea, with stone farm buildings, a carriage house, panelled dining rooms and a spa in the former stables.

locations.name: Palmse Manor
locations.setting: Restored baroque manor in Lahemaa national park with period interiors, a distillery, greenhouse, stables, a coach house and a park with ponds.

locations.name: Parnu Beach
locations.setting: Wide shallow sand beach on the gulf of Riga with low dunes, a promenade, a 1930s functionalist beach house and pine woods behind.

locations.name: Patarei Sea Fortress
locations.setting: Empty 1840s coastal fortress on the Tallinn shore used as a prison until 2002, with cell wings, long corridors, exercise yards, a hospital block and vaulted casemates.

locations.name: Pohjala Factory
locations.setting: Former rubber factory on the Kopli peninsula in Tallinn, with brick production halls, tall steel windows, raw concrete floors and enclosed yards, now let as studios and event space.

locations.name: Rummu Quarry
locations.setting: Flooded limestone quarry beside the former Murru prison, with a white spoil mountain, submerged buildings and machinery, clear water and open ground for a unit base.
locations.logistics: About 45 km south west of Tallinn in Vasalemma parish.

locations.name: Sagadi Manor
locations.setting: Baroque manor of 1753 inside Lahemaa national park, with a pink main house, symmetrical outbuildings, a forest museum, a hotel wing and a landscaped park.

locations.name: Schloss Fall (Keila-Joa Manor)
locations.setting: Neo-Gothic manor of 1833 above the Keila waterfall, restored with period rooms, a concert hall, a suspension bridge and a wooded park, hired for events and stays.

locations.name: Seaplane Harbour (Lennusadam)
locations.setting: Maritime museum in 1917 concrete seaplane hangars on Tallinn bay, three thin shell domes over a dark hall with a submarine and boats, plus quays and icebreakers outside.

locations.name: Sillamae town centre
locations.setting: Post war town built for a uranium processing plant, laid out as a Stalinist axis of pastel apartment blocks with a culture house and a stairway down to the sea.

locations.name: Soprus Cinema
locations.setting: Stalinist cinema of 1955 in Tallinn old town, with a columned portico, a decorated foyer with chandeliers and a single auditorium still in daily use.

locations.name: Tallinn Creative Hub (Kultuurikatel)
locations.setting: Former city power station between the old town and the harbour, kept as raw concrete and brick halls with boiler house volumes, now a hireable cultural venue with large open floors.

locations.name: Tallinn Old Town
locations.setting: Walled medieval town of cobbled lanes, merchant houses, guild halls, churches and defence towers on two levels, in everyday use and covered by city filming permits.

locations.name: Tallinn Song Festival Grounds
locations.setting: Open air arena by the sea with a shell shaped concrete stage of 1960, a stepped choir stand for thousands of singers, a light tower and a wide sloping field.

locations.name: Tallinn Town Hall
locations.setting: Gothic town hall of 1404 on Raekoja square, with a vaulted citizens hall, council chamber, cellars and a tower, hired for events outside the visitor season.

locations.name: Tallinnfilm Studio (Tallinn Film Wonderland)
locations.setting: Studio complex under construction on the Paljassaare peninsula for the Estonian Film Institute, planned as three sound stages of about 3,500 sq m together, the largest 1,200 sq m with a 14 m ceiling.

locations.name: Tartu Airport
locations.setting: Small regional airport at Ulenurme south of Tartu, with one runway, a low terminal building, apron, hangars and light scheduled traffic.

locations.name: Tartu Market Hall
locations.setting: Functionalist market hall of 1937 in central Tartu, one wide barrel vaulted space with tiled counters for meat, fish, dairy and produce, and an open market outside.

locations.name: Tartu Town Hall Square
locations.setting: Sloping neoclassical square in the centre of Tartu, closed at the top by the 1789 town hall and lined with pastel merchant houses running down to the river.

locations.name: Telliskivi Creative City
locations.setting: Former railway repair works beside Tallinn's Baltic station, a block of low industrial buildings with painted brick walls, rail sidings, yards, bars, shops and studios.

locations.name: Ulemiste City
locations.setting: Business campus on a former factory site next to Tallinn airport, mixing glass office blocks with retained brick industrial halls, internal streets, car parks and a conference centre.

locations.name: Unibet Arena (Saku Suurhall)
locations.setting: Indoor arena in west Tallinn built in 2001 for concerts and sport, with a bowl seating several thousand, wide concourses, dressing rooms and truck access.

locations.name: University of Tartu Main Building
locations.setting: Neoclassical university building of 1809 with a columned portico, a white assembly hall, lecture rooms, an art museum and a former student lock-up in the attic.

locations.name: Vaba Lava Narva
locations.setting: Black box theatre in a converted building in central Narva, with a flexible main hall, technical grid, rehearsal rooms and offices available for hire.

locations.name: Vabamu and KGB Prison Cells
locations.setting: Museum of occupations at the foot of Toompea together with the preserved KGB prison cells on Pagari street, with holding cells, painted corridors and interrogation rooms.

locations.name: Vanemuine Theatre
locations.setting: Estonia's oldest theatre company in Tartu, working from a 1960s main house, a smaller house and a black box, with auditoria, foyers and set workshops.

locations.name: Vihula Manor Country Club and Spa
locations.setting: Manor estate in Lahemaa run as a hotel and spa, with a white main house, watermill, distillery, farm buildings, ponds and a park, listed in the Film Estonia catalogue.

locations.name: Cable Factory (Kaapelitehdas)
locations.setting: Former Nokia cable factory in Helsinki's Ruoholahti district, a long brick industrial building with high factory halls, now a large cultural centre housing museums, studios, galleries and rentable event spaces.
locations.facilities: Dedicated space-for-rent pages for event and studio hire within the former factory halls.
locations.logistics: Managed by Kiinteistö Oy Kaapelitalo; member of the Trans Europe Halles network of industrial cultural venues.

locations.name: Finlayson Area
locations.setting: Former cotton mill founded in 1820 beside the Tammerkoski rapids in Tampere, a complex of red-brick factory buildings including the 1877 Plevna weaving hall, now holding restaurants, a cinema, shops and offices.
locations.facilities: About 80,000 sq m of rentable space across the former factory buildings; individual premises range from about 10 sq m to several thousand sq m. The buildings hold the BREEAM In-Use environmental certificate.

locations.name: Hatanpaa Manor
locations.setting: A manor house on the shore of Lake Pyhajarvi close to central Tampere, set in an English-style park with rose gardens and on-site parking for about 20 cars.

locations.name: Haveri Mine
locations.setting: A former iron and gold mine near Ylojarvi, closed in 1960 and since flooded to form a deep, clear water-filled pit now used as a dive site.

locations.name: Helsinki Olympic Stadium
locations.setting: Functionalist 1938 stadium built for the 1952 Olympics, with a 72-metre tower and a renovated bowl used today for athletics, concerts, conferences and stadium tours.
locations.facilities: Meeting rooms, restaurant, seated event spaces and a rentable tower with panoramic views.

locations.name: Hiedanranta Area
locations.setting: A former pulp and paper mill site on Tampere's lakeshore, now repurposed as a mixed venue for arts, culture and research while redevelopment of the wider area continues.

locations.name: Ivalo
locations.setting: Village on the Ivalo River about 250 kilometres north of the Arctic Circle, surrounded by boreal forest and fells, with deep snow and polar night for much of the year.

locations.name: Kehräsaari
locations.setting: Former needle factory and wool mill on a small island in central Tampere, its 1897 red-brick U-shaped building now a shopping and business centre linked by footbridge to the riverside Koskikeskus district.
locations.facilities: Former needle factory and spinning mill, now used as a commercial and business centre between Laukontori marketplace and Koskikeskus shopping centre.
locations.logistics: 0.5 km from Tampere Central Square.

locations.name: Levi Ski Resort
locations.setting: Finland's largest ski resort on Levi fell in Kittila, with 43 marked slopes and 27 lifts amid birch and pine wilderness, used in winter for skiing and Northern Lights and in summer for fell hiking under the midnight sun.
locations.known_for: The Grand Tour: A Scandi Flick (2022)

locations.name: Mediapolis
locations.setting: Media campus at broadcaster Yle's Tohloppi site in Tampere, with fully equipped television studios and a 1,500 square metre factory hall stage available for hire.
locations.facilities: Two Yle broadcast studios of 432 m2 (24 x 18 m) and 342 m2 (19 x 18 m) with tungsten lighting, hoists and 360-degree curtains; a 1,200 m2 Factory Hall (26 x 54.5 m, 10 m clear height); smaller TAMK and United studios of 133 and 198 m2; wardrobe and makeup rooms, six sound studios and edit stations.
locations.suitability: Studios are booked through a named contact per facility; the campus also offers production services, catering, event spaces and office facilities.
locations.logistics: 32,000 m2 campus in the Tohloppi district of Tampere where 1,000 to 1,100 people work and study daily

locations.name: Melo Power Plant
locations.setting: A hydroelectric power plant in Nokia near Tampere offering both industrial interiors and surrounding nature for productions, listed by Film Tampere as a filming location.
locations.logistics: Located at Melontie 59, 37140 Nokia, about 20 km from Tampere's central square

locations.name: Nokia Museums (Hinttala)
locations.setting: A local history museum in the town of Nokia occupying a relocated worker's house, part of a small cluster of preserved 19th and 20th century industrial-era homes.

locations.name: Parking Garages by Finnpark
locations.setting: A network of multi storey car parks operated by Finnpark in and around central Tampere, listed by Film Tampere as available filming locations.
locations.logistics: Filming enquiries for the parking garages are directed to Finnpark's Marketing Chief (contact published on the Film Tampere location page).

locations.name: Pekilo Performance and Event Venue
locations.setting: A former animal-feed factory building beside the closed Mantta pulp mill, converted into an exhibition and event space with variable rooms and a ceiling rising to 12 metres.

locations.name: Pirkkala Old Church
locations.setting: A wooden church built in 1921 in Pirkkala, with an adjoining cemetery, a church boat and a bird observation tower on the grounds.

locations.name: Pispala Area
locations.setting: A protected hillside neighbourhood in Tampere of narrow streets and restored wooden houses between two lakes, home to Rajaportti, the oldest public sauna in Finland.

locations.name: Pitkäniemi Hospital Area
locations.setting: Former psychiatric hospital on a lakeshore park in Nokia near Tampere, with stone buildings from the 1890s including an Italianate villa, in clinical use from 1900 until closure in 2024 and now largely vacant.
locations.facilities: Historical stone hospital buildings completed in 1894-1895 in parkland on the shore of Lake Pyhäjärvi, part of Tampere University Hospital. The former chief's residence ('the Castle') has Italian Renaissance-style columned terraces and now houses the Pitkäniemi Hospital Museum.
locations.logistics: 12.5 km from Tampere Central Square.

locations.name: Sarkanniemi Amusement Park
locations.setting: A lakeside amusement park in central Tampere combining rides, an aquarium, a planetarium, a children's zoo and the Nasinneula observation tower.

locations.name: Senate Square
locations.setting: Neoclassical square by Carl Ludvig Engel framed by Helsinki Cathedral, the Government Palace and the university, long used as a stand-in for imperial St Petersburg and Soviet-era Moscow.

locations.name: Sibelius Hall
locations.setting: A wooden concert hall on the shore of Lake Vesijarvi in Lahti, with a main hall, several conference rooms and a live music club, offering full event production and streaming services.
locations.facilities: Main hall (Paasali), Metsahalli, Puusepan Sali, conference rooms, restaurants and the Finlandia-klubi live music venue
locations.logistics: Located at Ankkurikatu 7, Lahti

locations.name: Stable Yards (Tallipiha)
locations.setting: A 19th century stable courtyard from the Finlayson factory community in Tampere, restored with Russian style cottages that now house craft shops and a cafe, listed by Film Tampere as a filming location.
locations.logistics: Located at Kuninkaankatu 4, about 0.7 km from Tampere's central square

locations.name: Suomenlinna
locations.setting: Sea fortress built from 1748 across a cluster of islands off Helsinki, with stone bastions, tunnels, dry docks and cobbled courtyards, now a UNESCO World Heritage site with museums and open parkland.
locations.logistics: Official site publishes separate instructions for filming and photography and a dedicated contact for bookings.

locations.name: Suvilahti
locations.setting: Former power plant and gasworks complex in Helsinki with red-brick industrial halls and open concrete yards, now a cultural venue mixing galleries, restaurants and a brewery inside the original industrial shells.
locations.facilities: Site explicitly offers outdoor and indoor space rental for events, festivals and photo shoots.
locations.logistics: Managed by Kiinteistö Oy Kaapelitalo; multiple independent tenants occupy separate buildings on the site.

locations.name: Tampere City Hall
locations.setting: A neo renaissance city hall from 1890 on Tampere's central square, with several period halls, listed by Film Tampere as a filming location.
locations.logistics: Located at Keskustori 10, at the edge of Tampere's central square

locations.name: Tampere Hall
locations.setting: Largest congress centre in the Nordic countries, a modern building beside Sorsapuisto park in central Tampere with a 1,756-seat main auditorium and several smaller halls used for concerts and conferences.

locations.name: Tampere Market Hall (Kauppahalli)
locations.setting: Largest market hall in the Nordic countries when it opened in 1901, a protected two-story brick building in central Tampere with roughly 30 food stalls, cafes and restaurants.
locations.facilities: 174 retail outlets, opened 1901; about 40 percent of outlets are cafes and restaurants (Film Tampere).
locations.logistics: Address Hameenkatu 19, 33200 Tampere; 0 km from the Central Square (Film Tampere).

locations.name: Tullikamari
locations.setting: A former customs warehouse in Tampere converted into a cultural venue with a large main hall and a smaller club space, used for concerts, theatre and festivals, listed by Film Tampere as a filming location.
locations.logistics: Located at Tullikamarin aukio 2, about 1 km from Tampere's central square

locations.name: Turku Castle
locations.setting: Medieval keep begun around 1280 at the mouth of the Aura river, expanded into a Renaissance bailey under Gustav Vasa in the 16th century, now a city museum with period rooms, banqueting halls and rentable event spaces.
locations.known_for: Sadan miekan mies (1951), The Girl King (2015)
locations.facilities: Rooms published for hire: Kuninkaan sali (King's Hall, up to 250), Linnan kirkko (Castle Church, up to 240), Kuningattaren sali (Queen's Hall, up to 180), Bryggman-sali (up to 120 for lectures, 80 for banquets), Eteläinen sali (Southern Hall, up to 100), Kuningattaren kamari (Queen's Chamber, up to 50), Herrainkellari (Gentlemen's Cellar, up to 30), plus courtyard areas.

photo.author: Markus Koljonen (Dilaudid) with thanks to Jontts and Turku Cathedral

locations.name: Vehoniemi Car Museum
locations.setting: A car museum on the Vehoniemi ridge near Kangasala, open since 1983, with a rotating display of vintage vehicles kept in running order.

locations.name: Viitaniemi Quarry
locations.setting: An open-pit feldspar quarry near Orivesi, worked from 1935 to 1965 for lithium-bearing feldspar, with gemstones still found among its waste rock piles.

locations.name: Abbaye aux Hommes
locations.setting: Former Benedictine abbey whose 18th century monastic buildings house the Caen city hall, with a stone staircase, panelled halls, cloister and church alongside.

photo.author: Croydon Art Collection, Gallery Oldham, Russell-Cotes Art Gallery & Museum et No

locations.name: Abbaye de Beauport
locations.setting: Ruined 13th century abbey on the shore near Paimpol with a roofless church, vaulted cellar, chapter house, refectory over the sea and salt marsh grounds.
locations.suitability: The abbey publishes a hire offer for meetings and seminars in its historic rooms.

locations.name: Abbaye de Daoulas
locations.setting: Romanesque abbey at Daoulas with a 12th century cloister, church, fountain and a walled medicinal plant garden on a sloping site.
locations.suitability: Run by Chemins du patrimoine en Finistere, which publishes a private hire offer covering its houses, abbeys and estates.

locations.name: Abbaye de Fontenay
locations.setting: Cistercian abbey founded in 1118 in a wooded valley, with a plain unlit church, cloister, dormitory, forge, bakehouse and gardens, and no modern building in view.
locations.known_for: Angelique marquise des anges, Cyrano de Bergerac, L'Enfant des loups, La Marquise des ombres

locations.name: Abbaye de Saint-Michel-en-Thierache
locations.setting: A Benedictine abbey founded in 945 in Saint-Michel-en-Thierache, rebuilt several times, with a 17th century baroque facade, a central cloister, an abbey church, a chapter house and a refectory.

locations.name: Abbaye du Mont-Saint-Michel
locations.setting: Abbey stacked on a tidal rock, with a Romanesque nave, Gothic cloister and refectory, crypts, undercrofts and a treadwheel, above the bay sands.
locations.price_note: Centre des monuments nationaux publishes a filming and photography rate card as a downloadable document
locations.suitability: Run by the Centre des monuments nationaux, with published filming and photography access and a separate private hire offer.

locations.name: Abbaye du Relec
locations.setting: Cistercian abbey in the Monts d'Arree with a plain 12th century church, ponds, mill and open moorland around the monastic buildings.
locations.suitability: Run by Chemins du patrimoine en Finistere, which publishes a private hire offer covering its houses, abbeys and estates.

locations.name: Abbaye Royale de Fontevraud
locations.setting: Former royal abbey near Chinon founded in 1101, with a Romanesque church, medieval kitchens and cloisters plus an on-site hotel, its own site publishing information for film and TV shoots.
locations.suitability: The abbey has hosted film, documentary and music video shoots since the 1940s; interior and exterior spaces (cloisters, churches, gardens) are described as suited to crews of any size (own site).
locations.logistics: Truck access to on-site parking, dressing rooms, on-site accommodation and catering, and electrical connections (own site).

locations.name: Accor Arena
locations.setting: Multi-purpose indoor arena in Bercy seating up to about 20,300, built into a grass-covered pyramid, used for concerts, sport and large events.

locations.name: Aeroport Paris-Charles de Gaulle
locations.setting: France's main international airport north of Paris, with terminals, control-tower views and airside areas that operator Groupe ADP makes available for filming through a dedicated production service.

locations.name: Aitre Saint-Maclou
locations.setting: Enclosed timber framed plague cemetery courtyard of the 16th century in Rouen, with carved galleries of skulls and tools, an inner yard and adjoining rooms.
locations.suitability: The site is owned by the city of Rouen, which runs a filming service and issues shooting authorisations for municipal locations free of charge.

locations.name: Alignements de Carnac
locations.setting: Neolithic standing stone rows spread over several kilometres of heath and pasture at Carnac, with long straight alignments, enclosures and open sky.
locations.price_note: Centre des monuments nationaux publishes a filming and photography rate card as a downloadable document
locations.suitability: Run by the Centre des monuments nationaux, which publishes a filming and photography page for the alignments.

locations.name: Allianz Riviera
locations.setting: Nice football stadium with a translucent wave-shaped roof, home to OGC Nice and used for concerts and other large events.

locations.name: Aquaboulevard
locations.setting: Indoor and outdoor water park in the 15th arrondissement, with wave pools, slides and tropical-style planting, hired through its own professional booking service for shoots and events.

locations.name: Arenes de Nimes
locations.setting: Roman amphitheatre built around 100 AD in the centre of Nimes, seating up to 24,000 for its own ferias and concerts, with a covered arena floor usable for filming outside the events calendar.

locations.name: Ateliers des Capucins
locations.setting: Former naval machine shops above the Penfeld converted into a covered public plateau, with cast iron columns, overhead cranes, preserved machinery and a glazed roof.
