locations.suitability: The site publishes a private hire offer for seminars, conventions and receptions across its spaces, with catering on site.

locations.name: Base sous-marine de Saint-Nazaire (La Base)
locations.setting: Reinforced-concrete U-boat pens built by the German navy in WWII on the Saint-Nazaire docks, now holding exhibition halls, a climbing wall and a rooftop garden.

locations.name: Bassins de Lumières
locations.setting: Former WWII submarine pens on the Bordeaux docks converted into a digital art centre, with four raw concrete basins used for large-scale wall and floor projections.
locations.facilities: Two indoor spaces: the Citerne (155 sqm, 360-degree projection) and the Cube (220 sqm, soundproofed), plus elevated walkways and tiered seating. Overall capacity ranges from 50 to 900 for a cocktail reception or 50 to 700 for a seated dinner.
locations.suitability: The venue lists professional events as one of five event categories it hosts, alongside cocktails, seated dinners, and private visits.

locations.name: Bibliothèque nationale de France, site Richelieu
locations.setting: Historic national library building in central Paris with a 19th-century domed reading room and ornate galleries, reopened after a long restoration.
locations.facilities: At the Richelieu site, the Salle Ovale seats up to 220 for a dinner or holds up to 300 for a cocktail reception. Other hireable spaces are the Hall Vivienne, the Vivienne garden, and the Salon d'Honneur.
locations.suitability: Filming and photography require prior written authorization from BnF, covering the Richelieu, François-Mitterrand, Arsenal, Opéra and CTBnF sites; an exception applies only to images made for strictly private, non-commercial use.
locations.logistics: Richelieu site spaces can be hired from 6pm Wednesday to Sunday, and all day on Monday when the site is closed to the public.

locations.name: Bibliotheque nationale et universitaire de Strasbourg
locations.setting: Library of 1895 rebuilt inside in 2014: a stone entrance stair, a domed reading room, glazed floors around a central void and closed stacks, on place de la Republique.
locations.suitability: The library publishes hire of its spaces for outside events.

locations.name: Bourse de Commerce, Pinault Collection
locations.setting: Former 19th-century grain exchange with a circular rotunda and glass dome, renovated by Tadao Ando with an internal concrete cylinder as a contemporary art museum.
locations.facilities: Ground-floor Salon and Passage (up to 800 for a cocktail reception or 220 for a seated dinner), Foyer on floor -1 (up to 300 for a cocktail reception), a semi-circular Auditorium (284 seats), the Petit Salon (up to 70 people), and the restaurant La Halle aux Grains (125 for a cocktail reception or 100 for a dinner).
locations.logistics: Private events run Monday to Thursday from 8:30-10:30am and from 7:30pm, and from 7pm on Tuesdays when the museum is closed to the public.

locations.name: Cap Sciences
locations.setting: Science centre inside Hangar 20, a former dockside cargo warehouse on the Garonne in Bordeaux, keeping the hangar's steel roof trusses over its exhibition floor, with halls listed to hire.
locations.facilities: 6 work spaces plus a terrace; kitchen equipment includes a service lift, large-capacity refrigerator, oven and washroom (own site).

locations.name: Casino Grand Cercle, Aix-les-Bains
locations.setting: Casino of 1849 in the spa town, with a mosaic domed gaming room, an Italian style theatre of about 900 seats and reception rooms that are hired out.
locations.suitability: Reception rooms are offered for hire on the site's own page.

locations.name: Centre Historique Minier (Lewarde Mining Centre)
locations.setting: Preserved coal mine museum in the former Delloye colliery, with pithead buildings, a headframe, underground galleries and workshops from the Nord-Pas-de-Calais coalfield.
locations.price_note: Meeting room hire from EUR 145 per half day (34-36 sqm rooms) up to EUR 1,000 per full day for the Auditorium Georges Delerue; technical support is a mandatory extra at EUR 35 per hour (own site, 2026 rates)
locations.facilities: Salle Jules Mousseron (70 sqm), Salle Lucien Jonas (36 sqm) and Salle Albert Bouquillon (34 sqm) meeting rooms, plus the Auditorium Georges Delerue (200 seats: 175 armchairs with a writing tablet, 22 folding seats and 3 wheelchair spaces, with a 45 sqm stage, a 4x3m screen and an audio system). Wheelchair accessible by lift.

locations.name: Centre Pompidou-Metz
locations.setting: Museum of 2010 under a woven timber roof, with three tubular galleries stacked over a tall glazed forum and terraces facing the railway station quarter.
locations.suitability: The museum publishes privatisation of its spaces.

locations.name: Chamonix-Mont-Blanc
locations.setting: Alpine resort town below Mont Blanc with cable cars up to the Aiguille du Midi and nearby glaciers, a base for mountaineering and skiing since the 19th century.

locations.name: Chartreuse de Neuville
locations.setting: A former Carthusian monastery near Montreuil-sur-Mer, restored around cloistered gardens, run by an association that rents out its halls for events alongside its heritage and cultural programme.

locations.name: Chateau d'Angers
locations.setting: Ducal fortress with seventeen dark schist and limestone towers, a curtain wall walk above the Maine, chapel, royal lodging and terraced gardens in the moat.
locations.price_note: Centre des monuments nationaux publishes a filming and photography rate card as a downloadable document
locations.suitability: Run by the Centre des monuments nationaux, with published filming and photography access and a separate private hire offer.

locations.name: Chateau d'Azay-le-Rideau
locations.setting: Early Renaissance chateau standing on an island in the Indre, with a straight flight staircase, furnished rooms and a landscaped park with water reflections.
locations.price_note: Centre des monuments nationaux publishes a filming and photography rate card as a downloadable document
locations.suitability: Run by the Centre des monuments nationaux, which accepts films, series, documentaries, commercials and photography and handles requests through a named coordinator.

locations.name: Château d'If
locations.setting: 16th-century island fortress off Marseille used as a state prison into the 19th century, the setting of The Count of Monte Cristo and a location in The French Connection.
locations.facilities: 1,547 sqm of castle interior with several small rooms, 600 sqm of terraces, and a 1,700 sqm parade ground. The castle interior and terraces each hold up to 100 people standing; the parade ground holds up to 500 standing.
locations.suitability: Both interior and exterior filming are offered year-round, for films, series, documentaries and advertisements.

locations.name: Chateau de Bouges
locations.setting: Compact 18th century country house with intact period furnishing, service quarters, stables and outbuildings, set in a park and kitchen garden in the Berry countryside.
locations.suitability: Run by the Centre des monuments nationaux, which publishes a filming and photography page with a named contact for the site.

locations.name: Chateau de Chenonceau
locations.setting: Chateau built across the river Cher on a bridge gallery, with vaulted 16th century kitchens, furnished galleries, two formal gardens and a farm.
locations.suitability: The chateau publishes a private hire offer for seminars and receptions in the galleries, orangery and gardens.

locations.name: Chateau de Cheverny
locations.setting: Symmetrical 17th century chateau still lived in by the same family, with fully furnished period rooms, formal gardens, kennels and a large park.
locations.suitability: The estate publishes a room hire offer covering the orangery and other spaces for private and corporate use.

locations.name: Chateau de Joux
locations.setting: Fortress rebuilt by Vauban on a rock above the Doubs gorge, with five walled enclosures, a keep, drawbridges, cells used as a state prison and a 120 m well.
locations.suitability: The site's news pages document filming at the fortress.

locations.name: Chateau de la Verrerie, Le Creusot
locations.setting: Former crystal works turned Schneider family seat, with two conical glass furnaces in the forecourt, workshops, a small theatre and the Creusot steelworks archive.

locations.name: Chateau de Valencay
locations.setting: Renaissance and classical chateau once owned by Talleyrand, with Empire and Restoration furnished rooms, large service kitchens and a wooded park.
locations.suitability: The chateau takes drama and documentary series, music videos, short and feature films and television programmes, with drone work subject to prior approval, and staff assist during recces and shoot days.

locations.name: Chateau de Villandry
locations.setting: Renaissance chateau known for its terraced formal gardens, with an ornamental kitchen garden, water garden, maze and 18th century interiors.
locations.suitability: The estate publishes an events and private hire offer covering the chateau rooms and the gardens.

locations.name: Chateau du Clos Luce
locations.setting: Brick and tufa manor house where Leonardo da Vinci lived, with period bedrooms, galleries, an underground passage and a 7 hectare park with a terrace over Amboise.
locations.suitability: The house says it suits historical films, documentaries and photo shoots and can alternate period interiors with neutral technical spaces; a communications manager handles filming requests.

locations.name: Chateau du Plessis-Bourre
locations.setting: Late 15th century moated chateau reached by a long stone bridge, with a drawbridge, painted coffered ceiling, guardroom and unaltered exterior.
locations.suitability: The chateau keeps a public filming page listing the productions shot on the site.

photo.author: The original uploader was NonNobis at French Wikipedia.

locations.name: Chateau l'Hospitalet
locations.setting: Wine estate on the La Clape massif near Narbonne, with vineyards, cellars, a hotel and restaurants around a courtyard, hosting its own annual jazz festival and grounds used for private events.

locations.name: Chateau La Coste
locations.setting: Organic vineyard estate near Aix-en-Provence with a sculpture trail and pavilions by architects including Tadao Ando and Renzo Piano, a hotel and restaurant, and grounds hired for weddings.

locations.name: Chateau Royal de Blois
locations.setting: Four wings in four architectural styles around one courtyard, with furnished apartments, painted wall decoration and a view over the Loire, owned and run by the city of Blois.
locations.known_for: Jeanne d'Arc (Luc Besson), La Princesse de Montpensier, Secrets d'Histoire, Des racines et des ailes
locations.suitability: Filming needs prior authorisation from the director and a filming agreement may be drawn up depending on the request.

locations.name: Chemin de Fer de la Baie de Somme
locations.setting: Heritage steam and diesel railway running along the Somme bay between Le Crotoy, Saint-Valery-sur-Somme and Cayeux, with period stations and rolling stock.
locations.price_note: Private train charter from EUR 2,200 including tax for the Belle Époque steam train (March to September) or EUR 2,500 including tax for the 4 Saisons diesel train (October to February), plus meals at EUR 43 per adult and EUR 20 per child under 12 (own site, 2026 rates)
locations.facilities: Two heritage trains available for private charter: Belle Époque (steam, seats up to 115) and 4 Saisons (diesel, seats up to 96). Neither train is wheelchair accessible or pet-friendly.
locations.logistics: Lunch charter departs Saint-Valery at 12:00 with a meal stop on the sea wall from 12:10 to 14:15, returning at 15:20. Dinner charter departs the Saint-Valery Canal depot at 19:00, returning around 23:00-23:20. Booking requires a signed quote and a EUR 1,000 deposit, with the balance due 15 days before by bank cheque; no refund for late arrival or no-show.

locations.name: Chemins de fer de la Corse
locations.setting: Metre gauge railway of about 232 km linking Ajaccio, Bastia and Calvi, with tunnels, the Vecchio viaduct, small country halts, depots and railcars.

locations.name: Ciclic Animation
locations.setting: Animation studio and residency centre run by the regional film agency at Vendome, with shooting rooms for stop motion and drawn animation and post-production facilities.
locations.suitability: Operated by Ciclic Centre-Val de Loire, the regional agency that also runs the location and filming service for the region.

locations.name: Cinematheque de Toulouse
locations.setting: Film archive near the Saint-Cyprien quarter with two cinemas, a projection booth kept with 35 mm equipment, a reading room, film vaults and a brick courtyard.

locations.name: Circuit de Nevers Magny-Cours
locations.setting: Grand prix circuit with 4.4 km of track, pit lane and garages, grandstands, a control tower and open paddock space, hired by the day for track and vehicle work.

locations.name: Circuit des 24 Heures du Mans
locations.setting: Motor racing circuit combining a permanent track with closed public roads, pit lane and garages, grandstands, control tower and a museum on the same site.
locations.suitability: The Automobile Club de l'Ouest publishes a hire offer for seminars and events using the pit building, grandstands and track areas.

locations.name: Citadelle de Calvi
locations.setting: Genoese citadel on a rock above the harbour, with ramparts, bastions, a governors palace, narrow lanes inside the walls and views over the bay and the Balagne.

locations.name: Cite de Carcassonne
locations.setting: Double walled medieval town with 52 towers, a castle keep, lists between the ramparts and cobbled lanes, managed by the Centre des monuments nationaux.

locations.name: Cite de l'Automobile
locations.setting: Mulhouse car museum built around the Schlumpf brothers' collection, with several hundred vehicles under one roof lit by rows of replica cast-iron lamp posts, its site publishing venue-hire terms.
locations.facilities: Multiple hire spaces published: Espace Chefs-d'oeuvre 3,500 sqm; Salon Monaco 370 sqm (screen, speakers, wifi, video projector); Espace Course automobile 1,500 sqm; L'Espace Aventure automobile 9,500 sqm; L'Autodrome 270 sqm plus parking for up to 30 vehicles; Le Garage 425 sqm (own site).

locations.name: Cite de l'Espace
locations.setting: Space-themed science centre on the eastern edge of Toulouse, with a full-size Ariane rocket outdoors, planetarium domes and simulator halls, hired out for seminars and corporate events.

locations.name: Cite de la Mer
locations.setting: Maritime museum inside Cherbourg's 1933 Art Deco former transatlantic liner terminal, keeping the original departure hall, with a decommissioned submarine on display and dockside harbour views.
locations.suitability: The venue's events page lists tournage (filming) among the event types it hosts, alongside congress, seminar, exhibition, dinner, cocktail, show, private visit and ceremony (own site).

locations.name: Cité de la Mode et du Design
locations.setting: Former riverside customs warehouse on the Seine reclad in a green glass and steel skin, housing a design school, offices, a club and event floors over the water.

locations.name: Cité de la Voile Éric Tabarly (Keroman submarine base)
locations.setting: WWII U-boat pens on the Keroman peninsula in Lorient with roofs up to 7.5 metres thick, now holding a sailing museum, boatyards and a marina business park.
locations.facilities: Named spaces include the Auditorium, Karré Affaires (modular cocktail/reception space), two equipped meeting rooms, a permanent exhibition space, and Hall Pen Duick (modular for conferences, cocktails and exhibitions). Overall capacity ranges from 20 to 380 people. Equipped with tables, chairs, flipcharts, video projectors, UHD screens, sound systems, microphones and wifi.
locations.logistics: In Lorient, Brittany; about 3 hours from Paris by train, with Lorient station 10 minutes away. Pricing is by quotation only.

locations.name: Cité des Sciences et de l'Industrie
locations.setting: Large science museum in the Parc de la Villette built inside a converted 1960s abattoir hall, with the geodesic dome cinema La Géode standing alongside it.
locations.suitability: The site's commercial filming page groups available locations into interior exhibitions (Planetarium, Aquarium, Argonaute submarine), architecture (including the congress centre), behind-the-scenes areas (car parks, escalators, corridors, lifts) and exterior areas (moat, park), described as available by day and night. Past clients cited include TPS, Canal+, Yves Rocher and France Telecom (own site).

locations.name: Cité du Cinéma (Studios de Paris)
locations.setting: Studio campus in a converted riverside power station with sound stages, workshops and offices around a monumental glass-roofed nave.
locations.known_for: Lucy, Valerian and the City of a Thousand Planets
locations.facilities: Nine sound stages from 6,506 to 22,271 sq ft (largest Stage 5, 201 x 111 ft, about 2,070 m2) with 47 to 52.5 ft to the grid; offices, artist green rooms with hair and makeup, VIP green rooms, workshops and storage.
locations.suitability: Stages offered with adjoining offices, green rooms, workshops and storage inside the Cite du Cinema campus; the site keeps a list of productions shot there.
locations.logistics: 20 rue Ampere, Saint-Denis: 30 minutes from Charles de Gaulle airport, 20 minutes from Le Bourget, 30 to 40 minutes from central Paris; served by RER D and metro lines 13 and 14 (direct to Orly), A86 and A1 motorway access, two four-star hotels a five-minute walk away.

locations.name: Cite du design, Saint-Etienne
locations.setting: Design school and exhibition site in the former national arms factory, mixing 19th century workshop rows and a parade ground with a 200 m perforated aluminium hall.

locations.name: Cite du Livre
locations.setting: Former match factory in Aix-en-Provence, converted into a library and performance complex that keeps its industrial brick shell and a large auditorium used by the Festival d'Aix.

locations.name: Cite du Train
locations.setting: One of the world's largest railway museums, in Mulhouse, with locomotives and carriages under a long-span roof and a reconstructed period station platform, published as available for hire and filming.
locations.facilities: Two covered halls of 6,000 sqm and 13,000 sqm plus 16,000 sqm of outdoor space; named filming locations include station platforms, a turntable and a signal box (own site).
locations.suitability: Site publishes a filming/shooting page offering a technical site survey, a custom quote, on-site assistance during filming, and support with procedures via the Mulhouse Alsace Agglomeration film office. Past productions cited include Arte, France Televisions and SWR/ARD (own site).

locations.name: Cité Frugès
locations.setting: Estate of concrete houses built by Le Corbusier and Pierre Jeanneret in Pessac in 1926 in flat-roofed cubic and terraced forms, UNESCO-listed since 2016.

locations.name: Cite internationale de la gastronomie et du vin, Dijon
locations.setting: Dijon's former general hospital converted in 2022 into a food and wine campus, mixing 18th century wards, a chapel and courtyards with new brick and glass wings.

locations.name: Cité Internationale Universitaire de Paris
locations.setting: Campus of more than 40 national residence halls in varied architectural styles on the southern edge of Paris, housing international students since the 1920s.
locations.facilities: 34-hectare campus with 47 architecturally varied buildings dating from 1925 onward, offered for professional events as well as filming; parking for trucks and production equipment is positioned close to the sets, with a dedicated on-site team supporting productions.
locations.suitability: Described by CIUP as France's first multi-set filming location, with both interior settings (art deco lounges, halls, corridors, staircases, offices) and exterior settings (building facades, landscaped grounds). States that no prefectural authorization is required to film there; more than 500 productions have shot there in 10 years.

locations.name: Cite Plantagenet, Le Mans
locations.setting: Walled old town of Le Mans with Gallo-Roman ramparts, cobbled lanes, timber framed and Renaissance houses, staircases and a cathedral close.
locations.suitability: The city of Le Mans runs a filming service page for productions wanting to shoot in the old town and other municipal locations.

locations.name: Cité Radieuse, Marseille
locations.setting: Le Corbusier's 1952 concrete apartment block on stilts in Marseille, with 337 duplex units, an internal shopping street and a rooftop terrace.

locations.name: Couvent du Pouy
locations.setting: A 19th century convent on the edge of Dax, empty for over a decade, with a chapel, cloister galleries around a courtyard garden, and rooms and offices on three floors, listed by the regional film commission.

locations.name: Couvent Sainte-Marie de La Tourette
locations.setting: Dominican priory finished by Le Corbusier in 1960 on a slope near Lyon, with raw concrete cells on pilotis, a bare church, ramped cloisters and coloured light wells.

locations.name: Domaine national de Chambord
locations.setting: Renaissance royal chateau with a double helix staircase, terraced roofscape and open state rooms, set in a walled estate of 5,440 hectares of forest, meadow and canals.
locations.suitability: The estate states it takes feature, documentary and television shoots across the chateau and the enclosed park; requests go through the communication team.

locations.name: Domaine Pommery
locations.setting: Champagne house on 18 km of Gallo-Roman chalk pits about 30 m down, reached by a long stair, with carved galleries, bottle stacks and Elizabethan style buildings above ground.

locations.name: Ecluses de Fonseranes
locations.setting: Staircase lock of 1697 on the Canal du Midi at Beziers, about 300 m long with a drop of 21 m, stone chambers, towpaths and a lock keepers house.

locations.name: Écomusée Creusot Montceau
locations.setting: Industrial heritage network around the former Schneider steelworks in Le Creusot, with the Château de la Verrerie glassworks-turned-mansion as its main site.

locations.name: Ecomusee d'Alsace
locations.setting: Open air museum built from about seventy relocated Alsatian farmhouses, with lanes, a chapel, workshops, a mill and farmyards that together read as a complete pre-industrial village.
locations.suitability: The museum describes its buildings and grounds as privatisable outside opening hours.

locations.name: Ecomusee de Saint-Nazaire
locations.setting: Municipal museum on the old harbour covering shipbuilding, the port and the wartime destruction of the town, with displays, archive material and quayside views.
locations.suitability: The Saint-Nazaire tourist board, which runs the site, publishes a press and filming contact for reports, interviews and shoots.

locations.name: Entrepot Beraud-Sudreau
locations.setting: A 10,000 square metre former warehouse in Brive-la-Gaillarde, split into two halls of 6,000 and 4,000 square metres with 200 square metres of offices, listed by the regional film commission.
locations.facilities: Two buildings of 6,000 and 4,000 square metres including 200 square metres of offices

locations.name: Escal'Atlantic
locations.setting: Museum inside a block of the Saint-Nazaire submarine base that reconstructs the interiors of a transatlantic liner, with cabins, engine room, saloons and deck sets.
locations.suitability: The Saint-Nazaire tourist board, which runs the site, publishes a press and filming contact for reports, interviews and shoots.

photo.author: SS_Normandie_at_sea_view.JPG: *SS_Normandie_at_sea.jpg: Vick the Viking derivative work: Altair78 (talk) derivative work

locations.name: Escat
locations.setting: A former tobacco-processing plant in Bergerac with five buildings totalling 42,000 square metres, offered by the regional film commission for productions needing large industrial floor space.
locations.facilities: Five buildings of 20,000, 5,500, 5,500, 5,500 and 5,500 square metres

locations.name: Étretat Cliffs
locations.setting: White chalk cliffs with natural arches and a freestanding needle rising above a pebble beach on the Alabaster Coast.

locations.name: Faculte de medecine de Montpellier
locations.setting: Medical school founded in 1220 and housed in a former bishops palace, with a stone staircase, portrait galleries, a lecture theatre and an anatomy museum.
locations.suitability: The faculty publishes hire of its rooms.

locations.name: Familistere de Guise
locations.setting: A 19th century workers' housing complex in Guise built by industrialist Jean-Baptiste Godin, with glazed courtyards and communal apartment wings, now a museum that also hosts corporate events.

locations.name: Fort de la Bastille, Grenoble
locations.setting: Hill fort above Grenoble reached by the bubble cable car of 1934, with casemates, stair tunnels, terraces over the Isere and rooms inside the ramparts.
locations.suitability: Rooms in the fort are let out, listed on the site's hire page.

locations.name: Fort de Mutzig
locations.setting: German fortress begun in 1893 and spread over 254 hectares west of Strasbourg, with armoured turrets, concrete galleries, barrack rooms, a machine hall and an underground infirmary.

locations.name: Fort la Latte
locations.setting: Coastal fortress on a rock spur near Cap Frehel, reached by two drawbridges, with a round keep, curtain walls, a cannonball oven and cliff exteriors.
locations.known_for: The Vikings (1958), Les Trois Mousquetaires (1948), Le Parfum de la dame en noir (1931), L'Epervier

locations.name: Forteresse Royale de Chinon
locations.setting: Medieval hilltop fortress above the Vienne with curtain walls, three baileys, towers and undercrofts, run by the Indre-et-Loire department.
locations.suitability: The fortress states it offers filming possibilities for features, documentaries and broadcast, with a separate contact for corporate space hire.

locations.name: France-Tabac
locations.setting: A former tobacco warehouse complex on the edge of Sarlat-la-Caneda, five buildings totalling 14,400 square metres, listed by the Perigord film office for set construction and large interiors.
locations.facilities: Five buildings of 6,235, 2,700, 2,160, 2,160 and 1,141 square metres

locations.name: Futuroscope
locations.setting: Multimedia theme park north of Poitiers built around futuristic pavilions and a lake, with cinema domes and landscaped outdoor sets, offering seminar and private event hire outside opening hours.

locations.name: Gare Saint Sauveur
locations.setting: Former goods yard of a 19th-century Lille railway station, now an exhibition and events venue keeping the open shed structure and platform-level halls of the original depot.

locations.name: Grand Aquarium de Saint-Malo
locations.setting: Aquarium on the edge of Saint-Malo with ring shaped tank rooms, a walk through tunnel, a submarine ride and dark technical corridors behind the displays.
locations.suitability: The aquarium publishes a private hire offer for groups and companies outside public opening hours.

locations.name: Grand Port Maritime de Marseille
locations.setting: France's largest port, with the working container terminals and warehouses of Marseille-Fos and the historic Joliette basin, with its own published filming-permit process for productions.
locations.suitability: Filming within the port (Marseille or Fos-sur-Mer basins) requires an authorization convention; drone footage needs a separate authorization from the Harbormaster; filming at facilities occupied by port-based companies needs that company's written permission (own site).
locations.logistics: Applications should allow about 3 weeks after the file is processed; required documents include a KBIS (less than 3 months old), bank details, authorised signatory details, an on-site contact name, an insurance certificate covering the filming dates and a VAT number (own site).

locations.name: Grande Saline de Salins-les-Bains
locations.setting: Salt works with a 13th century vaulted underground gallery, brine pumps still in place and a 165 m evaporation hall, in a small spa town below wooded slopes.

locations.name: Gratte-Ciel de Villeurbanne
locations.setting: Municipal high rise district of 1934: two rows of stepped brick and concrete housing blocks along a straight avenue, closed by the town hall belfry and the TNP theatre.
locations.suitability: The city publishes the procedure for holding an event in its outdoor public spaces.

locations.name: Halle aux Toiles
locations.setting: Municipal hall in central Rouen used for fairs, concerts and exhibitions, with a large clear span room, gallery level and street frontage near the old market.
locations.price_note: Rouen issues filming authorisations free of charge; filming on public streets and in public buildings is free except in special cases (city site)
locations.suitability: The city of Rouen runs a filming service: requests need a letter, an authorisation form, a schedule, a synopsis and an insurance certificate, with about 15 working days notice.

locations.name: Halle de La Machine
locations.setting: Large hangar on the former Montaudran airfield holding street theatre machines, with a wide clear span hall, workshops and the old runway strip outside.
locations.suitability: The hall is offered for privatisation on the site's own page.

locations.name: Halle Tony Garnier
locations.setting: A vast steel-framed former livestock market hall of 1864 in central Lyon, converted into the city's largest standing-capacity venue for concerts, trade fairs and exhibitions.

locations.name: Halle Tropisme
locations.setting: Former army vehicle workshop of about 4,000 m2 in Montpellier turned into a cultural venue, with steel trusses, concrete floors, studios, a bar and a courtyard.
locations.suitability: The venue publishes privatisation of its spaces.

locations.name: Haras National de Lamballe
locations.setting: State stud farm founded in 1825 in a former army barracks in Lamballe, with stone stable blocks around a courtyard and a riding arena, its own site listing hire for weddings and seminars.

locations.name: Haras National du Pin
locations.setting: France's oldest national stud, an 18th-century complex of stables around a formal chateau-style courtyard in the Orne countryside, with an equestrian arena and grounds listed for seminar hire.

locations.name: Hôpital Bicêtre
locations.setting: Large hospital complex south of Paris with historic pavilions and a tall water reservoir building, listed by AP-HP among the sites it regularly opens to film crews.
locations.suitability: All filming at AP-HP hospitals is subject to prior authorization; arrangements must respect the image rights of patients, staff and visitors as well as hospital regulations. Filming gives rise to a fee for occupying public domain space, based on an internal AP-HP tariff scale that is not published online.

locations.name: Hopital Edouard Herriot
locations.setting: Pavilion hospital designed by Tony Garnier and opened in 1933, with brick and concrete blocks, glazed link corridors and tree lined internal streets inside the walls.

locations.name: Hôpital Maritime de Berck
locations.setting: Seafront AP-HP hospital in Berck-sur-Mer built as a 19th-century marine sanatorium, named on the AP-HP's list of hospitals that regularly welcome film shoots.
locations.suitability: All filming at AP-HP hospitals is subject to prior authorization; arrangements must respect the image rights of patients, staff and visitors as well as hospital regulations. Filming gives rise to a fee for occupying public domain space, based on an internal AP-HP tariff scale that is not published online.

locations.name: Hôpital Raymond-Poincaré
locations.setting: Rehabilitation hospital in Garches with early 20th-century pavilion wards and gardens, one of the AP-HP sites named as regularly opened for commercial filming.
locations.suitability: All filming at AP-HP hospitals is subject to prior authorization; arrangements must respect the image rights of patients, staff and visitors as well as hospital regulations. Filming gives rise to a fee for occupying public domain space, based on an internal AP-HP tariff scale that is not published online.

locations.name: Hopital Saint-Cyr
locations.setting: A 19th century hospital in central Villeneuve-sur-Lot, in use until 2015, with a neoclassical arcaded facade, a painted chapel, a former apothecary and wards over three floors around a wooded park.
locations.facilities: Large lorry-accessible car park, water and electricity available on site

locations.name: Hôpital Saint-Louis
locations.setting: Working Paris hospital built around an early 17th-century brick and stone quadrilateral courtyard, one of the AP-HP sites named as regularly hosting commercial filming.
locations.suitability: All filming at AP-HP hospitals is subject to prior authorization; arrangements must respect the image rights of patients, staff and visitors as well as hospital regulations. Filming gives rise to a fee for occupying public domain space, based on an internal AP-HP tariff scale that is not published online.

locations.name: Hospices de Beaune (Hotel-Dieu)
locations.setting: Charity hospital of 1443 with a glazed tile roof, the Room of the Poor and its curtained beds, a kitchen, pharmacy, chapel and paved timber galleried courtyard.

locations.name: Hotel Barriere L'Hermitage La Baule
locations.setting: Anglo-Norman seafront hotel of 1926 on the bay of La Baule, with a long facade, formal lounges, ballroom, spa and direct access to the beach.
locations.suitability: The hotel publishes a hire offer for seminars and private events covering its meeting rooms and reception spaces.

locations.name: Hotel Barriere Le Royal Deauville
locations.setting: Grand resort hotel of 1913 near the Deauville boardwalk, with a symmetrical facade, marble lobby, ballroom, restaurants and sea facing rooms.
locations.suitability: The hotel publishes a hire offer for seminars and private events covering its meeting rooms and reception spaces.

locations.name: Hotel Royal, Evian Resort
locations.setting: Palace hotel of 1909 on a hill above Lake Geneva, with painted salons, a long terrace, a ballroom, spa floors and grounds shared with a golf course.

locations.name: Hotel-Dieu Saint-Jacques, Toulouse
locations.setting: Former pilgrim hospital on the Garonne, built in brick with long vaulted wards, a chapel, a cloistered court and a river frontage, now offices and a medical museum.
locations.suitability: The hospital publishes hire of rooms for events.

locations.name: Institut Lumière
locations.setting: Museum in the former Lumière family home in Lyon, dedicated to Auguste and Louis Lumière and the birth of cinema, close to the site of their original factory.
locations.facilities: Hangar du Premier-Film: 300 sqm, seats 220 for a dinner or 300 for a cocktail reception, plus an adjoining cinema seating 269 (with 8 wheelchair spaces), 3 plasma screens, 2 x 35mm projectors and 1 digital projector. Jardin d'Hiver at Villa Lumière: 60 sqm, 35 seated or 70 for a cocktail reception. Villa Lumière also has two screening rooms in the basement.
locations.logistics: 25 rue du Premier-Film, Lyon 8e; 6 minutes from Bellecour, 15 minutes from Part-Dieu station, and next to the Monplaisir-Lumière stop on metro line D. Free public parking with 54 spaces beside the Hangar.

locations.name: InterContinental Lyon - Hotel Dieu
locations.setting: Hotel inside Lyon's former 18th century hospital, with a 32 m domed hall, long vaulted corridors, a chapel, inner courtyards and a river facade on the Rhone.

locations.name: L'Aventure Michelin
locations.setting: Michelin's visitor site in a former factory building at Cataroux in Clermont-Ferrand, with exhibition halls, period machinery, tyre making displays and industrial yards.

locations.name: La Cite du Vin
locations.setting: Twisting glass and aluminium tower on Bordeaux's Garonne quays, built around a wine museum and a top-floor tasting room, with function spaces used for private events and film screenings.

locations.name: La Cite, Nantes Events Center
locations.setting: City congress centre with three auditoriums, wide foyers, glazed galleries and exhibition halls, used for conferences, concerts and trade events.
locations.suitability: The centre publishes a hire offer for congresses, trade shows and corporate events across its halls and auditoriums.

locations.name: La Comedie de Clermont-Ferrand
locations.setting: Theatre opened in 2020 inside the 1950s bus and rail station, keeping the long concrete canopy and adding two auditoriums, foyers, rehearsal rooms and workshops.

locations.name: La Condition Publique
locations.setting: Former municipal wool-conditioning warehouse in Roubaix, a long glass-roofed 19th-century industrial hall now run as a cultural and event venue.
locations.facilities: More than 10,000 sqm across named spaces: Rue couverte, Verrière, Halle A, B and C, Plateau Coucke et Labos, Le Club, L'Alim, and Les Toits Terrasses. Overall capacity ranges from 10 to 5,000 people.
locations.suitability: Filming ("tournages") is listed among the event types the venue hosts, alongside meetings, conferences, evening events, corporate seminars, fashion shows and team-building.

locations.name: La Défense
locations.setting: Purpose-built business district west of Paris with high-rise office towers, an elevated pedestrian esplanade and the Grande Arche at its western end.

locations.name: La Friche la Belle de Mai
locations.setting: Former SEITA tobacco factory in Marseille converted into a multi-storey arts complex, with raw concrete floors, a rooftop garden and a skatepark, hired out through its own privatisation service.
locations.facilities: Accommodates 10 to 4,000 people; La Cartonnerie is a 2,500 sqm modular space; the roof terrace is 8,000 sqm with views over Marseille; meeting rooms hold 10 to 150 people; Place des Horizons is a modular covered plaza (own site).

locations.name: La Piscine, Musee d'Art et d'Industrie Andre Diligent
locations.setting: 1932 Art Deco municipal swimming pool in Roubaix converted into a museum, keeping its tiled pool basin, stained glass and rows of former changing cubicles as exhibition space.

locations.name: La Sucriere
locations.setting: Former sugar warehouse on the Confluence docks in Lyon, a long brick and concrete shed on the Saone quayside, now an exhibition and events venue run by a professional events operator.
locations.facilities: 5,100 sqm covered in total, including 3,800 sqm of event space and 1,700 sqm of exhibition space; 5 balcony terraces overlooking the Saone; capacity up to 1,500 seated, 4,000 for a cocktail reception or 1,000 for a conference; riverside privatisation is also possible (own site).
locations.logistics: Accessible by tram T1/T2 to Hotel de Region Montrochet and by bus S1; parking available at the nearby Confluence shopping centre and surrounding paid spaces (own site).

locations.name: Lagora
locations.setting: A disused 10,000 square metre leisure and commercial complex in Angouleme, split across three buildings and listed by the regional film commission for large-scale sets.
locations.facilities: Three buildings of 3,650, 2,411 and 1,552 square metres

locations.name: Le 104 (Centquatre-Paris)
locations.setting: Former municipal funeral parlour in northern Paris with two vast glass-roofed halls, now an arts centre with studios and space hired for events and shoots.
locations.facilities: Nef Curial: 1,026 sqm plus 1,000 sqm of circulation space, seats 1,000 or holds 1,780 standing. Jardin: 420 sqm, 250 seated or 600 standing. Salle 400: 400 sqm, 395 seated or 740 standing. Salle 200: 300 sqm, 190 seated or 580 standing. Écuries: 2,000 sqm across one main hall and 8 sections, 180-800 seated depending on configuration or 1,500+ standing. Also two meeting rooms (20-40 seated), a workshop space (70 seated/95 standing) and a catering area (80 seated/150 standing). Loading dock and on-site parking available.
locations.suitability: Described as suitable for fashion shows, cocktails, trade fairs, dinners, sports events, conferences, seminars and performances.

locations.name: Le Bateau Feu
locations.setting: A 20th century national theatre in central Dunkirk with a large main stage and backstage artist workshops, named by the regional film commission among its exceptional filming locations.

locations.name: Le Fresnoy
locations.setting: A national contemporary art school in Tourcoing built inside a former early 20th century entertainment complex, with production studios under a large suspended roof and rentable spaces for private events.
locations.facilities: Production studios, a cinema, a restaurant, rooftop access, rooms available for private hire

locations.name: Le Grand Hotel Barriere Dinard
locations.setting: Late 19th century resort hotel above the Ecluse beach at Dinard, with a white rendered facade, sea facing lounges, bar, restaurant and meeting rooms.
locations.suitability: The hotel publishes a hire offer for seminars and private events covering its meeting rooms and reception spaces.

locations.name: Le Grand Hôtel Cabourg
locations.setting: Belle Époque seafront hotel in Cabourg that inspired Marcel Proust's Grand Hôtel de Balbec, with period public rooms overlooking the beach.

locations.name: Le Grand Rex
locations.setting: 1932 Art Deco single-screen cinema and concert hall on Boulevard Poissonniere, with a domed starlit auditorium seating over 2,700, hired out for premieres, shows and filming.
locations.facilities: Grande Salle seats 800 to 2,700; other spaces include Les Halls (800), Le Club (350), Rex Infinite (285), Rex 3 (238), Rex 5 (163), Rex 4 (122), Rex 7 (109) and Rex 6 (78); technical equipment includes projection, sound, microphones and internet access (own site).
locations.logistics: Address 1 Boulevard Poissonniere, 75002 Paris; nearest metro Bonne Nouvelle (own site).

locations.name: Le Silo
locations.setting: 1920s grain silo on Marseille's Arenc docks, gutted and rebuilt inside as a concert and conference hall while keeping its raw concrete exterior, hired for shows and corporate events.

locations.name: Le Train Bleu
locations.setting: Belle Époque restaurant inside Gare de Lyon station, listed as a historic monument since 1972, with gilded ceilings and large painted murals of French regions.
locations.known_for: La Femme Nikita (1990), Mr. Bean's Holiday (2007), Micmacs (2009), Place Vendôme (1998)

locations.name: Le Tripostal
locations.setting: Former postal sorting depot beside Lille-Flandres station, converted into a bare-shell exhibition hall with high ceilings and loading-bay access, hired for shows and events.

locations.name: Les Abattoirs, Musee - Frac Occitanie Toulouse
locations.setting: Former municipal slaughterhouse on the Garonne in Toulouse, converted into a contemporary art museum that keeps the original brick halls, steel roof trusses and a loading yard.
locations.price_note: Room hire published per space: Salle du Conseil EUR 1,000 (20 people); Auditorium EUR 3,000 (up to 199 seated); Hall d'Accueil EUR 3,000 (150 people, 180 sqm); Salle Picasso EUR 8,000 (150 people); La Nef EUR 8,000 to 32,000 depending on headcount; outdoor spaces (up to 2,000 people) on custom quote (own site).
locations.facilities: La Nef is 38 m long and 10 m wide with brick walls and high ceilings; Salle Picasso is 15 m by 12 m; the Auditorium stage is 10.8 m long and 3.8 m deep with 4 m under the ceiling; Hall d'Accueil is 180 sqm (own site).
locations.logistics: Security staffing is mandatory outside operating hours, at extra cost; all interior spaces are accessible to mobility-impaired visitors; no catering exclusivity and no corkage fee (own site).

locations.name: Les Deux Magots
locations.setting: Historic Saint-Germain-des-Prés cafe with a covered terrace and wood-panelled interior, a literary and artist meeting place since the late 19th century.

photo.author: Cheng-en Cheng from Taichung City, Taiwan

locations.name: Les Docks, Marseille
locations.setting: Row of 19th-century dockside warehouses on the Joliette waterfront, restored around an internal courtyard of offices, shops and restaurants.

locations.name: Les Fermes de Marie
locations.setting: Alpine hotel in Megève built from reassembled 18th and 19th-century farm buildings, with a spa and chalet-style interiors furnished in reclaimed wood.

locations.name: Les Frigos
locations.setting: Former refrigerated railway goods depot near the old Paris-Ivry station, now artist studios behind a graffiti-covered brick facade, with raw interiors and a covered yard in the 13th arrondissement.

locations.name: Les Halles de Lyon Paul Bocuse
locations.setting: Covered food market in Lyon with about fifty stalls of butchers, cheesemongers, bakers and small restaurants, named after chef Paul Bocuse.
locations.facilities: 8,000 sqm total, with two indoor terraces and one outdoor terrace. La Verrière (mezzanine) holds 50 to 300 for cocktails or seated dining; L'Espace Convivial (partial closure) holds 500 to 1,000; La Balade Gourmande (full privatisation of the market) holds 1,000 to 3,500. Wheelchair accessible, with nearby parking and EV charging.

locations.name: Les Machines de l'Ile
locations.setting: Former Dubigeon shipyard halls on the Ile de Nantes, with steel framed naves, gantries and workshops housing large mechanical animals and a carousel.
locations.suitability: The site publishes a private hire offer for companies covering the shipyard naves and the machine galleries.

locations.name: Les Studios de Saint-Menet
locations.setting: A former chocolate factory in Marseille's Saint-Menet district converted into roughly 30,000 square metres of sound stages, office space and three usable rooftop terraces across three buildings.
locations.facilities: A former chocolate factory offering close to 30,000 m2 of floor area over several levels: building A, the former production hall, 21,700 m2 over 4 levels; building D, the former administration block, 4,700 m2 usable as production offices; building E, a multi-purpose space of 3,000 m2. Ready-to-shoot sets, three fully practicable roof terraces and a green screen studio for effects work.
locations.suitability: Sound stages and office space for film and TV production
locations.logistics: Private parking for more than 200 vehicles on site.

locations.name: Les Subsistances
locations.setting: Former military supply depot on the Saone quays in Lyon, now a centre for performing-arts creation with rehearsal halls, a courtyard and studios, published as available to hire.
locations.facilities: La Verriere and La Boulangerie each take up to 2,000 people for a cocktail reception or 800 for a seated dinner (La Verriere available April to October only; the two can be combined); Le Hangar has 610 sqm total with a 300 sqm stage and fixed seating for 220 (up to 400 with extra chairs); La Terrasse holds 20 to 200 people; Les Plateaux is 130 sqm, seating 126 for a conference/show or about 20 for workshops; L'Accueil holds 30 for meetings or 50 for a cocktail (own site).

locations.name: Lycee Gaston Monnerville
locations.setting: A working vocational and general secondary school in Cahors, listed by the local film office as an available shooting location for productions needing classrooms and school corridors.

locations.name: Maison de George Sand
locations.setting: The writer's country house at Nohant with furnished 19th century rooms, a private theatre and puppet theatre, garden and farm buildings.
locations.known_for: Secrets d'Histoire, Une maison un ecrivain
locations.suitability: Run by the Centre des monuments nationaux, which publishes a filming and photography page with a named contact for the site.

locations.name: Manoir de Kernault
locations.setting: Late medieval Breton manor house at Mellac with a granite main building, a raised stone granary on pillars, farm buildings, orchards and a 30 hectare estate.
locations.suitability: Run by Chemins du patrimoine en Finistere, which publishes a private hire offer covering its houses, abbeys and estates.

locations.name: Marche International de Rungis
locations.setting: The world's largest wholesale food market, south of Paris, with vast refrigerated halls, loading docks and pre-dawn trading floors, offering event space and press filming through its own services team.
locations.suitability: Every filming request must go through a formal authorization process with the SEMMARIS communications department (own site).
locations.logistics: Requests must be submitted at least 3 days in advance, described as non-negotiable because market operators work staggered schedules; applicants must specify subject, format, needs, synopsis, broadcast date and equipment used (own site).

locations.name: Memorial de Caen
locations.setting: Museum of the Second World War built over a German command bunker, with a cleft stone facade, long exhibition galleries, an auditorium and gardens.
locations.suitability: The museum publishes a business hire offer covering its auditorium, meeting rooms and reception areas.

locations.name: Memorial de Verdun
locations.setting: Battlefield museum rebuilt in 2016 in concrete and glass, with dark galleries, a reconstructed battlefield floor, a roof terrace and the wooded ruins of Fleury outside.
locations.suitability: The museum publishes hire and privatisation of its rooms and auditorium.

locations.name: Mine temoin d'Ales
locations.setting: Training colliery on the edge of Ales with about 650 m of galleries, cutting machines, timber and steel props, a pithead yard and a lamp room.
locations.suitability: The site publishes hire of its rooms.

locations.name: Motoco
locations.setting: Former DMC textile hall in Mulhouse used as artist and maker studios, with long concrete bays, roof lights, freight doors and bare brick walls over several floors.
locations.suitability: Halls and rooms in the building are offered for hire on the site's room hire page.

locations.name: MuCEM
locations.setting: Marseille museum in a concrete cube wrapped in a black lattice screen, linked by a footbridge to the 13th-century Fort Saint-Jean at the harbour entrance.
locations.suitability: Accepts filming for documentaries, adverts, feature and short films, series, music videos and trailers, in Building J4 and Fort Saint-Jean (parade ground, courtyard, officers' gallery). Filming is possible on Tuesdays all day, other days by request; images of the J4 building are subject to copyright restrictions. MuCEM also hosts more than 100 corporate events a year, including filming, among seminars, conferences, team building and galas.

locations.name: Musee Aeroscopia
locations.setting: Aviation museum beside the Airbus plant at Blagnac, with Concorde, Super Guppy and A300 airframes under one hall of about 7,000 m2 and aircraft parked outside.
locations.suitability: The museum's site advertises filming and privatisation of the halls.

locations.name: Musee de l'Air et de l'Espace
locations.setting: Aerospace museum built around historic hangars at the edge of Paris-Le Bourget airport, with aircraft, open apron and runway views bookable through its own filming and photography service.
locations.suitability: Filming takes place only on Mondays, the museum's weekly closing day. Available spaces include the Boeing 747, the Concorde, WWII, Inter-War, Space and Helicopter halls, the control tower, the tarmac, the planetarium and terraces. Extra staffing, aircraft relocation, special technical work and copyright royalties are billed separately from the standard tariff (own site).

locations.name: Musee de la Corse, Corte
locations.setting: Regional museum inside the Corte citadel, joining old barrack buildings to a 1997 gallery, with fortress courtyards, ramparts and mountain views.

locations.name: Musee des Confluences
locations.setting: Steel and glass museum at the point where the Rhone meets the Saone, with a raised plinth, angular ramps, a tall crystal hall and dark windowless galleries.
locations.suitability: The museum publishes privatisation of its spaces.

locations.name: Musee des mines de fer de Lorraine, Neufchef
locations.setting: Iron ore museum set inside a real gallery, with about 1.5 km of tunnels, rail wagons, drilling and loading machines and lit ore faces at three periods of working.

locations.name: Musee des phares et balises
locations.setting: Lighthouse museum in the outbuildings of the Creac'h light on Ouessant, with optics, lamps, buoys and the black and white banded tower on the cliff outside.
locations.suitability: Run by Chemins du patrimoine en Finistere, which publishes a private hire offer covering its museums and sites.

locations.name: Oceanopolis
locations.setting: Ocean science centre in Brest marina with three climate pavilions, large viewing tanks, tunnels and technical back of house areas.
locations.suitability: The centre publishes an events and business hire offer covering its pavilions and meeting spaces.

locations.name: Omaha Beach
locations.setting: Stretch of Normandy coast where American forces landed on D-Day, 6 June 1944, backed by bluffs, the American Cemetery and the Overlord Museum.

photo.author: Chief Photographer's Mate (CPHoM) Robert F. Sargent

locations.name: Ouvrage du Hackenberg
locations.setting: Largest work of the Maginot Line, with about 10 km of underground galleries, an electric railway, a generator hall, kitchens, dormitories and gun blocks in raw concrete and steel.

locations.name: Palace of Versailles
locations.setting: Baroque royal palace with the Hall of Mirrors, state apartments, vast formal gardens and two smaller palaces in the park.
locations.suitability: The estate publishes a dedicated page for organising filming (tournage) on the Domaine de Versailles, alongside gala dinners, cocktails, concerts and private prestige visits; capacity and presentation of each space are said to be listed on a page per space (own site).

locations.name: Palais de justice de Nantes
locations.setting: Courthouse of 2000 by Jean Nouvel on the Loire quay, a black steel box with a tall glazed hall, red lined courtrooms and long corridors.

locations.name: Palais de Justice Historique de Lyon
locations.setting: 24-column neoclassical courthouse on the Saone in Vieux Lyon, its listed interior including a vast public hall, still used for hearings and available for filming by arrangement with the Cour d'appel.

locations.name: Palais des congres, Opera de Vichy
locations.setting: Art nouveau opera and congress building of 1901 in the spa quarter, with a gold and white auditorium, former casino rooms, glazed galleries and a park frontage.

locations.name: Palais des Festivals et des Congres
locations.setting: Cannes' seafront convention centre and home of the Cannes Film Festival, with cinema auditoriums, exhibition halls and the red-carpet staircase, hired for congresses and events year round.

locations.name: Palais Fesch, musee des beaux-arts
locations.setting: 19th century palace in central Ajaccio holding a large collection of Italian painting, with a courtyard, chapel, grand staircase and galleries over three floors.

locations.name: Palais Garnier
locations.setting: 19th-century opera house with a grand marble staircase, a gilded foyer and a ceiling painted by Chagall, home to the Paris Opera Ballet.
locations.facilities: Public areas hold up to 2,000 people for a cocktail reception; the Grand Foyer seats up to 700 for a gala dinner. Other hireable spaces include the Avant-Foyer, Rotonde des abonnés, Rotonde du glacier and Galerie Aline Foriel-Destezet.

locations.name: Palais Jacques-Coeur
locations.setting: Flamboyant Gothic merchant's palace in central Bourges with carved facades, a courtyard, chapel, galleries and vaulted service rooms.
locations.price_note: Centre des monuments nationaux publishes a filming and photography rate card as a downloadable document
locations.suitability: The whole palace is offered for films, series, documentaries, commercials and photography, available all year, with a named coordinator for bookings.

locations.name: Palais Lumiere, Evian-les-Bains
locations.setting: Former thermal baths of 1902 on the lakefront, now an exhibition centre and library, with a glazed hall, mosaics, ironwork, a colonnade and a terrace over Lake Geneva.

locations.name: Parc de Wesserling
locations.setting: Former royal textile works in a Vosges valley: 19th century spinning and weaving halls, a chimney, a chateau, workers housing and terraced gardens inside one site.

locations.name: Parc naturel regional de Briere
locations.setting: Regional park of marshland, reed beds and canals north of Saint-Nazaire, with thatched villages, flat bottomed punts, open water and long horizons.
locations.logistics: Managed by the Parc naturel regional syndicate, which covers 21 communes between Saint-Nazaire and the Vilaine.

locations.name: Parc naturel régional de Camargue
locations.setting: Rhône delta wetland reserve of lagoons, salt pans and marshland grazed by black bulls and white horses, managed as a regional nature park.

locations.name: Paris Expo Porte de Versailles
locations.setting: Paris's largest exhibition centre, eight halls totalling over 200,000 square metres beside the ring road, hired for trade shows, corporate events and filming through operator Viparis.

locations.name: Passage du Gois
locations.setting: A 4.1 kilometre tidal causeway to the island of Noirmoutier that is covered by the sea twice a day, with rescue poles, mudflats and no side barriers.
locations.logistics: The causeway is a departmental road managed by the Vendee department and is only passable around low tide.

locations.name: Passage Pommeraye
locations.setting: Covered shopping arcade of 1843 on three levels linked by a broad staircase, with statues, wooden shopfronts and a glazed roof over the walkway.
locations.suitability: The arcade has a documented history of film shoots, including newsreel coverage of a shoot in the passage in 1965.

photo.author: Statue: UnknownUnknown ; architects of the site: Jean-Baptiste Buron and Hippoly

locations.name: Phare de Cordouan
locations.setting: Working lighthouse on a rock at the mouth of the Gironde estuary, built from 1584 with a royal apartment and chapel inside, UNESCO-listed since 2021.

locations.name: Piscine Molitor
locations.setting: Art Deco outdoor and indoor swimming pool complex from 1929 in western Paris, restored as part of a hotel with the original tiled pools kept in use.
locations.facilities: Salons Longchamp & Auteuil and Salon Murat each hold up to 130 (theatre style); Salon Murat is 135 sqm and doubles as an urban art gallery. Le Solarium rooftop is 160 sqm, holds up to 130, and is open May to September only. Restaurant Molitor is 200 sqm for up to 150. Bar Bikini is 75 sqm for up to 50. Configurations offered: theatre, cabaret, U-shape, classroom, cocktail. Indoor and outdoor pools on site.

locations.name: Pôle Pixel
locations.setting: A creative-industries hub in Villeurbanne, near Lyon, combining a green screen studio and lighting stages with shared offices, co-working space and casting areas for film, animation and digital production.
locations.known_for: Studio 24, the site's original soundstage founded in 2002 by Roger Planchon, also hosts rehearsals for the Opéra de Lyon
locations.facilities: Studio 24: a modular soundproofed stage of 900 sqm; Lumière 1 and 2 (added 2009): combined shooting surface of over 2,000 sqm with 700 sqm of dressing rooms and offices; plus a green screen studio, lighting studios, projection rooms and rental offices from 10 to over 50 sqm across three buildings; co-working area; cafeteria; casting areas.
locations.logistics: Address: 24-26-36 rue Émile Decorps, 69100 Villeurbanne.

locations.name: Pont du Gard
locations.setting: Three tier Roman aqueduct bridge 49 m high over the Gardon, with dry stone arches, river banks, scrub covered slopes and no modern building in the frame.

locations.name: Pont Eiffel sur le Lot
locations.setting: A 19th century metal footbridge over the Lot river at Bouzies, on the riverside towpath through the gorge, listed as a filming location by the Lot department's film office.

locations.name: Pont-canal de Briare
locations.setting: A 662 metre steel navigable aqueduct of 1896 carrying a canal over the Loire, with lamp standards, towpaths and open water on both sides.
locations.logistics: Managed by Voies navigables de France, the public body responsible for the French waterway network.

locations.name: Prison Jacques-Cartier
locations.setting: Disused city prison of 1903 in Rennes with a radial cell block, landings and walkways, exercise yards and a high perimeter wall, now owned by the city.

locations.name: Provence Studios
locations.setting: A studio complex on 22 hectares near Martigues with sixteen sound stages up to 2,400 square metres, two 18,000 square metre backlots and ready-built prison, police station and courtroom sets.
locations.known_for: Titane, The Serpent Queen, Gaston Lagaffe
locations.facilities: Over 15 stages across 26,000 m2 of studio space on a 22-hectare site, listed as 17 modular stages. Studio M07 2,450 m2 (49.51 x 33.10 m, 9.20 m ceiling); Studio M01 1,000 m2 (50 x 20 m, 15 m ceiling); M06 950 m2 and M05 900 m2 (39.77 m long, 9.20 m ceiling); M04 680 m2 (9.20 m); M02 400 m2 (4.90 m); M03 250 m2 (5.30 m). Also green screens, an underwater tank, backlots for exterior sets and stunts, ready-to-shoot standing sets, a virtual production LED stage of 14 by 14 metres, 1,000 m2 of production offices and 8,000 m2 of workshops and joinery.
locations.suitability: Ready-built prison, police station, morgue, hospital room and courtroom sets, plus two exterior backlots
locations.logistics: 7 Boulevard Maritime, 13500 Martigues: 25 minutes from Aix-Marseille TGV station (Paris 3 hours by TGV), 25 minutes from Marseille Provence airport and 30 minutes from the centre of Marseille.

locations.name: Puits Couriot, Parc-Musee de la Mine
locations.setting: Colliery closed in 1973 and kept as a museum: winding towers, the 1948 hanging changing room, lamp room, workshops, slag heaps and a visitable underground gallery.

locations.name: Puy du Fou
locations.setting: Historical show park with a Gallo-Roman arena, a medieval fort, a reconstructed 1900 village and large open air stages with standing sets and stabling.
locations.suitability: The park publishes a dedicated filming page for productions wanting to use its sets and arenas.

locations.name: Saline royale d'Arc-et-Senans
locations.setting: Semicircular saltworks of 1779 by Ledoux, with a columned gatehouse, the director's house, two long evaporation halls and a wide open courtyard closed by woodland.
locations.suitability: The site has its own page for film and photo shoots.

photo.author: This Photo was taken by Wolfgang Moroder. Feel free to use my photos, but please mention me as the author and send me a

locations.name: Site Le Corbusier, Firminy
locations.setting: Le Corbusier's Firminy-Vert complex, completed after his death, with a raw-concrete Unite d'habitation apartment block, a stadium and a church, its visitor centre offering room hire for seminars.

locations.name: Sous-marin Espadon
locations.setting: Cold war French submarine preserved afloat in the lock of the Saint-Nazaire submarine base, with control room, torpedo room, bunks and engine spaces open inside.
locations.suitability: The Saint-Nazaire tourist board, which runs the site, publishes a press and filming contact for reports, interviews and shoots.

locations.name: Stade de France
locations.setting: National stadium in Saint-Denis seating over 80,000, built for the 1998 World Cup and used for major sport, concerts and ceremonies.

locations.name: Stade Geoffroy-Guichard
locations.setting: Football ground of 1931 with four separate steep stands, about 41,000 seats, players tunnels, dressing rooms, press areas and a surrounding car park.

locations.name: Stade Marie-Marvingt (MMArena)
locations.setting: Football stadium of 2011 seating about 25,000, with a translucent shell, unbroken seating bowl, changing rooms, press areas and hospitality lounges.
locations.suitability: The stadium publishes a hire offer for seminars and corporate events in its lounges and stadium spaces.

locations.name: Station F
locations.setting: Former Halle Freyssinet railway freight depot, a single steel-framed hall over 300 metres long in southeast Paris, now a start-up campus with open floors and event space.

locations.name: Studio 24
locations.setting: Shooting and rehearsal stage in Villeurbanne used for film and television work, also hired for rehearsals and live performances, on the eastern edge of Lyon.

locations.name: Studio de Tourcoing
locations.setting: A single soundproofed stage in Tourcoing, near Lille, run by lighting and studio rental group Transpa and fitted out with an in-house DIT and data lab for on-set post-production.
locations.facilities: One stage of 500 sqm equipped with a DATALAB DIT service.
locations.logistics: Address 99B/C Boulevard Descat, 59200 Tourcoing. By car follow the D656 to Boulevard Constantin Descat; nearest metro station Alsace, bus station Roubaix; Lille-Lesquin airport 20 km away.

locations.name: Studios d'Épinay
locations.setting: A four-stage soundstage complex on the site of the former Éclair film laboratories in Épinay-sur-Seine, now owned by TSF, with stage ceiling heights of up to 15 metres.
locations.known_for: Le Grand Bleu, La Reine Margot, Amour, The Substance
locations.facilities: Plateau F: 1,500 sqm (42.35m x 32.40m); Plateau C: 800 sqm (36.60m x 23.85m); Plateau D: 800 sqm (39m x 16.30m); Plateau E: 200 sqm (18.35m x 11.50m); ceiling heights up to 15 metres; set-design workshops, secure storage, dressing rooms, production offices.
locations.logistics: 20 minutes from central Paris by car, around 35 minutes via RER C and metro line 14.

locations.name: Studios de Bry
locations.setting: A large multi-stage production complex east of Paris, built by SFP in the late 1970s and 1980s and now run by Transpalux, with workshops and offices for feature films and television drama.
locations.known_for: Babylon A.D., Colombiana, Les Rivières pourpres 2, L'Odeur de la papaye verte
locations.facilities: Stage B1: 1,000 sqm; B2: 700 sqm; B3: 700 sqm; Neo B4: 300 sqm; B5: 1,100 sqm; B6: 900 sqm; B10: 350 sqm (above B4); carpentry workshop 450 sqm; paint workshop 400 sqm plus 100 sqm mezzanine; metal workshop 300 sqm; upholstery workshop 200 sqm; pre-assembly workshops of 1,200 and 600 sqm; production offices over 2,300 sqm; dressing rooms/makeup totalling 1,650 sqm including 8 VIP rooms of 21 sqm each; on-site restaurant.
locations.logistics: 1 Boulevard Georges Melies, 94350 Villiers-sur-Marne. By car the A4 motorway, exit 6 Champigny / Bry, then the D3 towards Avenue de l'Europe; RER line A to Bry-sur-Marne or Noisy-le-Grand-Mont d'Est; bus lines 520 and 120, stop Moliere. Airports: Roissy CDG 35 km, Le Bourget 21 km, Orly 21 km. On-site storage of 1,200 m2 in units of 50 to 300 m2, a lighting store run by Transpalux and a restaurant on site.

locations.name: Studios de France
locations.setting: A television production group operating soundstages at three sites in Paris and Saint-Denis, used for game shows, entertainment formats and drama for French broadcasters.
locations.known_for: Star Academy, La France a un Incroyable Talent
locations.facilities: Stages across three Paris sites, listed from 135 m2 to 2,000 m2: Studio 217 is 2,000 m2 (35.40 x 54.30 m, 14 m usable height, ERP audience limit 2,000); Lendit L1 1,323 m2 (32.20 x 41.10 m, 13 m); Studio 128 1,200 m2 (28.65 x 42 m, 12.50 m); Lendit L5 1,079 m2 (30.50 x 35.40 m, 12 m); Studios 130 Plateau 1 932 m2 and Plateau 2 924 m2 (10.33 m); Studios 107 Plateau 1 900 m2 (10 m); Studios 210 Plateaux 1 and 2 815 m2 each (10 m). Every stage is listed as soundproofed and air-conditioned, most with fibre in and out, motorised or fixed rigging and traditional lighting; published ERP audience limits run from 150 to 2,000 places.

locations.name: Studios de la Victorine
locations.setting: Film studios founded in 1919 in a walled park in Nice and run directly by the city since 2017, with eleven stages, workshops and an outdoor lot.
locations.known_for: Les Enfants du Paradis, Day for Night

locations.name: Studios SETS
locations.setting: A production complex created in 1982 in Stains, just north of Saint-Denis, with soundproofed stages up to 800 sqm, a built-in tank stage and set-building workshops.
locations.known_for: Le Routard, Ad Vitam, De l'autre côté du périph
locations.facilities: Studio 800A: 800 sqm, 8m ceiling; Studio 800B: 800 sqm, soundproofed, 9m ceiling, with a 2.3m deep pool built in; Studio 500A: 500 sqm, soundproofed, approved for public access, 8m ceiling; Atelier 600: 600 sqm, 5.25m ceiling; Atelier 300: 288 sqm, 3.43m ceiling; Atelier 500B: 430 sqm, 4.7m ceiling; Espace 100: 80 sqm, 2.35m ceiling; two carpentry workshops; 5 production offices; 14 dressing rooms including 3 makeup/hair/costume rooms; on-site restaurant seating 100; two enclosed parking areas.
locations.logistics: About 10 km north of central Paris.

locations.name: Theatre Antique d'Orange
locations.setting: Best-preserved Roman theatre stage wall in Europe, in Orange, with tiered stone seating for around 9,000, used every summer as the main stage of the Choregies opera festival.

locations.name: Theatre Antique de Vienne
locations.setting: Roman theatre cut into a hillside above Vienne on the Rhone, with tiered stone seating for around 7,000, used every summer as the main stage of the Jazz a Vienne festival.

locations.name: Theatre des Arts, Rouen
locations.setting: Opera house of 1962 in central Rouen with a 1,300 seat auditorium, orchestra pit, stage tower, foyers and rehearsal rooms, home of the Normandy opera and orchestra.
locations.suitability: The opera publishes a professional hire offer for events in its auditorium and public spaces.

locations.name: Theatre National Populaire, Villeurbanne
locations.setting: Municipal theatre of 1934 rebuilt in 2011, with a large main auditorium, a smaller studio, scenery workshops and a brick front on the Gratte-Ciel square.

locations.name: Transpalux
locations.setting: A film lighting and grip company's premises in Saint-Yrieix-sur-Charente near Angoulême, offered by the regional film commission as three separate industrial halls of 487 to 710 square metres.
locations.facilities: Three buildings of 603.7, 710.4 and 487.1 square metres

locations.name: Tribunal de Paris
locations.setting: Renzo Piano's 160-metre glass courthouse tower at Porte de Clichy, housing Paris's civil and criminal courts around a public hall and stacked courtroom floors, with filming possible by arrangement.

locations.name: TSF Studios d'Aquitaine
locations.setting: A 400 square metre studio building run by a film equipment rental company in Bègles, in the Bordeaux metropolitan area, listed by the regional film commission for shoots needing a single controllable space.
locations.facilities: A 400 m2 stage (Plateau 400) with a three-sided cyclorama and a motorised grid, plus a set-design workshop, actors' dressing rooms, production offices and an on-site TSF lighting and grip equipment store.
locations.logistics: Secure parking on site.

locations.name: UCLy campus Saint-Paul (former Saint-Paul prison)
locations.setting: Lyon's 19th century Saint-Paul prison converted into a university campus, keeping the radial cell wings, iron walkways, central rotunda and gatehouse.
locations.suitability: The university offers privatisation of spaces on the campus.

locations.name: Viaduc de Millau
locations.setting: Cable-stayed road bridge across the Tarn valley, the tallest of its kind in the world at 343 metres, carrying the A75 motorway.

locations.name: Vichy Celestins Spa Hotel
locations.setting: Spa hotel on the Allier riverfront in Vichy, with thermal pools, treatment floors, a restaurant, lounges and rooms looking over the park and the lake.

locations.name: Villa Demoiselle
locations.setting: Art nouveau villa of 1904 next to the Pommery cellars, restored with period furniture, stained glass, mosaics, a main staircase and a walled garden.

locations.name: Villa Les Roches Brunes
locations.setting: Belle Epoque seaside villa of 1893 on the Pointe du Moulinet at Dinard, owned by the town, with panelled reception rooms, a veranda and terraces above the sea.
locations.logistics: Owned and run by the town of Dinard, which uses the villa for exhibitions and events.

locations.name: Villa Majorelle
locations.setting: Art nouveau house of 1901 by Henri Sauvage, reopened in 2020 with original woodwork, stained glass, ceramic fireplaces, fitted furniture and a small garden.

locations.name: Villa Savoye
locations.setting: Le Corbusier's white 1931 villa in Poissy raised on thin pilotis, with ribbon windows, a roof garden and a spiral ramp, managed as a national monument.
locations.facilities: Interior capacity up to 70 people; garden/exterior capacity up to 450.
locations.suitability: Available for filming and photography year-round except during exhibitions. Images made at Villa Savoye are subject to image rights managed by the Fondation Le Corbusier and ADAGP.

locations.name: Vulcania
locations.setting: Volcano-themed science park built into the Auvergne hillside near Clermont-Ferrand, with underground galleries and a crater-shaped amphitheatre, listing seminar and private event hire.

locations.name: 069 Westside Studio
locations.setting: A large rental film and photo studio in Frankfurt, about nine minutes from the airport, equipped with a robotic camera rig and rail system plus extensive lighting gear.
locations.facilities: 300 m2 studio floor with a 5 m ceiling and a 22 m drivable cyclorama, entrance height 2.40 m, 63 A three-phase power, business fibre with synchronous upload and download, ceiling truss and ceiling sail, green and blue screen, ARRI lighting and 4K camera equipment, sound recording possible, changing room and make-up, a lounge area and catering on request. A floor plan is published as a PDF.
locations.logistics: Westerbachstrasse 105, 65936 Frankfurt am Main, five minutes from Messe Frankfurt and 15 minutes from Frankfurt airport, with parking at the studio and a 2.40 m entrance height.

locations.name: 101 Studios
locations.setting: A rental photo and film studio in Frankfurt's Eschersheim district, with blackout windows and roller shutters, a make-up room with shower, a kitchen and on-site parking.
locations.price_note: Studio 101 EUR 135 for 4 hours on weekdays and EUR 145 at weekends and on public holidays, EUR 155 / EUR 165 for 6 hours, full day (8 hours) from EUR 260; Studio 102 EUR 120 / EUR 130 for 4 hours, EUR 140 / EUR 150 for 6 hours, full day from EUR 200; Studio D16 EUR 130 / EUR 140 for 4 hours. Prices include continuous and RGB lighting, flash and effect lights cost a flat EUR 40; prices shown include VAT for private customers and exclude VAT for business customers (own site)
locations.facilities: Three hire studios in Frankfurt-Eschersheim: Studio 101, 105 sqm, one large room with an open side room, makeup room with shower, 4 to 6 m ceiling and two background systems up to 3.55 m wide; Studio 102, 80 sqm in two rooms (60 sqm and 20 sqm) with a 2.72 m background system; Studio D16, 110 sqm in three rooms in industrial style with a 2.72 m background system on six rolls. A 24 sqm kitchen shared by Studios 101 and 102 can also be used for shoots.
locations.logistics: The studios are in the Dreihäusergasse in Frankfurt-Eschersheim and have their own parking spaces.

locations.name: Abtei Brauweiler
locations.setting: Former Benedictine abbey near Pulheim later used as a workhouse and detention site, with cell wings, plain institutional corridors, a Romanesque church and courtyards.

locations.name: Albrecht Duerer Airport Nuremberg
locations.setting: Bavaria's second airport, running around the clock with two departure halls, one arrivals hall, three multi storey car parks and open views onto the apron from the parking decks.
locations.logistics: Nuremberg city centre about 13 minutes away on U-Bahn line 2, 9,000 parking spaces

locations.name: Alte Feuerwache Mannheim
locations.setting: A disused early-20th-century fire station converted into a cultural centre, keeping its engine hall, brick facade and yard, now hired for concerts and events.

locations.name: Alte Klinik Greifenstein
locations.setting: A former specialist lung clinic at Waldhof in Greifenstein, in operation until 2020, with about 4,500 square metres of floor space across an older building and later extensions.

locations.name: Alte Lokhalle Freiburg
locations.setting: Old locomotive hall and surrounding industrial ground near Freiburg main station, offering hall space alongside office and administration rooms.

locations.name: Alte Oper Frankfurt
locations.setting: Rebuilt 1880s opera house in Frankfurt, now a concert and congress venue with a restored historicist facade and a modern auditorium behind it.
locations.facilities: Grosser Saal (Grand Hall): 2,064 m2, 17.5 m high, up to 2,434 in row seating, 1,150 to 1,228 banquet, 644 parliamentary. Mozart Saal: 817 m2, 6.2 m high, up to 718 row seating, 362 to 376 banquet, 220 parliamentary. Salons (Schumann, Liszt, Mendelssohn, Telemann): 75 to 83 m2, 2.5 to 5.5 m high, 30 to 72 people depending on layout. Foyers (Paul Hindemith, Clara Schumann, Hertie, Albert Mangelsdorff): 260 to 880 m2, capacity 136 to 265.

locations.name: Alte Schokoladenfabrik Oderwitz
locations.setting: A fully vacant former chocolate factory site in Oderwitz near Goerlitz, with an administration building with a period staircase alongside disused production and storage halls.

locations.name: Alter Elbtunnel
locations.setting: Tiled road and foot tunnel of 1911 under the Elbe with two long tubes, domed entrance halls and vehicle lifts, managed by the Hamburg Port Authority.

locations.name: Andaz Munich Schwabinger Tor
locations.setting: Design hotel on Leopoldstrasse in Schwabing with the highest rooftop bar in Munich, looking over the city towards the Alps.
locations.facilities: Parking for vehicles up to 7.5 t, level delivery access

locations.name: AquaMar Marburg
locations.setting: Marburg's municipal sports and leisure pool, with indoor and outdoor basins, a water slide, a diving pool, a wellness and sauna area and a seasonal outdoor water park.

locations.name: Autostadt Wolfsburg
locations.setting: Car-brand visitor park beside the Volkswagen plant in Wolfsburg, with pavilions, glass delivery towers, a museum hall and landscaped grounds beside a canal.

locations.name: Backstage Munich
locations.setting: Event and culture centre of about 5,500 sq m on the former AGA Gas works site in Munich, split into Werk, Halle, Club and arena areas plus an open air stage, with the industrial fabric largely kept.
locations.facilities: Indoor areas of about 800, 350, 150 and 1,200 sq m, no access restrictions, ample on site parking, standard supply to 63 A

locations.name: Bahnpark Augsburg
locations.setting: Former Deutsche Bahn depot in Augsburg with track fan, roundhouse, steam locomotive shed, forge, old bunkers and historic rolling stock including a mail coach.
