locations.setting: A 1952 railway water tower in Wrocław converted into a brick and steel venue of over 350 square metres, with a cafe, a workshop and conference space, two studio apartments and a rooftop terrace with a 360 degree view.

locations.name: EC1 Lodz
locations.setting: A former coal-fired power station of 1907 in central Lodz, restored as a science and culture centre with its original turbine hall, boiler house and control rooms intact.

locations.name: Elektrownia Powisle
locations.setting: A former Warsaw power station on the Vistula riverside, its turn of the century turbine and boiler halls converted into a retail, dining and event complex while keeping the original brick and steelwork.
locations.facilities: Industrial-style halls for events and exhibitions, food hall, day spa
locations.logistics: ul. Dobra 42, Warsaw, Powisle district

locations.name: Expo Lodz exhibition hall
locations.setting: A modern exhibition centre in Lodz with conference rooms alongside its main trade-fair hall, used for events and available for filming.

locations.name: Former City Prison, Wrocław
locations.setting: A former municipal prison on Więzienna street in Wrocław, built from the late 14th century and enlarged into a closed quadrangle by the 1680s, its basement interrogation cells now a pub and the rest an academic institute.

locations.name: Former Halemba-Wirek Mine Dismantling Centre
locations.setting: A former coal mine site in Ruda Śląska with intact workshop halls, overhead cranes, technological tracks, warehouses and an abandoned residential building, used mainly for exteriors.
locations.suitability: crime, action, war, historical, thriller, horror and post-apocalyptic productions, automotive commercials, music videos
locations.logistics: on-site office space, briefing room and shower facilities

locations.name: Former hospital on Drewnowska street, Lodz
locations.setting: A former hospital building on Drewnowska street in Lodz with its own chapel and grounds, listed by the local film commission as a location for institutional interiors.

locations.name: Former synagogue, Zarki (MGOK)
locations.setting: A 19th-century former synagogue in the small town of Zarki, now the municipal cultural centre (MGOK), with power, water and vehicle access offered for filming.

locations.name: Fort VI, Poznań
locations.setting: One of the 19th-century ring forts of the Poznan Fortress, built to the German fortification pattern with barrack buildings, a caponier, a dry moat and outer gates largely unaltered.

locations.name: Franowo Tram Tunnel
locations.setting: A 2 kilometre tram line between Poznan housing estates that runs mostly through a tunnel separated from road traffic, ending at a modern loop and depot.

locations.name: Gdansk Shipyard (European Solidarity Centre)
locations.setting: The historic Lenin Shipyard gate and slipways where the Solidarity movement began in 1980, bordered by the European Solidarity Centre's rusted-steel museum building and surviving shipyard halls.
locations.facilities: Auditorium: 483 sq m, up to 417 people, with a 7x11 m stage, a 12x7 m movie screen, 4 simultaneous interpretation booths (8 language channels) and 2 dressing rooms, plus an adjoining 125 sq m mezzanine. Other spaces: Winter Garden 400 sq m, Foyer 500 sq m, Observation Deck 600 sq m (over 25 m high, up to 50 people, seasonal access), Multifunctional Hall 220 sq m (up to 200 people), Library 180 sq m (up to 100 people), Media Library 85 sq m (up to 70 people), Archive Reading Room 72 sq m (up to 30 people), and workshop rooms of 92 sq m (up to 70 people) and 52 sq m (up to 50 people).

locations.name: Glogowska Tram Depot, Poznan
locations.setting: A working tram depot in Poznan opened in 1907 on a 2.9 hectare site, with vehicle maintenance halls, a 1962 office block and a preserved horse-drawn tram kept in running order.

locations.name: H. Cegielski Works, Poznan
locations.setting: The last working section of the historic Cegielski engineering works in Poznan, with early 20th-century production halls, later office blocks, in-house built machinery and its own rail siding.
locations.facilities: Rail siding on site, mixed production and office halls

locations.name: Hala Koszyki
locations.setting: A 1908 steel-framed market hall in Warsaw's Ochota district, restored behind its original facade into a food hall of restaurants, bars and shops around a glazed central nave.

locations.name: Hel Peninsula
locations.setting: A 35-kilometre sand spit enclosing the Bay of Gdansk, with pine-backed Baltic beaches on its open-sea side and a historic fishing town and former naval base at its tip.

locations.name: Heliodor Święcicki Clinical Hospital
locations.setting: A working Poznan hospital complex combining a 1908 main building with a chapel, and later wings from 1973 to 2001, set among wooded grounds with benched paths.

locations.name: Historic Guido Coal Mine
locations.setting: A former working coal mine in Zabrze, now a branch of the Museum of Coal Mining, with underground tours down to 320 metres and a preserved pithead machine hall.

locations.name: Hotel Diament Ustron
locations.setting: A resort and spa hotel in the wooded Zawodzie district of Ustron, with a pyramid-shaped main building from 1979, 121 rooms, conference space and an indoor pool with a wave feature.
locations.facilities: 121 rooms, conference hall, spa and wellness area with pool, on-site restaurant, parking

locations.name: Huta Batory director's building
locations.setting: A 1915 modernist administration building at the Huta Batory steelworks in Chorzow, still in office use, with a roof turret, three bas-reliefs over the entrance and an interior courtyard.
locations.facilities: Power and water, parking, meeting rooms, original period interiors

locations.name: ICE Krakow Congress Centre
locations.setting: A congress centre on the Vistula riverbank in Krakow run by the city's development agency, with an auditorium hall, a theatre hall and a chamber hall used for conferences, concerts and theatrical productions.
locations.logistics: ul. Marii Konopnickiej 17, Krakow

locations.name: Jeżyce Fire Station, Poznań
locations.setting: A 1908 fire station in Poznan's Grunwald district with baroque-influenced brickwork, a training yard with obstacles for firefighters and a cobbled forecourt.

locations.name: Jotes Machine Factory, Lodz
locations.setting: A working machine-tool factory in Lodz tracing back to an 1866 mechanical workshop, still designing, building and distributing surface, cylindrical and internal grinders.

locations.name: Juliusz Slowacki Theatre
locations.setting: A late 19th-century municipal theatre on plac Swietego Ducha in Krakow, with an ornate main auditorium plus the smaller Dom Machin and MOS stages, offering building tours and venue hire.

locations.name: Karol Szymanowski Academy of Music, Katowice
locations.setting: A music conservatory in central Katowice combining a neo-Gothic former Silesian Sejm building with a modern wing holding a 480-seat concert hall, library and practice rooms.
locations.facilities: Electricity on site, parking in front of the building

locations.name: Kasprowy Wierch Cable Car
locations.setting: A 1936 aerial cableway climbing from Kuznice to the 1,987-metre summit of Kasprowy Wierch in the Tatras, run in two stages with a mid-station at Myslenickie Turnie.

locations.name: Katowice-Muchowiec Airport
locations.setting: A small general-aviation airfield and aeroclub on the southern edge of Katowice, with grass and paved runways, hangars and open apron space inside the city ring road.

locations.name: Kazimierz, Kraków
locations.setting: Kraków's former Jewish quarter, where synagogues, cobbled lanes and tenement courtyards still follow the pre-war street layout.

locations.name: Koneser (former Warsaw Vodka Factory)
locations.setting: A former vodka distillery in the Praga district of Warsaw, its 19th-century factory buildings and central plaza now hosting restaurants, shops, galleries and a vodka museum, hired for markets, concerts and exhibitions.
locations.logistics: Plac Konesera 1, Warsaw, Praga-Polnoc district

locations.name: Kościół Św. Wawrzyńca w Mikołowie (Church of St Lawrence, Mikołów)
locations.setting: A brick parish church in the Mokre district of Mikołów, built in the mid-16th century and rebuilt several times, with stained glass windows in its interior.

locations.name: KWK Centrum Coal Mine
locations.setting: A Bytom coal mine, working from 1881 and in liquidation since 2015, with a mining shaft, an escape-apparatus store and a security building still standing among the halls being demolished.
locations.facilities: Vehicle access, on-site production base, parking

locations.name: Laziska Power Plant
locations.setting: A coal-fired power station at Laziska Gorne built in 1917, still operated by Tauron, with heat-exchanger halls, an on-site energy museum and surrounding woodland and meadow.
locations.facilities: Electricity on site, parking available, energy museum on the premises

locations.name: Lodz Film School (PWSFTviT)
locations.setting: The national film, television and theatre school in Lodz, with shooting halls, screening rooms and post-production labs used by students, and a production history running through Polish cinema since the 1940s.
locations.known_for: Alumni include Andrzej Wajda, Roman Polanski, Krzysztof Kieslowski

locations.name: Manufaktura
locations.setting: Izrael Poznanski's 19th-century red-brick textile mill complex in Lodz, converted into a shopping, leisure and museum quarter around its original factory yard and chimney.

locations.name: Miechowice Combined Heat and Power Plant, Bytom
locations.setting: An operating heat and power plant in Bytom-Miechowice built 1950-1954 on former power-station grounds, with four chimneys, boiler halls and turbine sets amid urban forest.
locations.facilities: Large parking area on site

locations.name: Mieszczański Brewery, Wrocław
locations.setting: A 19th-century brewery complex on Hubska street in Wrocław's Huby district, operating from 1894 to 1996 and now a cultural venue with galleries, a theatre, a photography studio and workshop spaces.

locations.name: MOCAK Museum of Contemporary Art
locations.setting: A contemporary art museum in Krakow's Zablocie district, built into the former administrative building of the Oskar Schindler Enamel Factory, with galleries laid out through the historic industrial structure.
locations.logistics: ul. Lipowa 4, Krakow

locations.name: Morasko Campus, Adam Mickiewicz University
locations.setting: A university campus in northern Poznan built from 1984 onward in late modernist and postmodernist styles, with wide pedestrian routes, lecture buildings, a sports centre and a swimming pool.

locations.name: MOSiR Sports Hall, Lodz
locations.setting: A 1957 socialist-realist sports hall in Lodz nicknamed the Palace of Sport, seating around 9,000 and also used for concerts, trade events and religious gatherings.

locations.name: Muzeum Emigracji (Emigration Museum)
locations.setting: A restored 1930s ocean liner terminal on the Gdynia waterfront, now the Emigration Museum, with its original passenger halls open to visitors and offered as rentable event space.
locations.facilities: Rentable spaces at the Maritime Station building: an audiovisual room, a cinema room, the main hall and the exhibition corridor, used for conferences, training, screenings, concerts, performances, film screenings, workshops, presentations and symposia (own site).

locations.name: Muzeum Hutnictwa Cynku Walcownia (Zinc Metallurgy Museum)
locations.setting: A zinc-processing museum in the Szopienice district of Katowice covering over 5,000 square metres of former rolling-mill halls, with an intact production line of furnaces and rollers.

locations.name: Muzeum Kinematografii w Łodzi (Museum of Cinematography)
locations.setting: A house museum since 1986 in the former Scheibler family palace on Plac Zwycięstwa in Łódź, whose historic interiors have served as scenography for dozens of Polish films and TV series.

locations.name: National Forum of Music (NFM)
locations.setting: A 2015 concert hall complex on plac Wolnosci in Wroclaw, run jointly by the city, the region and the ministry of culture, with a main hall plus red, black and chamber halls available to hire.
locations.facilities: Four halls (Main Hall plus three chamber halls) plus a foyer and a VIP room available to hire, within about 50,000 m2 of event space. Includes top-standard artist dressing rooms, a spacious backstage, a buffet and restaurant, restrooms on every floor, three cloakrooms, accessibility facilities and an adjoining underground car park with over 600 spaces (own site).
locations.suitability: Non-music events such as conventions, symposia and conferences can be held in the concert halls, but the venue states each event must include an artistic component (own site).
locations.logistics: Underground parking for over 600 cars adjoining the building (own site).

locations.name: Nikiszowiec
locations.setting: A brick workers' housing estate built 1908-1918 for the Giesche coal mine, its enclosed courtyard blocks, arcaded passages and communal bakery still inhabited today.

locations.name: Norblin Factory
locations.setting: A 19th-century metalware factory in the Wola district of Warsaw, its brick production halls preserved as an open-air industrial museum alongside offices, shops and restaurants across a 2 hectare site.
locations.facilities: Atmospheric post-industrial halls used for conferences, premieres, concerts and fashion shows
locations.logistics: ul. Zelazna 51/53, Warsaw, Wola district

locations.name: Nowa Huta
locations.setting: A planned socialist-realist steelworkers' town built from 1949 beside the former Lenin steelworks, with a monumental central square, arcaded avenues and uniform apartment blocks.

locations.name: Ogrodzieniec Castle
locations.setting: Ruined 14th-century castle on the highest hill of the Kraków-Częstochowa Upland, its broken towers rising among limestone outcrops on the Trail of the Eagles' Nests.

locations.name: Okrąglak Department Store, Poznań
locations.setting: A cylindrical 1948-1955 department store in central Poznan, 45 metres tall with 9 floors above ground and 2 below, its interior staircase winding around a central shaft with a rooftop city view.

locations.name: Opera Lesna (Sopot Forest Opera)
locations.setting: An open-air amphitheatre cut into wooded dunes above Sopot, seating around 4,300 beneath a part-covered stage, home to the annual Sopot Festival.

locations.name: ORP Blyskawica
locations.setting: A Grom-class destroyer launched in 1936 and preserved as a museum ship on Gdynia's waterfront, with its bridge, gun turrets and below-deck compartments open to visitors.
locations.facilities: The museum building (not the ship itself) rents an audiovisual hall for up to 121 people, with daylight and ceiling lighting, a screen and projector, lectern, WiFi, cloakroom and ground-floor toilets, plus a small classroom for up to 15 people. Space in front of the building is not available for hire.

locations.name: Osiedle A
locations.setting: The first planned housing estate of postwar Tychy, built from the 1950s with low modernist blocks around courtyards and green space, named winner of the Silesian Film Location 2024 award.
locations.suitability: Listed with medium light intensity and medium noise intensity, and road access marked as possible (Silesia Film Commission listing).
locations.logistics: Parking available on site; distance from the production base is listed as on site (Silesia Film Commission listing).

locations.name: Pałac Kultury Zagłębia (Palace of Culture of Zagłębie)
locations.setting: A 1950s culture centre in Dąbrowa Górnicza designed by Zbigniew Rzepecki, with a cinema hall, theatre stage, wedding hall and gallery still in public use.

locations.name: Palace of Culture and Science
locations.setting: A 237-metre socialist-classicist tower built in 1955 as a gift from the Soviet Union, holding theatres, cinemas, a congress hall, museums and an observation deck over central Warsaw.
locations.facilities: 237 m tall building with 46 floors and 3,288 rooms; the viewing terrace is at 114 m.

locations.name: PGE Narodowy
locations.setting: Warsaw's national stadium of 2011, built on the site of the former Tenth-Anniversary Stadium, with a retractable roof and a facade patterned on the Polish flag.
locations.facilities: Over 50,000 m2 of business space, including what the venue describes as the largest conference and congress centre in Warsaw (own site).

locations.name: Plac Rybny, Będzin
locations.setting: A small historic square in Będzin's old town named after its former fish market, framed by townhouses and used by the city for public events.
locations.facilities: Open public square with parking nearby

locations.name: Podlesice 38
locations.setting: A small countryside guesthouse near Kroczyce in the Polish Jura, with a 50 square metre apartment, three ensuite bedrooms, a living room and a terrace.
locations.facilities: Electricity, water and parking on site

locations.name: Polish Theatre, Bielsko-Biała
locations.setting: An 1890 eclectic theatre building in Bielsko-Biała designed by Viennese architect Emil von Förster, with a Big Stage, a Small Stage and a smaller studio stage.
locations.facilities: Electricity, water and parking on site

locations.name: Poznań City Hall Offices (Urząd Miasta Poznania)
locations.setting: A baroque, horseshoe-shaped former Jesuit college in central Poznan built in two stages between 1701 and 1737, now the city administration's offices around a large courtyard.

locations.name: Poznań Garbary Railway Station
locations.setting: A two-platform 1888 railway station near Poznan's Citadel, refurbished in 2008, with industrial land to the west and green riverside ground to the east.

locations.name: Poznań Główny Railway Station
locations.setting: A 2012 postmodern integrated transport hub in Poznan combining the main railway and bus station with a shopping gallery, next to the older 1960s socialist-realist station building.

locations.name: Poznan International Fair (MTP)
locations.setting: Poland's largest trade fair complex in central Poznan, dating from 1921, with 15 pavilions, a congress centre, banqueting spaces and an event plaza used for exhibitions and large-scale events.
locations.facilities: 15 exhibition pavilions, congress centre, underground parking, on-site hotels and restaurants

locations.name: Poznan Town Hall
locations.setting: A Renaissance town hall of 1560 on Poznan's Old Market Square, rebuilt to Italian designs, with an arcaded facade, a mechanical clock with butting goats and a council chamber now a history museum.

photo.author: This image was produced by me, David Castor (user:dcastor). The pictures I submit to the Wikipedia Project are released

locations.name: Poznan University of Physical Education campus
locations.setting: A university sports campus in Poznan with a multi-function stadium, swimming pool, tennis courts and a sports hall, alongside a 1960s socialist-realist main building and an early 20th-century rectorate.

locations.name: Poznan-Lawica Airport
locations.setting: A single-runway regional airport in Poznan named after Henryk Wieniawski, with a compact modern terminal, a mezzanine level and a nearby vintage 1916 Albatros aircraft on display.
locations.facilities: Large car park in front of the terminal

locations.name: Rędziński Bridge, Wrocław
locations.setting: A cable-stayed road bridge over the Oder in Wrocław carrying the A8 motorway on a single 122 metre pylon with 160 stays, spanning 612 metres as the tallest structure of its kind in Poland.

locations.name: Regional Court in Katowice
locations.setting: A six-storey courthouse in Katowice completed in 2009, an elongated cuboid block with 51 courtrooms, a planted internal courtyard and over 600 office rooms.
locations.facilities: 51 courtrooms, internal courtyard, rear parking area

locations.name: Regional Specialist Hospital No. 5, Sosnowiec
locations.setting: A working trauma hospital in Sosnowiec opened in 1988 on the site of the former Coal Miners' Hospital, with a helicopter landing pad and an underground tunnel to its emergency department.
locations.facilities: Helicopter landing pad, underground patient transfer tunnel, on-site car park

locations.name: Restauracja Rusałka, Poznań
locations.setting: A lakeside restaurant a few minutes from central Poznan, set among woodland and used for dining, family occasions and corporate events year round.

locations.name: Rödl & Partner Office Building, Gliwice
locations.setting: A three-storey modernist office building in Gliwice, 300 metres from the Old Town, with meeting and conference rooms, a lecture hall, a terrace and parking in front.
locations.facilities: Electricity and parking on site

locations.name: Sąd Rejonowy w Sosnowcu (Sosnowiec District Court)
locations.setting: A district court operating since 1945 inside one of the Schön family's eclectic 1903 palaces in Sosnowiec, with courtrooms set in the original ballroom, dining room and library.

locations.name: Sieradz railway station
locations.setting: A 19th-century station building typical of small stations built under Russian rule, on the only stop between Lodz and Kalisz, about 70 kilometres from Lodz.

locations.name: Silesian Library
locations.setting: A glazed 1998 public library on European Council Square in central Katowice, with reading rooms, a hall and storage floors that read as modern civic interiors.
locations.facilities: Electricity, water, high natural light and on-site parking

locations.name: Silesian Trade Centre, Hall 3, Chorzow
locations.setting: An empty 40 by 100 metre steel-framed exhibition hall at a trade centre next to Silesia Park in Chorzow, with a loading ramp and two vehicle entrance gates, ready to be dressed for a build.
locations.facilities: Electricity on site, parking in front of the hall, loading ramp and two vehicle entrance gates

locations.name: Silesian Voivodeship Office, Katowice
locations.setting: A 1925-1929 government headquarters in central Katowice with a 260-seat former regional parliament hall, a marble ceremonial hall, and six kilometres of corridors across 634 rooms.
locations.facilities: 634 rooms, 260-seat hall, marble hall, on-site parking

locations.name: Spodek
locations.setting: A saucer-shaped 1971 sports and concert arena in central Katowice, its suspended roof spanning a hall seating up to about 11,500 for events.
locations.suitability: A standard filming day covers 12 hours of shooting plus 2 hours for equipment setup and teardown, and includes an electrical connection, a dedicated event manager, a break room and parking; an extra setup/teardown day costs 50 percent of the daily filming rate. Interior photo sessions are allowed subject to the event schedule, roof photography is not permitted, and drone shots must comply with Polish aviation regulations.

locations.name: Stadion Slaski
locations.setting: A bowl stadium built in 1956 on a reclaimed slag heap in Chorzow, rebuilt with a membrane roof and seating around 54,000 for football, speedway and concerts.
locations.facilities: Maximum stand capacity 54,378 (about 30,000 for concerts on the pitch), 2,092 business seats, 384 VIP box seats (22 boxes for 16 people, 1 box for 32), and 106 spaces for visitors with disabilities. Outdoor: an artificial-turf athletics pitch 105x68 m with floodlighting at 500 lx, a natural-turf pitch 94x64 m at 250 lx, 3 tennis courts, a western perimeter area of about 23,000 sq m (asphalt, concrete, grass) and a technical backup area of about 5,000 sq m. Indoor: a conference centre of 1,785 sq m (divisible into 3), a 700 sq m conference hall with 2 retractable stands of 180 seats each, 2 multifunctional halls of 310 sq m each, a 940 sq m main hall, 2 reception/foyer areas of 364 sq m each, a large VIP box of 80 sq m and small VIP boxes of 34 sq m each.

locations.name: Stara Gazownia, Poznan
locations.setting: A mid-19th-century former gasworks on the Warta riverbank in central Poznan, part restored as red and clinker brick offices with a period staircase, part left in ruin.

locations.name: Stary Browar
locations.setting: A former brewery in central Poznan converted into a mixed retail, dining and contemporary art complex, with the original brick brewery buildings kept alongside new gallery and shopping spaces.
locations.logistics: ul. Polwiejska 42, Poznan

locations.name: Stary Szpital w Żywcu (Old Hospital, Żywiec)
locations.setting: A disused hospital building on Sienkiewicza street in Żywiec, listed by the regional film commission as a filming site with on-site parking and mains utilities.

locations.name: Studio Filmowe Arterion
locations.setting: Two air-conditioned sound stages in central Lodz, 15x11m and 17x10m with 4.2m ceilings, used for commercials, corporate video and photo shoots with blue and green screen.
locations.facilities: Studio 1: 15x11m, 4.2m height. Studio 2: 17x10m, 4.2m height. 346m2 total, two dressing rooms with private bathrooms, two make-up rooms, suspended lighting rig, blue and green screen.
locations.suitability: Blue and green screen filming, good truck access for scenography.
locations.logistics: Central Lodz, close to the A2 motorway exit and Lodz Fabryczna railway station; ul. Pomorska 69/71.

locations.name: Superjednostka
locations.setting: A 15-storey slab apartment block in central Katowice built 1967 to 1972 from prefabricated concrete panels raised on stilts, holding 762 flats for about 3,000 residents.

locations.name: Szczecin Philharmonic
locations.setting: An angular glass and white concrete concert hall in Szczecin, winner of the EU Mies van der Rohe architecture award, with a large symphonic hall plus smaller chamber and multimedia halls and a hall rental service.

locations.name: Szkoła Podstawowa w Bieruniu (Bieruń Primary School)
locations.setting: A municipal primary school in Bieruń with an original wing from 1848 extended in later decades, now spread across two buildings with 42 classes and a gym hall.

locations.name: Szombierki Coal Mine
locations.setting: A disused coal mine in Bytom dating to 1870, with two shafts, winding towers, tracks and utility buildings behind a perimeter fence; the Krystyna shaft tower is a listed monument.
locations.facilities: Parking available on site

locations.name: Sztygarka Training Mine (Kopalnia Ćwiczebna)
locations.setting: An underground training mine built in 1927 for mining school students, with three levels of tunnels and period equipment, now a branch of the Sztygarka municipal museum.

locations.name: Teatr Muzyczny im. Danuty Baduszkowej
locations.setting: A musical theatre building on plac Grunwaldzki in Gdynia with the largest musical stage in Poland alongside a new stage and a chamber stage, staging large scale musical productions.

locations.name: Teatr Polski, Poznań
locations.setting: An 1873-1875 theatre in Poznan built by public subscription, with a restored auditorium and boxes, its main facade partly original though foyer detail has since been altered.

locations.name: Textilimpex office building, Lodz
locations.setting: A mid to late 20th-century office building in central Lodz with a spacious entrance hall, listed by the local film commission for interior office shoots.

locations.name: The Villa, Łaziska Górne
locations.setting: A two-storey brick villa built in 1908 for a coal mine director in Łaziska Górne, later a community centre and now offices, set in open grounds with mature trees.
locations.facilities: Electricity, water and parking on site

locations.name: Tor Poznan racing circuit
locations.setting: A car and motorcycle racing circuit near Poznan built in 1975-1977, with an adjoining karting track, small grandstands and a mix of open and wooded surrounding terrain.

locations.name: Twierdza Boyen (Boyen Fortress)
locations.setting: A 19th-century Prussian fortress in Gizycko with ramparts, a parade ground, a powder laboratory and an armourer's workshop, hosting reenactments, festivals and light shows on its central majdan.
locations.logistics: ul. Turystyczna 1, Gizycko

locations.name: Tychy Municipal Sports and Leisure Centre, Indoor Pool
locations.setting: A modern municipal indoor pool complex in Tychy, with a 25 by 12.5 metre competition pool with a diving tower and a separate warm-up pool.
locations.facilities: Electricity, water and parking on site

locations.name: Tyskie Brewery (Tyskie Browary Książęce)
locations.setting: A working brewery in Tychy dating to 1629, with a visitor centre inside its historic industrial buildings, noted by the regional film commission for its industrial character.

locations.name: University of Warsaw Library (BUW)
locations.setting: The main library of the University of Warsaw on the Vistula riverside, combining large glazed reading rooms with a landscaped roof garden above the building, and space available to hire for events.
locations.logistics: ul. Dobra 56/66, Warsaw, Powisle district

locations.name: Vienna House Easy Katowice
locations.setting: A hotel on Sokolska street in central Katowice with a fully glazed ground floor holding the reception, lobby, restaurant and breakfast room in daylight-filled open space.

locations.name: Warsaw Uprising Museum
locations.setting: A former tram power station on Wola's Przyokopowa street, converted into a museum of the 1944 uprising, retaining its brick turbine hall and machinery among the exhibition spaces.

locations.name: Water Tower Restaurant, Pszczyna
locations.setting: A 1926 municipal water tower in Pszczyna converted into a restaurant on its top floor, with a Steampunk-styled reception room spread across two levels of the tower.
locations.facilities: Electricity, gas, water and parking on site

locations.name: WFDiF (Wytwornia Filmow Dokumentalnych i Fabularnych)
locations.setting: Warsaw production complex dating to 1949, with two sound stages added in 1960 for feature films, historically used by directors including Andrzej Wajda and Krzysztof Kieslowski.
locations.facilities: Two shooting halls of 600 m2 each with 8.5 m working height and air conditioning; a studio of 450 m2 with 4.3 m working height; a studio of 220 m2 with 5.8 m working height and air conditioning; two casting studios of 100 m2 each with 4.5 m working height and air conditioning. Make-up rooms for 1, 2 and 4 positions plus mobile stations, dressing rooms of 10 to 80 m2, prop rooms of 15 to 80 m2, about 2,500 m2 of offices, a conference room, 900 m2 of production space and 750 m2 of storage. Address ul. Chelmska 21, Warsaw.

locations.name: Wieliczka Salt Mine
locations.setting: A working salt mine near Krakow dating to the 13th century, its tunnels reaching over 300 metres deep and including carved underground chapels and chambers open to visitors.
locations.known_for: On the Silver Globe (1988), Spellbinder: Land of the Dragon Lord (1997)

locations.name: Wielka Krokiew
locations.setting: A ski jumping hill and stadium on the edge of Zakopane, host of the Four Hills Tournament and of televised New Year's Eve concerts broadcast live from its outrun and stands.

locations.name: Wieża Ciśnień Katowice-Borki (Borki Water Tower)
locations.setting: A 66-metre brick water tower in the Borki district of Katowice, built 1911 to 1912 to a design by the Zillmann architecture studio and topped with a helmet-shaped dome.

locations.name: Wolsztyn Roundhouse
locations.setting: A working steam locomotive depot in Wolsztyn, reputedly the only one in Europe still running scheduled passenger services, with around 30 steam locomotives, historic wagons and working repair workshops.

locations.name: Wrocław Świebodzki Railway Station
locations.setting: A disused 1843 railway terminus in Wrocław, closed to regular trains in 1991, now home to a stage of the Polish Theatre and a large Sunday flea market inside its restored hall.

locations.name: Żywiec Brewery Museum
locations.setting: A working brewery museum in Żywiec, opened 2006 on the site of an 1856 Habsburg-era brewery, with a recreated 19th-century street, a tavern, a bar and manufacturing spaces.
locations.facilities: Electricity and on-site parking

locations.name: Adega Baía da Arruda
locations.setting: Small working winery on Pico Island in the Azores, set among the UNESCO-listed currais, stone-walled plots that shelter vines grown directly on volcanic rock.

locations.name: Adega Mayor
locations.setting: A contemporary winery building in Campo Maior, Alentejo, offering vineyard tours and tastings alongside its architecture, listed in Portugal Film Commission's location database.

locations.name: Alfama
locations.setting: Lisbon's oldest quarter, a hillside maze of steep cobbled lanes, tiled facades and tram lines above the Tagus.

locations.name: Algarve International Circuit
locations.setting: FIA-grade motor racing circuit near Portimao with elevation changes of up to forty metres, a start-finish straight, paddock buildings and grandstands.

locations.name: Algarve Studios
locations.setting: Multimedia content studio in central Faro offering studio space, equipment rental and production crew for video and photo shoots in the Algarve.
locations.facilities: Espaco 1 of 25 m2 usable with a 55 inch screen and HDMI, meeting table and lounge area; Espaco 2 of 115 m2 usable on level -1 with a 3.37 m ceiling, air conditioning and blackout, suitable for larger set builds; a separate 25 m2 meeting room. Male and female toilets, kitchen facilities (microwave, coffee machine, fridge) and floor plans published per space.
locations.suitability: Site lists equipment rental, production crew (camera operators, cinematographers, drone operators, producers), lighting and casting services.
locations.logistics: Praceta Aleixo da Cunha no 8, Faro, Algarve

locations.name: Armazéns do Chiado
locations.setting: A rebuilt 19th century department store in Lisbon's Chiado district, now a shopping centre behind its restored historic facade after the 1988 Chiado fire.

locations.name: Barbadinhos Steam Pumping Station
locations.setting: Steam-powered water pumping station in Xabregas that operated from 1880 to 1928, preserving four steam engines inside its industrial hall as part of Lisbon's water museum.

locations.name: Braga Municipal Stadium
locations.setting: Football stadium built into a disused granite quarry on Monte Castro, with seating on two sides only and the bare quarry rock face left exposed behind each goal.

locations.name: Cabo da Roca Lighthouse
locations.setting: Working lighthouse on Cabo da Roca near Colares, mainland Europe's westernmost point, standing on wind-blown cliffs above the Atlantic.

locations.name: Cabo de Sao Vicente Lighthouse
locations.setting: Working lighthouse at the tip of Cabo de Sao Vicente near Sagres, on the cliffs of Portugal's south-western corner, listed in the national film commission's lighthouse network.

locations.name: Cabo Espichel Lighthouse
locations.setting: Working lighthouse on the cliffs of Cabo Espichel near Sesimbra, beside a walled pilgrimage sanctuary and rows of former pilgrims' lodgings on an open headland.

locations.name: Cacela Velha
locations.setting: Small fortified hilltop village on the eastern Algarve coast overlooking the Ria Formosa lagoon, with whitewashed houses, a small fort and a parish church around a single square.

locations.name: Casa da Musica
locations.setting: Angular concrete concert hall by Rem Koolhaas on Porto's Rotunda da Boavista, with a shoebox-shaped main auditorium and several smaller performance rooms.

locations.name: Casa de Mateus
locations.setting: Baroque manor house near Vila Real with formal box-hedge gardens and a cedar tunnel, pictured on the label of Mateus Rose wine and used as a venue for concerts and cultural events.

locations.name: Casa dos Patudos
locations.setting: Early twentieth-century manor house in Alpiarca designed by architect Raul Lino for collector Jose Relvas, with period interiors and furnishings now open as a museum.

locations.name: Casa Junqueiro Regional Museum
locations.setting: Regional museum opened in 1998 in the historic centre of Freixo de Espada a Cinta, on the ground floor of the mansion that belonged to the father of poet Guerra Junqueiro, showing the town's stately-home character.

locations.name: Castelo de Beja
locations.setting: A medieval castle with a tall keep in the town of Beja, southern Alentejo, catalogued among Portugal Film Commission's castle locations.

locations.name: Central Tejo, MAAT
locations.setting: Former early 20th century thermoelectric power station on the Lisbon riverfront in Belem, now part of the MAAT museum complex, with its former turbine halls hired out for corporate events.
locations.suitability: Corporate events, bookings via the museum's venue hire contact

locations.name: Centro de Artes do Espetáculo de Portalegre
locations.setting: Municipal performing arts centre in Portalegre's historic centre, built on the site of a former religious retreat house, with a large auditorium, a smaller auditorium and a multipurpose cafe-concert hall.

locations.name: Centro Português de Fotografia
locations.setting: Porto's former prison and law court building on Largo Amor de Perdição, now the national photography museum and archive, with its original cell wings preserved.

locations.name: Cinema São Jorge
locations.setting: Art Deco cinema opened in 1950 on Lisbon's Avenida da Liberdade, run by the city's culture agency EGEAC and host to the city's main film festivals, with its screening rooms available for space rental.
locations.suitability: Cedencia de espacos (space rental) for private events

locations.name: Convent of Jesus, Setubal
locations.setting: Late 15th century Manueline convent church in Setubal, one of the earliest examples of the style, with twisted stone columns and a vaulted interior, its former convent buildings now housing a municipal museum.

locations.name: Convento de Cristo
locations.setting: Templar castle and convent complex crowned by the round Charola oratory, with Manueline cloisters and hilltop ramparts above Tomar.
locations.known_for: The Man Who Killed Don Quixote (2018)

locations.name: Corroios Tide Mill
locations.setting: Restored 17th century tide mill on the Coina estuary in Seixal, part of the Seixal municipal ecomuseum, using the rise and fall of the tide to power its milling machinery.

locations.name: Culturgest
locations.setting: Arts centre run by a bank foundation inside its Lisbon headquarters, with galleries and auditoriums used for theatre, music, cinema and conferences, and its own space-rental service.
locations.suitability: Aluguer de espacos (space rental) for private hire

locations.name: Estacao do Rossio
locations.setting: Neo-Manueline railway station on Lisbon's Rossio square, with two horseshoe-arched doorways on its facade and platforms reached through a tunnel under the Bairro Alto hill.

locations.name: Estádio do Dragão
locations.setting: FC Porto's stadium in Campanhã, opened in 2003 with about 50,000 seats, offering pitch, stands, museum and hospitality areas.

locations.name: Estoi Palace
locations.setting: Rococo and neoclassical revival palace from the 19th century near Faro, mixing Baroque and Romantic decoration, with formal gardens and a wing now run as a hotel.

locations.name: Estudio da Fabrica
locations.setting: Multifunctional video and photo studio in the Lisbon area with two sound stages for commercials, music videos, interviews and online video production.
locations.facilities: Two studios of 200 m2 each, both 10.00 m wide x 14.00 m deep (20.00 m in total) x 7.60 m high, with 5.00 m to the lighting grid (Prolyte X30D truss). Studio A has a permanent three-wall white U-shaped cyclorama of 10.00 x 8.50 x 4.20 m, repaintable in any colour, base pre-lighting on dimmers and a sliding vehicle gate of 3.40 m wide x 3.20 m high for cars and vans. Studio B has a permanent three-wall chroma green or blue U-shaped cyclorama of 10.00 x 7.50 x 4.20 m with base pre-lighting on dimmers. Both can be draped in black flannel as a black box. Also two hair and make-up rooms, a green room and an equipped kitchen.
locations.suitability: Site states the studios are rented by producers, independent filmmakers, photographers, advertising and digital agencies and music video production companies; equipment rental covers HD/4K/6K cameras, lighting, a Blackmagic ATEM multi-camera system, audio gear and a teleprompter.

locations.name: Estudios Valentim de Carvalho
locations.setting: Television studio complex in Paco de Arcos with six sound stages used for national broadcasts, music recording and the Portuguese Eurovision selection show.
locations.facilities: Six studios. Studio 1: 176 m2 (16 x 11 m, 6.5 m ceiling) with 2 dressing rooms with shower, a make-up room and a meeting room. Studio 2: 450 m2 with 350 kW of installed lighting capacity, 8 dressing rooms (one with a private bathroom), two make-up rooms, a production room and reception areas. Studio 2B: 230 m2. Studio 3: a 1,500 m2 stage plus a 600 m2 warehouse, 13 m ceiling, lighting grid at 10 m, up to 12 cameras, a 98 channel digital sound control room, its own 1,100 kVA generator, dressing rooms, production and technical support rooms, a refectory and an 1,100 m2 support zone. Studios 4, 5 and 6: 144 m2, 216 m2 and 216 m2.
locations.suitability: Site states Studio 1 has soundproofed acoustic conditions used for music recording; the complex is used for national TV broadcasts and the RTP Festival da Cancao.
locations.logistics: Studio 3 has a private car park with 250 spaces.

locations.name: Evora Historic Centre
locations.setting: UNESCO-listed Alentejo city within Roman and medieval walls, with a Roman temple, whitewashed streets, a granite cathedral and the bone-lined Capela dos Ossos.

locations.name: Fábrica Braço de Prata
locations.setting: A former military ammunition factory in Marvila, Lisbon, converted into a cultural complex with a theatre, bar and exhibition halls across its old industrial buildings.

photo.author: Vitor Oliveira from Torres Vedras, PORTUGAL

locations.name: Farol dos Capelinhos
locations.setting: Coastal lighthouse on Faial partly buried by ash from the 1957-58 Capelinhos submarine volcanic eruption, standing on the new lava and ash landscape it created.

locations.name: Forte das Berlengas
locations.setting: 17th century fort on the Berlengas archipelago off Peniche, built to defend the islands and now shared with a nature reserve, reached only by boat.

locations.name: Herdade do Freixo
locations.setting: A rolling Alentejo wine estate near Redondo whose modern winery building won ArchDaily's Building of the Year in 2018, set among vineyards with wide viewpoints.

locations.name: Loulé Rock Salt Mine
locations.setting: Underground rock salt mine in the Algarve hinterland near Loulé, with excavated caverns and tunnels used for cave and underground filming; coordinates mark the town centre, not the mine entrance.

locations.name: Lousal Mining Museum
locations.setting: Former pyrite-mining village in Grandola built around a twentieth-century mining company's power plant, now a museum with mining machinery, tools and worker housing.

locations.name: Madeira Botanical Garden
locations.setting: Terraced hillside garden above Funchal with exotic and native plant collections on volcanic slopes, reached by road or by a cable car from Monte.

locations.name: Marvao
locations.setting: Walled hilltop village on the Spanish border in the Serra de Sao Mamede, with a castle, whitewashed houses and long views over the surrounding plain.

locations.name: Mercado do Bolhao
locations.setting: Porto's historic municipal market, reopened in 2022 after renovation, with two levels of fish, meat, flower and grocery stalls under a restored iron and glass roof.

locations.name: Mercado Municipal de Loulé
locations.setting: Historic municipal market hall in the centre of Loulé, described by the town council as the building that most defines the town, with stalls for local produce, fish and crafts.

locations.name: Monastery of Coz
locations.setting: Cistercian nunnery near Alcobaca founded in the 13th century, one of the wealthiest female monasteries of the order in Portugal by the 16th century, protected as a National Monument since 2021.

locations.name: Monastery of Grijo
locations.setting: Former Augustinian canonry near Vila Nova de Gaia, mother house of the community that later moved to build the Monastery of Serra do Pilar, left partly in ruins after that move.

locations.name: Monastery of Serra do Pilar
locations.setting: Augustinian monastery complex above Vila Nova de Gaia begun in 1538, notable for its circular church and cloister, occupied by Wellington's troops in 1809 during the Peninsular War for its command of the Douro.

locations.name: Monchique Range
locations.setting: Forested mountain range in the western Algarve rising to Fóia, with natural pools, waterfalls and hillside villages, cooler and greener than the coast below.

locations.name: Mosteiro de São Martinho de Tibães
locations.setting: A Benedictine monastery complex near Braga with a baroque church, cloisters and gardens spanning eight centuries of building history, catalogued as a Portugal Film Commission location.

locations.name: Mourisca Tide Mill
locations.setting: Restored tide mill on the Sado estuary near Setúbal, using the rise and fall of the tide to turn its grinding wheels, now managed as a heritage and educational site.

locations.name: MovieBox Studios Algarve
locations.setting: Former brewery site in Loule converted into a production complex with warehouses, stages and workshops, plus hardstanding for builds and unit base, used for film and TV productions in the Algarve.
locations.facilities: Units A1-A3, 2000 sqm each at 18m height; stage B1, 3716 sqm at 8.4m with equal-size ancillary unit B2; unit C, 1250 sqm at 10.4m; unit D, 1465 sqm at 10.4m; stage E1, 906 sqm at 8.4m with construction workshop unit E; production suite F, 450 sqm; units G (573 sqm), H propstore (83 sqm), I (342 sqm), J (236 sqm); unit K, 3500 sqm at 18m; unit L, 1655 sqm at 7m; propstores M, 578 sqm at 6m
locations.suitability: Site describes exclusive-use warehouse and stage space plus about 20,000 sq ft of workshop and ancillary space for prop storage and construction, with a concrete hardstanding area for builds, parking and VFX work; further sound stages and specialist VFX and water stages are planned.
locations.logistics: Loteamento Industrial de Loule 3, 8100-285 Loule; multiple loading doors, on-site parking

locations.name: Museu Nacional Ferroviario
locations.setting: National railway museum on the site of Entroncamento's railway works, with steam locomotives, carriages and workshop sheds spanning more than a century of Portuguese rail history.

locations.name: Museum Condes de Castro Guimaraes
locations.setting: Early 20th century neo-Manueline mansion on the Cascais waterfront, built as a private residence and now a municipal museum with towers, a library and gardens overlooking the bay.

locations.name: Paço de Calheiros
locations.setting: Manor house and wine estate above the Lima valley near Ponte de Lima, run by the same family for seven centuries, with historic gardens, vineyards, a pool and dining rooms, hosting weddings, corporate events and filming.
locations.suitability: Welcomes photo sessions and filming on the estate grounds

locations.name: Palácio da Bolsa
locations.setting: Former 19th century stock exchange building in Porto, now the headquarters of the Porto Commercial Association, with a conference centre, restaurant and ornate historic rooms open for guided tours and events.

locations.name: Pero Negro Railway Station
locations.setting: Small rural railway station on the Oeste line near Sobral de Monte Agraço, with a period station building, platform and level crossing still used by regional trains.

locations.name: Pestana Palace Lisbon
locations.setting: 19th century palace in Alcantara converted into a luxury hotel, keeping its period reception rooms and gardens alongside newer hotel wings, listed in the national film commission's palace catalogue.

locations.name: Piscina das Marés
locations.setting: Álvaro Siza's tidal swimming pools built into the rocks at Leça da Palmeira, Matosinhos, using seawater pools framed in board marked concrete.

locations.name: Portalegre Tapestry Museum (Guy Fino)
locations.setting: Tapestry museum inside a former noble town house in Portalegre, remodelled to display the local tapestry workshop's collection and archive alongside the original architecture.

locations.name: Portimao Museum
locations.setting: Municipal museum in Portimao housed in a former fish canning factory on the riverfront, keeping the industrial shell and machinery pits of the cannery alongside its exhibition galleries.

locations.name: Porto de Leixões
locations.setting: The deep water port of Leixões between Matosinhos and Leça da Palmeira, with container terminals, a cruise terminal and breakwaters managed by port authority APDL.

locations.name: Praia do Guincho
locations.setting: Wide Atlantic surf beach backed by dunes and the Sintra hills, known for strong wind and heavy waves.

locations.name: Quinta da Fidalga
locations.setting: Municipal park and former country estate in Seixal, on the south bank of the Tagus, with wooded grounds listed by the national film commission for garden and forest settings.

photo.author: Vitor Oliveira from Torres Vedras, PORTUGAL

locations.name: Quinta de Sant'Ana do Gradil
locations.setting: Working farm and vineyard estate near the village of Gradil, 35km north of Lisbon, with 12 hectares of vines, olive and cypress groves, orchards, meadows and several holiday cottages.
locations.facilities: Five holiday houses, gardens, swimming pool

locations.name: Quinta do Pisao
locations.setting: Former farm estate on the edge of the Sintra-Cascais Natural Park, with old agricultural buildings, pine woods, pasture and a small lake open to visitors.

locations.name: Rabelo Boat Yard
locations.setting: Working shipyard on the Douro riverfront in Porto that still builds and repairs traditional rabelo boats once used to carry Port wine barrels downriver.

locations.name: Ria Formosa
locations.setting: Lagoon system of barrier islands, salt marshes and channels along the eastern Algarve coast near Tavira and Faro, home to fishing communities, salt pans and wading birds.

locations.name: Santa Cruz Municipal Aerodrome
locations.setting: Small municipal airfield close to the Santa Cruz beaches near Torres Vedras, home to the local aeroclub and one of the earliest civil aviation sites near Lisbon.

locations.name: Santa Marta Lighthouse
locations.setting: Working lighthouse on the Cascais waterfront built inside the grounds of the former Santa Marta Fort, a white tiled quadrangular tower with blue stripes and a red lantern overlooking the Tagus estuary, with a lighthouse museum on site.

locations.name: Sao Domingos Mine
locations.setting: Abandoned open-pit copper and pyrite mining complex near Mertola, worked from the 1850s to 1966, left with ochre-coloured pit lakes, spoil heaps and derelict processing buildings.

locations.name: Setubal Fishing Dock
locations.setting: Working fishing dock on the Sado estuary at Setubal, with moored trawlers, quayside fish auction sheds and views across the estuary to the Troia peninsula.

locations.name: Silk and Territory Museum
locations.setting: Museum in Freixo de Espada a Cinta holding the town's ethnographic, archaeological and geological collections alongside a display on hand silk weaving, still practised locally with centuries-old wooden looms.

locations.name: Teixeira Lopes House Museum
locations.setting: House and sculpture workshop built in 1895 in Vila Nova de Gaia for sculptor Jose Teixeira Lopes, now a city council run house museum holding his art collection.

locations.name: Time Out Market Lisboa
locations.setting: The restored 1892 Mercado da Ribeira market hall by Cais do Sodré in Lisbon, now a large food hall with dozens of kitchens and counters under Time Out's management.
locations.facilities: Includes a dedicated events room (Estudio Time Out) of 400 square metres on the first floor of the market; full exclusive venue hire covers over 3,000 square metres in total (own site).

locations.name: University of Coimbra (Paco das Escolas)
locations.setting: UNESCO-listed royal-palace-turned-university courtyard in Coimbra, with the Joanina Baroque library, a bell tower and ceremonial halls still in academic use.

locations.name: VLC Studios
locations.setting: Purpose-built production studio complex in Vale de Cambra, near Porto, listed in the national film commission's building catalogue under modern architecture.

locations.name: Wine Cellars Jose Maria da Fonseca
locations.setting: Historic wine cellars of one of Portugal's oldest table wine producers, founded in 1834 in Azeitao, with ageing cellars, a museum house and production buildings open to visitors.

locations.name: Anghel Saligny Bridge, Cernavoda
locations.setting: Steel lattice railway bridge of 1895 over the Danube, with stone portals and guardian statues, standing next to the newer crossing on the Bucharest to Constanta line.

locations.name: ASTRA Open Air Museum, Sibiu
locations.setting: Open air museum with over 400 relocated rural buildings, watermills, workshops and farmsteads set among 96 hectares of forest, meadows and a lake.

locations.name: Babes-Bolyai University, Cluj-Napoca
locations.setting: Main university building of 1902 in central Cluj with an aula magna, wide corridors, lecture halls and a courtyard, plus faculties spread across the city.

locations.name: Bucharest Film Studios (Buftea)
locations.setting: Studio complex north west of Bucharest with 19 sound stages, four indoor water tanks, a large backlot for standing sets, costume and prop stores and construction workshops.
locations.facilities: 19 sound stages, four indoor water tanks for underwater work, construction and props departments, over 30,000 costumes, armoury, picture vehicles, make up and dressing rooms
locations.logistics: About 25 minutes from Henri Coanda airport and 35 minutes from central Bucharest (studio site).

locations.name: Bucharest National Opera
locations.setting: Opera house of 1953 near the Dambovita with a horseshoe auditorium of about 950 seats, orchestra pit, rehearsal rooms and marble foyers.

locations.name: Bucharest North Railway Station (Gara de Nord)
locations.setting: Main passenger station of Romania: iron trainshed over long platforms, ticket halls, underpasses and a 1960s concourse, in daily use for national and international trains.

locations.name: Cantacuzino Castle, Busteni
locations.setting: Neo Romanian mansion of 1911 on a mountain slope, with arcaded terraces, a heraldic hall, cellars, caves and a park facing the Bucegi ridge.

locations.name: Carol I Central University Library, Bucharest
locations.setting: Library facing the former royal palace, with a domed rotunda reading room, galleried stacks, study halls and a modern extension added in 2001.

locations.name: Caru' cu Bere
locations.setting: Beer hall of 1899 in the old town with carved wood, stained glass, painted vaults, mosaic floors and a gallery, still working as a restaurant.

locations.name: Casa Capsa
locations.setting: Cafe, confectionery, restaurant and small hotel founded in 1852 on Calea Victoriei, with mirrored salons, a pastry counter and period furniture.

locations.name: Castel Film Studios
locations.setting: Studio at Izvorani with ten sound stages, an underwater tank stage, a 25 hectare backlot carrying western, urban and gothic standing sets, plus forest and lake frontage.
locations.facilities: Ten sound stages from about 216 to 3,344 sq m, underwater tank stage with viewing windows, one floatable stage, 25 ha backlot, 44 dressing rooms, standing sets
locations.logistics: Str. Complex Olimpic 48, Izvorani, Ciolpani, Ilfov, about 35 km north of central Bucharest (studio contact page).

locations.name: CEC Palace
locations.setting: Savings bank headquarters of 1900 on Calea Victoriei, with a glass dome over the banking hall, marble counters, stucco ceilings and a columned entrance.

locations.name: Cluj-Napoca Avram Iancu International Airport
locations.setting: Regional airport east of Cluj with departure and arrival terminals, check in desks, glazed piers, apron and runway views, the busiest airport outside Bucharest.

locations.name: Cluj-Napoca City Hall
locations.setting: City hall of 1898 near the centre of Cluj, with a clock tower, council chamber, ceremonial rooms, marble stair and long office corridors.

locations.name: Coltea Hospital, Bucharest
locations.setting: Historic city hospital rebuilt in 1888 behind a neo Romanian facade, with wards, operating theatres, an inner court and a church in the grounds.

locations.name: Constanta Casino
locations.setting: Art nouveau casino on the Black Sea promenade, restored and reopened in 2024, with a ballroom, stained glass, curved terraces and sea views.

locations.name: Constanta Shipyard
locations.setting: Shipyard inside the port with dry docks, gantry cranes, fabrication halls and outfitting quays, used for hull building and ship repair.
locations.known_for: The Brothers Bloom, What Happened to Monday

locations.name: Corvin Castle, Hunedoara
locations.setting: Gothic castle of the fifteenth century with a bridge over a ravine, knights hall, chapel, towers and a deep well court, next to a former steel town.
locations.known_for: The Nun, BloodRayne, Ghost Rider: Spirit of Vengeance

locations.name: CREIC Film Studio, Cluj-Napoca
locations.setting: Soundproofed stage of about 630 sq m inside the Cluj regional centre for creative industries, with screening room, production offices and technical rooms in the same building.
locations.facilities: Stage of about 630 sq m with internal access, screening room of about 143 sq m, production offices, technical rooms and a meeting room

locations.name: Damen Shipyards Galati
locations.setting: River shipyard on the Danube with covered building halls, slipways, heavy cranes and outfitting quays, one of the largest yards in the country.

locations.name: Filipescu-Cesianu House
locations.setting: Restored boyar house on Calea Victoriei with period rooms, parquet floors, a garden and a permanent display on Bucharest social history.

locations.name: Grand Hotel Continental, Bucharest
locations.setting: Hotel of 1886 on Calea Victoriei with a restored belle epoque facade, salons, a stair hall and rooms looking onto the boulevard.

locations.name: Grigore Antipa National Museum of Natural History
locations.setting: Natural history museum of 1908 on the Kiseleff boulevard, with dark exhibition rooms, dioramas, a whale skeleton and a modern reworked display route.

locations.name: Hala Laminor, Bucharest
locations.setting: Rolling mill hall of the former Malaxa works in east Bucharest, a steel framed industrial space of about 68,000 sq m kept for cultural and event use.

locations.name: Halele Carol and Nod Makerspace, Bucharest
locations.setting: Former Hesper factory halls beside the Dambovita, now workshops and studios with brick walls, steel trusses, gantry beams and tall windows, rented out for shoots and events.

locations.name: House of the Free Press
locations.setting: Stalinist tower of 1956 built as the state printing house, with a symmetrical wing plan, marble lobbies, offices and former printing halls, set in a wide square.

locations.name: Hungarian Theatre of Cluj
locations.setting: Theatre building of 1910 shared with the Hungarian opera, with a horseshoe auditorium, painted ceiling, boxes and a smaller studio stage.

locations.name: I.L. Caragiale National Theatre, Bucharest
locations.setting: State theatre in the city centre, rebuilt in the 1970s and reclad in 2014, with six stages, workshops, wide foyers and a roof terrace.

locations.name: Large Square (Piata Mare), Sibiu
locations.setting: Wide baroque square in the upper town, framed by the Brukenthal palace, the council tower, arcaded houses and cobbles, with lanes and stairs leading off it.

locations.name: Liberty Galati steelworks
locations.setting: Integrated steel plant on the Danube with blast furnaces, coke batteries, rolling mills, rail sidings and its own river port, the largest industrial site in eastern Romania.

locations.name: Manuc's Inn
locations.setting: Early nineteenth century inn around a wooden galleried courtyard in the old town, with cellars, a restaurant, event rooms and guest rooms above.

locations.name: Metropolitan Circus, Bucharest
locations.setting: Circus building of 1961 with a ribbed dome over a ring and about 2,000 seats, plus training rooms, backstage areas and a park setting.

locations.name: Militari Tram Depot, Bucharest
locations.setting: Working tram depot on the western edge of Bucharest with inspection pits, yard tracks, overhead wires and rolling stock from several decades side by side.

locations.name: Monteoru House, Writers' Union
locations.setting: Late nineteenth century mansion on Calea Victoriei with painted ceilings, salons, a grand stair and a courtyard, used by the Writers' Union.

locations.name: Museum of the Romanian Peasant
locations.setting: Neo Romanian brick building of 1912 holding rural collections, with timber galleries, a reassembled wooden church and workshop rooms inside the museum.

locations.name: National Bank of Romania Palace
locations.setting: Central bank headquarters of 1890 in the old town, with a marble banking hall, council room, vaults and a later wing facing Lipscani street.

locations.name: National Museum of Romanian History
locations.setting: Former central post office of 1900 on Calea Victoriei, with a colonnaded front, marble halls and vaulted galleries, now the national history museum.

locations.name: National Oil Museum, Ploiesti
locations.setting: Museum of the Romanian oil industry with derricks, pumps, drilling rigs and refinery equipment in the yard, in a city ringed by working refineries.

locations.name: National Theatre and Opera, Timisoara
locations.setting: Palace of Culture on Victory Square holding the national theatre and the opera, with an auditorium of 1928 behind a neo Byzantine facade.

locations.name: Neptun Baths, Baile Herculane
locations.setting: Derelict nineteenth century thermal bath house on the Cerna river, with decayed halls, iron and glass roofing and an ongoing rescue project run by a volunteer association.

locations.name: Oil Terminal Constanta
locations.setting: Oil storage and handling terminal in the port with tank farms, pipe racks, pump houses and loading jetties spread over several platforms.

locations.name: Oravita to Anina mountain railway
locations.setting: Mountain railway of 1863 through fourteen tunnels and ten viaducts in the Banat hills, with small stone stations and a terminus in the former mining town of Anina.

locations.name: Palace of Justice, Bucharest
locations.setting: Courthouse of the 1890s on the Dambovita with a stone facade, a grand stair hall, panelled courtrooms and long corridors, seat of the Bucharest Court of Appeal.

locations.name: Palace of the Parliament
locations.setting: Government palace of the 1980s with marble halls, ceremonial staircases, ballrooms, long corridors and deep basements, facing a wide boulevard.

locations.name: Pitesti Prison Memorial
locations.setting: Surviving wing of the prison used for the re education experiment of the early 1950s, with bare cells, barred windows and a documentary display.

locations.name: Politehnica University of Bucharest
locations.setting: Large campus in west Bucharest with concrete faculty blocks of the 1960s, lecture theatres, laboratories, long corridors and open plazas between buildings.

locations.name: Port of Constanta
locations.setting: Largest Black Sea port, with container and grain terminals, silos, quays, breakwaters and a small older basin next to the historic peninsula.

locations.name: Praid Salt Mine
locations.setting: Salt mine in Szekely Land reached by bus through a gallery to a chamber about 120 m down, with rough salt walls, mine plant and a large open underground space.

locations.name: Primaverii Palace, Ceausescu Mansion
locations.setting: Villa of the Ceausescu family in the diplomatic quarter, with mosaics, panelled rooms, an indoor pool, a winter garden and 1970s furniture left in place.

locations.name: Ramnicu Sarat Prison
locations.setting: Disused prison of silence with a central hall, single cells on two levels, iron walkways and bare plaster, held as a memorial site by the IICCMER institute.

locations.name: Resita Steam Locomotive Museum and works quarter
locations.setting: Open air line of locomotives built in Resita, set in the old ironworks quarter with furnace buildings, works housing and rail infrastructure around it.

locations.name: Retezat National Park
locations.setting: Mountain park with glacial lakes, granite ridges above 2,000 m, beech and spruce forest, alpine pasture and marked routes from the valleys below.

locations.name: Romanian Athenaeum
locations.setting: Concert hall of 1888 with a circular domed auditorium, a painted frieze, marble foyer and columned portico, home of the George Enescu Philharmonic.

locations.name: Romexpo, Bucharest
locations.setting: Exhibition centre with a domed central pavilion of the 1960s, flanking halls, open aprons and large parking areas, used for fairs and big events.

locations.name: Rosia Montana mining landscape
locations.setting: Mining village with Roman galleries, nineteenth century stamp mills, tailings ponds and empty company houses, added to the UNESCO list in 2021.

locations.name: Sighet Memorial, former prison
locations.setting: Former political prison turned museum, with two levels of cells, iron doors, tiled corridors and an inner courtyard kept close to their 1950s condition.

locations.name: Sighisoara Citadel
locations.setting: Inhabited medieval citadel on a hill, with cobbled lanes, guild towers, a clock tower, covered stair and burgher houses, on the UNESCO list.

locations.name: Slanic Prahova Salt Mine (Unirea Mine)
locations.setting: Disused salt mine with fourteen trapezoidal chambers, machine cut walls, ceilings about 55 m high and a constant temperature, reached by lift from the surface plant.

locations.name: Sulina Old Lighthouse and Danube mouth
locations.setting: Nineteenth century lighthouse and European Danube Commission buildings at the river mouth, with the shipping canal, quays, an abandoned dock and a wide sand spit nearby.

locations.name: Therme Bucuresti
locations.setting: Thermal spa under large glass domes north of Bucharest, with palm planting, pools, slides, saunas and lounge areas, open all year.

locations.name: Timisoara Traian Vuia International Airport
locations.setting: Airport in western Romania combining 1960s terminal architecture with newer halls, a cargo apron and open runway approaches over flat farmland.

locations.name: Transfagarasan mountain road (DN7C)
locations.setting: High mountain road with hairpin bends, viaducts, a summit tunnel and a glacial lake at about 2,000 m, managed by the national roads company and closed by snow in winter.

locations.name: Turda Salt Mine
locations.setting: Former salt mine open to visitors, with bell shaped chambers, preserved timber winding gear, a mine shaft lift and an underground lake about 100 m below ground.

locations.name: Union Square, Oradea
locations.setting: Riverside square lined with restored art nouveau and eclectic buildings, including the Black Eagle Palace and its glazed arcade.

locations.name: Unirea Shopping Center
locations.setting: Department store of 1976 at Unirii square, with escalator wells, wide sales floors, service corridors and a roof level over the boulevard.

locations.name: University of Bucharest, main building
locations.setting: Nineteenth century university palace on University Square, with a columned front, an aula, lecture rooms, stone staircases and an inner courtyard.

locations.name: Vacaresti Nature Park, Bucharest
locations.setting: Wetland inside Bucharest in the basin of an unfinished 1980s reservoir, with reed beds, ponds, willow scrub and the city skyline above the dikes.

locations.name: Vaser Valley Forestry Railway (Mocanita)
locations.setting: Narrow gauge steam railway climbing a forested valley from Viseu de Sus, with wooden carriages, water stops, timber halts and a working locomotive shed and yard.

locations.name: Vasile Alecsandri National Theatre, Iasi
locations.setting: Theatre of 1896 by Fellner and Helmer in central Iasi, with a gilded auditorium, painted curtain, chandelier, boxes and a marble stair.

locations.name: Vila Golescu, Campulung
locations.setting: Family villa and park above Campulung restored by the Pro Patrimonio foundation, with wooden verandas, plain period interiors and an orchard.

locations.name: Avala Studios
locations.setting: The oldest studio complex in the country, set in Kosutnjak park, with four soundproof stages, two indoor water tanks in the largest stage and a backlot of about 9,850 square metres.
locations.facilities: Stage 1 of 48 x 30 m and 16 m high with two indoor water tanks, stages of 40 x 14 m, 32 x 13 m and 24 x 15 m, backlot of 9,850 sq m, offices, vehicle storage, apartments for cast
locations.logistics: Kneza Viseslava 88, about 6 km from central Belgrade

locations.name: Avala Tower
locations.setting: Telecommunications tower of 204 metres on Avala mountain south of Belgrade, with a viewing level, restaurant and parking at the base.

locations.name: Banovina Palace
locations.setting: Modernist government building of 1940 in Novi Sad, 185 metres long with 569 rooms and a 42 metre tower, seat of the provincial government and assembly.

locations.name: Belgrade Arena
locations.setting: Multipurpose indoor arena in New Belgrade used for sport, concerts, exhibitions and fairs, seating up to 25,000 depending on the event.

locations.name: Belgrade City Library
locations.setting: Public library on Knez Mihailova Street in the former Srpska Kruna hotel of about 1867, with reading rooms, exhibition space and period interiors.

locations.name: Belgrade Fair
locations.setting: Trade fair complex of 24 hectares on the Sava bank with 14 halls and about 100,000 square metres of exhibition space, including large domed halls.

locations.name: Belgrade Fortress and Kalemegdan
locations.setting: Citadel above the meeting of the Sava and the Danube with ramparts, gates, tunnels and a large public park, managed by a city company.

locations.name: Belgrade Philharmonic Hall
locations.setting: Concert hall of the Belgrade Philharmonic in the city centre, seating 201, equipped for filming and for audio and video recording.
locations.suitability: The commission page states the hall provides conditions for film shoots and for audio and video recording

locations.name: Blue Train
locations.setting: Presidential train of 1959 kept in Belgrade, with art deco salon, conference car, dining car, kitchen and sleeping car in original materials.

locations.name: Branko's Bridge
locations.setting: Road bridge of 1956 over the Sava linking old Belgrade and New Belgrade, resting on the masonry pylons of the pre-war bridge.

locations.name: Cipranin Military Barracks
locations.setting: Disused military barracks at Sombor: several buildings in an enclosed compound surrounded by mature trees.

locations.name: CityStudio Belgrade
locations.setting: Production base in the Obilicev Venac pedestrian zone used for castings, creative meetings, pre-production, rehearsals and recordings, a short walk from Knez Mihailova Street.

locations.name: Cruiser Cafe

locations.name: Ecka Castle

locations.name: Faculty of Dramatic Arts
locations.setting: Brutalist teaching building of 1974 in New Belgrade with concrete and timber interiors, lecture rooms, studios and screening spaces.

locations.name: Faculty of Philosophy Novi Sad
locations.setting: Modernist university building on the Danube campus in Novi Sad, in concrete, brick, aluminium and copper, with classrooms, an amphitheatre, library and laboratories.

locations.name: Felix Romuliana
locations.setting: Late Roman imperial palace and fortified compound at Gamzigrad near Zajecar, on an open plateau, listed by UNESCO.

locations.name: Firefly Studios

locations.logistics: Milesevska 11, Pancevo, roughly half an hour by road from central Belgrade

locations.name: General Hospital of South Banat
locations.setting: Hospital built in 1838 in classical style, standing inside the largest town park in Pancevo, with period facades and grounds.

locations.name: GTC House

locations.name: House of Jevrem Grujic

locations.name: House of Prince Milos

locations.name: Kabinet Brewery

locations.name: Karlovci Grammar School

locations.setting: Main pedestrian street of Belgrade lined with late nineteenth century facades, running from Terazije square to the Kalemegdan fortress.

locations.name: Kostolac Power Plant

locations.setting: Former industrial hall in Belgrade used as a theatre, club and event space, with raw brick and steel structure and flexible floor area.

locations.name: Kulpin Castle

locations.name: Lepenski Vir Hotel

locations.name: Mechanical Industry Nis

locations.setting: Working Danube river port in Belgrade with concrete and glass halls, quays and open storage areas in a modernist industrial setting.

locations.name: Princess Ljubica's Residence

locations.name: Radisson Collection Hotel, Old Mill Belgrade
locations.setting: Hotel built into a converted nineteenth century mill near the Sava, combining brick industrial structure with contemporary rooms, restaurant and bar.

locations.name: Smederevo Fortress
locations.setting: Triangular medieval fortress of 1428 to 1430 on the Danube at Smederevo, with heavy ramparts, towers and large open interior ground.

locations.name: Sombor Theatre
locations.setting: Classical theatre building of about 1882 in Sombor, with a painted ceiling, staircases, lobby and an auditorium of 324 seats.

locations.setting: Former silk dyeing works in the Almaski quarter of Novi Sad, kept as industrial heritage and reused as a gallery, office, cafe and event space.

locations.name: Tesnjar

locations.name: The Babe Hotel

locations.name: Topcider Railway Station
locations.setting: Railway station of 1888 in the Topcider valley in Belgrade, built around the former royal waiting room, with platforms and sidings.

locations.name: Viscose Factory Loznica
locations.setting: Large abandoned chemical plant founded in 1957 at Loznica in western Serbia, with production halls, pipework and yards.

locations.name: Vision Team Studios

locations.name: Vukov Spomenik Underground Station
locations.setting: Underground railway station of 1995 beneath Vracar in Belgrade, with two tracks, deep platforms and long access shafts.

locations.name: Yugoslav Film Archive
locations.setting: Cinematheque in central Belgrade in a house of 1846, renovated to about 5,000 square metres with three cinemas, a library, reading room and museum rooms.

locations.name: Zeleni Venac Market

locations.facilities: Stage 70 x 30 m, 9.5 m height, 2100 sq m plus support areas, LED video walls, studio lighting, sound, Spidercam, hotel and restaurants nearby, parking for 600 cars.

locations.name: Andrej Bagar Theatre, Nitra

locations.name: Apartment in the Centre of Bratislava

locations.facilities: 200 sq m, lift access, three bedrooms, two bathrooms plus guest toilet, air conditioning, high speed wifi.

locations.name: Banska Stiavnica

locations.name: Bardejov

locations.name: Bata Shoe Factory Partizanske

locations.name: Bojnice Castle

locations.name: Bratislava Old Town Streets
locations.setting: Compact medieval centre of narrow lanes, squares and Baroque townhouses, largely pedestrian and close to the Danube.

locations.name: Bratislava-Nove Mesto Railway Station
locations.setting: Railway station in service since 1962, with a 1960s concourse, platforms, its own car park and public transport stops nearby.

locations.name: Fajnorka Engineering School

locations.setting: Mountain hotel of 1904 in the High Tatras below Slavkovsky stit, the first large hotel in the range, with period public rooms, a dining hall and timber detailing.

locations.name: Hammam Thermal Spa, Trencianske Teplice
locations.setting: Turkish bath completed in 1888 in a spa town, with a tiled bathing hall lit through three glazed cupolas and Moorish arcades and decoration.

locations.name: Hodrusa-Hamre Mining Village
locations.setting: Mining village in a narrow valley with ore processing buildings, adits and miners' houses, part of the UNESCO listed Banska Stiavnica mining landscape.

locations.name: Hotel Devin
locations.setting: Functionalist hotel of 1954 on the Danube embankment by the architect Emil Bellus, a protected landmark whose interiors have been used by production companies before.
locations.suitability: The hotel states that its interiors have been used for filming by production companies.

locations.name: House of Arts, Piestany
locations.setting: Cultural and social centre on the Ivan Krasko embankment built between 1974 and 1979 to a design by Ferdinand Milucky, with a concert hall, foyers and terraces.

locations.name: House of Culture ZSR, Zvolen
locations.setting: Railway workers' cultural and social centre in Zvolen, with an auditorium, club rooms and socialist era public interiors.

locations.name: Iron Curtain Border Installation, Kopcany
locations.setting: Reconstructed section of the Cold War border zone next to a First World War cemetery, with wooden posts, eleven strands of barbed wire, warning signs and a guard hut.

locations.name: Karlova Huta Blast Furnace
locations.setting: Charcoal fired blast furnace at Vlachovo, part of the Slovak Technical Museum, kept as an example of nineteenth century pig iron production with its stone stack and casting house.

locations.name: Koliba Studios
locations.setting: Slovakia's largest studio complex at the foot of the Small Carpathians, with sound stages, technical buildings, stores and 87,000 square metres of grounds used by broadcasters and production companies.

locations.name: Kosice International Airport
locations.setting: Slovakia's second largest airport, handling scheduled and charter flights, with a terminal, apron and runway on the southern edge of Kosice.

locations.name: Levoca
locations.setting: Walled town in the Spis region with a Renaissance square, town hall, Gothic church and streets of preserved merchant houses.

locations.name: Luky House of Culture Supply Tunnel, Petrzalka
locations.setting: Service tunnel and basement level under a 1980s culture house in the Petrzalka housing estate, partly neglected, with concrete corridors, pipe runs and plant rooms.

locations.name: Mlada Garda Student Dormitory
locations.setting: University hall of residence of 1954 by the architect Emil Bellus, a large symmetrical block with courtyards, canteen and long repeating room corridors.

locations.name: Munition Factory Dubnica nad Vahom
locations.setting: Heavy engineering works built in 1937 as part of the Skoda group, later making bridges, locomotives and construction machinery, with large halls and yards on the edge of Dubnica.

locations.name: National Council of the Slovak Republic
locations.setting: Slovak parliament building on the hill beside Bratislava Castle, with a debating chamber, committee rooms and terraces looking over the Danube.

locations.name: Nivy Market and Bus Station
